passages.title: Shatterspear Laborers
passages.text:
There are a large number of Shatterspear trolls picking through the ruins to the north and northeast. I suspect that they're looking for magical artifacts, but none of our scouts have reported the discovery of anything of significance turning up from their digs. They may well just be fueling their war.

One thing is fairly certain though: less laborers would slow down their offensive, so less laborers is what they're going to get. You in?

passages.title: Shatterspear Laborers
passages.text: Good work. Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Remnants of the Highborne
passages.text:
There are several ruins similar to these spread through Darkshore, many of them inhabited by the troubled spirits of the Highborne. Out of mild courtesy for their cursed souls, we haven't been overly proactive about stripping the ruins of artifacts, but those hesitancies vanish in light of this new troll threat.

While you're aiding the Sentinels in their goals within the ruins, please collect any artifacts that you stumble upon and bring them back to me. I would like to preserve what little I can.

passages.title: Remnants of the Highborne
passages.text: Were you able to recover any artifacts?

passages.title: Remnants of the Highborne
passages.text: Perfect! Thank you so much. I would hate to lose more records of our culture to war - far too much has been sacrificed already.

passages.title: Denying Manpower
passages.text:
To the north, the Shatterspear have a war camp where they are constructing their catapults. The camp is guarded by some of their mystics, but I've started receiving reports that there are sightings of orcs and tauren there as well.

I don't want to make any assumptions as to what that suggests, but I do want you to go in and kill them before they can make any further strikes on our Sentinels.

passages.title: Denying Manpower
passages.text: Excellent work. One more threat we can worry a bit less about. We'll continue the offensive while they are still off-guard.

passages.title: Swift Response
passages.text:
I have a scout that we lost contact with a couple days ago. I assumed her dead, but it appears that she's been captured. The trolls indicate that they have at least two captives though... the only other person that comes to mind is Alanndarian Nightsong, a civilian that was in the area against my advisement early yesterday.

The Shatterspear have established a war camp to the north - it is almost certainly where any of their prisoners are being taken. Find them and free them if you're able.

passages.title: Swift Response
passages.text:
<Alanndarian looks very pale, though shallow breaths betray the life that remains in her.>

You're here...  to save me? A bit later... than I hoped.

passages.title: War Supplies
passages.text:
The trolls are building their forces and supplies at the war camp to the north. When they feel they are ready, they will almost certainly launch their attack on Lor'danel from that location. It shouldn't take us long to rout this rabble, but I'm not one for taking unnecessary risks.

I want you to fight your way into the war camp and set fire to any stockpiles of supplies that you see. The setback should buy us quite a bit of time before they can muster a counterattack.

passages.title: War Supplies
passages.text: Excellent work. That should slow them down a bit.

passages.title: Timely Arrival
passages.text:
It's good to see you. I wasn't looking forward to enduring what Alanndarian did, so the rescue is somewhat welcome.

I saw the troll leader before I was captured, and thought I had the perfect opportunity to kill him, but he's protected by some sort of magic shield. Morra needs to know before she mounts her assault, but first, we need to get out of here.

Help me to the dock - I'll make my way to Lor'danel via water, and you can go back to Morra with the intel.

passages.title: Timely Arrival
passages.text: Some sort of shield you say? We might have a way around that. Balthule had an idea for breaking whatever protective enchantments their shaman had, so it might work on this too. Thank you for saving Aynasha and bringing me this information - it may well make the difference in our battle.

passages.title: One Bitter Wish
passages.text:
Morra sent you? I should have listened to her - it's just hard to take trolls seriously I guess.

<Alanndarian lets out a weak chuckle.>

It's way too late for that anyway. We're mortal now... this is the fate we have to face, one way or another. I've had time to accept that.

I have one request though... kill the torturer that did this to me. They call him Rit'ko... you can find him just ahead with the other prisoner.

<Alanndarian offers a small smile, then winces and slumps back over in pain.>

passages.title: One Bitter Wish
passages.text: Alanndarian is dead then. That saddens me greatly, but it is not entirely unexpected. I expect no mercy from these savages, and will show them none.

passages.title: Strategic Strikes
passages.text:
Striking at the head of the beast doesn't work if there's another head to replace it. Before we can kill their leader, we need to kill the subleaders that may try to step up. Right now, they are not as well defended, and you should be able to best them without much support.

Take this dryad spear and hunt them down. The poison on its tip should slow their incantations. My scouts reported one inside the water chamber in the ruins to the east and the other past the remains of the tower to the southwest.

passages.title: Strategic Strikes
passages.text: You've shown a great deal of talent for one so young. Good work. It seems the final battle is before us.

passages.title: On the Brink
passages.text:
I've already been working on something for breaking down their protective wards. With a focus based in their power and a bit of druidic magic, we should be able to breach their shields.

Find their shaman to the east and southeast and recover several of their amulets. I will prepare them and imbue an arrow that you can deliver to Sandrya Moonfall for the attack.

passages.title: On the Brink
passages.text: Did you recover the amulets?

passages.title: On the Brink
passages.text: These will do perfectly. I will prepare them for Sandrya - you are sure to be dispatched to meet with her shortly.

passages.title: The Last Wave of Survivors
passages.text:
It's too late for Laird, he didn't make it in time.

The last wave of night elves from Auberdine attempted to escape a couple of hours ago. They stayed in their old home, clinging to the hope that it could be salvaged, but it seems they were finally forced out. I fear many of them won't make it, like Laird did not.

Quickly, go down the coast to the west and find any survivors that you can. We're sending Sentinels and Hippogryphs down, but every moment counts - we need to know which ones might make it.

passages.title: The Last Wave of Survivors
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>. Some of them surely would not have made it without you.

We'll be taking the wounded to the main building once we have them all safely back in town. Perhaps you can meet us there later?

passages.title: The Boon of the Seas
passages.text:
It is good to see you. You were key in ensuring that our loved ones made it home, and I hold some hope that you may yet help us further.

Like Laird, their wounds will be grave - every one of them battered by the coast and assaulted by the elementals. I am doing what I can, but it seems that those elementals hosted a toxin that is weakening their ability to heal. I believe I can concoct a salve, but I will need secretion from the muscles of the clams that inhabit this coast. Can you help me?

passages.title: The Boon of the Seas
passages.text: Did you bring muscles from the clams? I worry that our time grows very short.

passages.title: The Boon of the Seas
passages.text:
This will do perfectly. Thank you so much!

I suspect they will want to thank you personally should they recover, so perhaps you can stop by later on.

passages.title: Threat from the Water
passages.text:
Some of the survivors of this last Auberdine attack are still trying to make it up the coast to safety. We only caught word that they were coming within the last hour. I wish that we had more warning...

The coastline west of us is swarming with vile spray, vicious little water elementals. We need to clear them out if any of the survivors are to have a chance of making it to Lor'danel. Depart immediately and kill every elemental you see.

passages.title: Threat from the Water
passages.text: Your efforts are very much appreciated. Since the Cataclysm, the elementals have been out of control. We have little hope of taking back Auberdine without extinguishing their presence first.

passages.title: What's Happening to the Blackwood Furbolg?
passages.text:
Our ancestors lived alongside the Blackwood furbolgs for generations. But recently, we have lost contact with their settlements deeper in the forest. One of their larger villages, Blackwood Hold, can be found to the south.

Travel there and find Elder Brolg. Ask him why his people have withdrawn from us and offer your help, if necessary.

passages.title: What's Happening to the Blackwood Furbolg?
passages.text:
Why have you come here, outsider?

<You tell the elder that you were sent by Foriel Broadleaf at the Grove of the Ancients. He seems to relax slightly.>

The elf is right. The forces of Felwood have seeped into Darkshore and sickened my people.

passages.title: The Bear's Paw
passages.text:
The foul satyr of Felwood have started to introduce their poison into Darkshore, into our lands. Their corruption kills the land and twists the creatures who live in it. My people are no exception.

Our magic alone is not enough to bring them back to their senses. There is an herb, called bear's paw, that we use to break fevers and fortify the weak. With its help, we may be able to break the influence of the satyr. The herb grows in the wilds around the village.

passages.title: The Bear's Paw
passages.text: Have you gathered the bear's paw?

passages.title: The Bear's Paw
passages.text: These are poor, weak stalks, but they are all we have. The corruption spreads quickly, even among the plants of the forest.

passages.title: No Accounting for Taste
passages.text:
<The machine buzzes for a few moments before Wizbang's voice breaks through.>

Interesting! The source of this corruption definitely came from something external--no surprises there--but it appears that in this case they've been eating something foul. A large mammal probably. Most likely a bear.

Search the beach for a bear carcass for me. Slightly east of there would make the most sense, on the inland side of the beach. Bring me the sample back at town.

passages.title: No Accounting for Taste
passages.text: Welcome back! Did you find that bear sample that I was looking for?

passages.title: No Accounting for Taste
passages.text: This definitely looks like the stuff they were eating. Let me take a closer peek...

passages.title: The Corruption's Source
passages.text:
I rushed here as soon as I heard the news from Wizbang. I know who's behind this mess now. Zenn Foulhoof.

He came over from Teldrassil after he was chased out for performing perverse magics. The kinds of corruption he employs are not welcome among my people, and it seems he's taken it a step further this time, perhaps as some form of revenge.

Zenn's been given too many chances, it's time we remove this threat to all that is natural. Kill Zenn and his minions, and then find me back in Lor'danel.

passages.title: The Corruption's Source
passages.text: It is done then. Thank you. I only hope that the wildlife here will see more peace with his passing.

passages.title: A Taste for Grouper
passages.text:
Between boat rides and building, I'm exhausted... and hungry. You know what sounds tasty? Fish. Fish sound delicious.

Darkshore is known for its grouper. If you fish me up some, I'll make it worth your time.

passages.title: A Taste for Grouper
passages.text:
<Johnathan's belly grumbles as you approach.>

Couldn't have said it better with words.

passages.title: A Taste for Grouper
passages.text:
It looks like fishing's your thing. My belly appreciates the gift.

I'm thinking you would get more use out of this pole than I would. Have at it.

passages.title: Three Hammers to Break
passages.text:
I've flown through the ruins of Auberdine on a scouting mission. There are three Twilight's Hammer cultists that are responsible for the elementals that have overrun the destroyed town.

Head west into the ruins. Seek out and slay Cloudtamer Wildmane, Windmaster Tzu-Tzu, and Skylord Braax.

Only then will Sentinel Selarin and her forces stand a chance of taking back their home.

passages.title: Three Hammers to Break
passages.text:
Without those three coaxing them, perhaps the flow of elementals into the Ruins of Auberdine will be stemmed.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Bear's Blessing
passages.text:
Before the bear's paw can be used to cleanse the afflicted, it must be completed and blessed. To the north of the village roams a tallstrider named Fleetfoot. You'll need its tailfeathers to complete the herb bundle.

Bring the tailfeathers and the bear's paw bundle to the ancient bear statue in the ruins around the Grove of the Ancient, further north of where you'll find Fleetfoot.

While at the shrine, combine the tailfeathers with the bear's paw and receive the bear spirit's blessing.

passages.title: The Bear's Blessing
passages.text: Have you visited the old bear statue?

passages.title: The Bear's Blessing
passages.text:
<Elder Brolg accepts the blessed bundle from you and looks over it.>

This is exactly what we needed. The bear's spirit favors us and there may be hope for my brothers after all.

passages.title: Call Down the Thunder
passages.text:
Aetherion is almost in our world, but he can still be dealt with!

At the end of the dock floats a ritual orb. I want you to use it to complete the ritual, beckoning the elemental lord down from his vortex.

Trust me, <name>, I and the other spirits that you have freed will greatly weaken Aetherion. However, it will be up to you to finish him off for good and save the Kaldorei people of Darkshore from utter destruction.

Deliver his essence to Corvine Moonrise at the refugee camp so he will know.

passages.title: Call Down the Thunder
passages.text: You have returned. What news do you bring?

passages.title: Call Down the Thunder
passages.text:
Yalda? The spirits of others from the Ruins of Auberdine?

<The druid ponders what you've conveyed about your adventure in the ruins.>

I remember them all. They will be dearly missed, but they have moved on into the Goddess's embrace and that is for the best.

Ande'thoras-ethil, may your troubles be diminished, <name>!

passages.title: Solace for the Highborne
passages.text: I have come to Bashal'Aran to grant peace to the troubled spirits of the Highborne, but I find my hand hesitates with each blow. If you would like to aid me, you would have my gratitude.

passages.title: Solace for the Highborne
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Solace for the Highborne
passages.text:
You have my thanks. Though they may not be able to show it, you have the thanks of the Highborne spirits as well.

Fare safely, traveler.

passages.title: The Final Flame of Bashal'Aran
passages.text:
It is in times like these that we are forced to stop and examine our way of life. We are mortal now, and no matter how much we desire otherwise, we are deserving of our new place in this world.

Bashal'Aran, down the road to the south, once a city of our ancestors, it now is home to their cursed ghosts. We held hope of salvation for them as with ourselves, but we have left them in torment for too long. It is time to extinguish the Final Flame of Bashal'Aran.

passages.title: The Final Flame of Bashal'Aran
passages.text: You have our thanks. It is time that we leave the past behind us, and start looking to our future.

passages.title: A Love Eternal
passages.text:
I would like to extend my gratitude for saving us. I would call myself fortunate, but my beloved, Anaya, lays long dead. I am alone and deeply troubled, and sadly, I require your aid yet again.

Wandering the woods of Darkshore after my rescue, I found myself in the ruins of Bashal'Aran... where I saw the haunted spirit of my beloved.

She must be freed, but I lack the heart to do it. Her spirit must be destroyed.

passages.title: A Love Eternal
passages.text:
I somehow avoided being inflicted with the same toxin that the other survivors now endure. I cannot help but be envious of them to a degree though... living an eternity alone seems not worth living at all.

I miss you so much, Anaya.

passages.title: A Love Eternal
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. Perhaps it would have been better... if I had done it myself. But even after these thousands of years, I could not bear to raise my hand against my beloved.

Please, I would be alone with my grief...

passages.title: A Lost Companion
passages.text:
Please help... I can barely sit up.

My friend, a bear named Grimclaw, he's not here. I sent him ahead to let the Sentinels know we were coming before we left Auberdine, but he never arrived. I sensed something might be amiss as we were leaving, but with the evacuation, I never had a chance to act on it.

If he's injured, there's only one place that he would go - the Withering Thicket, north of Auberdine, down the road to the south from here. Bring him back to me safely... he's my only family.

passages.title: A Lost Companion
passages.text:
Greetings, traveler. You seem to have an interest in my friend here. You're here on behalf of his friend Volcor then I imagine? If Volcor didn't come himself, he must be injured as well. I hope he recovers quickly.

Gimclaw is too injured to be moved far and he's going to need some immediate treatment. I'm afraid I can't let you take him back just yet, but perhaps you can help me while I tend to him.

passages.title: Spirit of the Stag
passages.text:
In these woods reside three great spirits, that of the Stag, that of the Thistle Bear, and that of the Moonstalker. These spirits make powerful allies, but you can only align yourself with one of them.

If you wish to align yourself with the Great Stag Spirit, take this incense to the woods just north of Bashal'Aran. Meditate before the great spirit while burning the incense on the ground between you, and face his trial to earn his blessing. Should you succeed, return to me.

passages.title: Spirit of the Stag
passages.text:
I am the caretaker for my kind, leading not through force, but through wisdom and swift action. Wisdom is what carries us into the deeper forest when danger beckons and swiftness is what leaves our enemies basking in our absence.

In this wisdom, I see through to your true intentions, and I know that you are deserving of my blessing, the blessing of my swiftness. It can be yours, but know that the other spirits will not welcome you once you proceed - consider this carefully before accepting my boon.

passages.title: Spirit of the Moonstalker
passages.text:
In these woods reside three great spirits, that of the Stag, that of the Thistle Bear, and that of the Moonstalker. These spirits make powerful allies, but you can only align yourself with one of them.

If you wish to align yourself with the Great Moonstalker Spirit, take this incense to the land just south of the Ruins of Lornesta. Meditate before the great spirit while burning the incense on the ground between you, and face his trial to earn his blessing. Should you succeed, return to me.

passages.title: Spirit of the Moonstalker
passages.text:
I share these forests willingly, accepting night elf kind into my home, and on occasion calling them friend. Though they have been tainted greatly in recent memory, I can see in you the same strength, honor, and spirit that first endeared them to me.

If you place value in the ferocity necessary to overcome all odds, then I am willing to call you my champion. Know now that if you side with my kind, the other spirits will not accept you, so consider your choice carefully.

passages.title: Peering Into the Vortex (DEPRECATED)
passages.text:
There is no time to waste, <race>! It is taking every ounce of my power to keep Darkshore's entire landmass from being shattered and swept into the ocean... you must listen to me very carefully.

On that hippogryph there is an orb. Take the hippogryph to the top of the vortex and use the orb to sample the energy surrounding it. Hurry, <name>. I don't know how much longer I can hold!

passages.title: The Land Is in Their Blood
passages.text:
If we're to stabilize the forces of nature, we'll need every little bit of help we can get. The furbolg of the Blackwood tribe have long inhabited the area and have strong ties to the land.

Their elder Shaman, Elder Brownpaw, wields great power over the elements -- his assistance would be invaluable. See if you can obtain their aid.

passages.title: The Land Is in Their Blood
passages.text: I have much respect for the great Malfurion Stormrage.  I cannot, however, leave my people in their time of need.  Maybe there is a way we can both help each other.

passages.title: The Last Wildkin
passages.text:
The wildkin were once numerous in Darkshore. Such are their ties to the land that the Cataclysm that shattered Darkshore also decimated their numbers.

The wildkin Aroom is the last of his tribe and is a powerful elder with a strong connection to Elune. His help will be most necessary in healing the land -- you will find him north of here at the Moontouched Den.

passages.title: The Last Wildkin
passages.text: A terrible sadness surrounds the creature.  Its eyes stare beyond you as you approach it.

passages.title: Aroom's Farewell
passages.text:
<The creature hoots sadly as it addresses you.>

Aroom is last of tribe...

Others won't rest... need funeral pyre. Bring Aroom the feathers of others.... let them rest.

Then Aroom help you.

passages.title: Aroom's Farewell
passages.text: You bring others' feathers?

passages.title: Aroom's Farewell
passages.text: I thank you, <race>.  Soon my kin will rest.

passages.title: Protector of Ameth'Aran
passages.text:
Nothing will repair the land quicker than the strength of those who inhabit it. We night elves are fortunate that some of our best allies just happen to be both the land and its inhabitants at once.

The Ancient of War known as Selenn was charged with guarding the ruins of Ameth'Aran, to the south. Go there and seek his help.

passages.title: Protector of Ameth'Aran
passages.text:
If the great Malfurion requires my presence, it is my duty to heed his call.  It is also my duty to protect these ruins, however.

Perhaps you'll help me fulfill both my obligations, <name>?

passages.title: The Blackwood Pledge
passages.text:
It won't be immediate, but the elementals' anger will soon die down and my people will live to fight another day.

I will go help you and Malfurion in any way that I can.

passages.title: The Blackwood Pledge
passages.text: This is fortunate news, <name>.  The furbolg may seem little more than a savage race, but their ties to the land are ancient and their shamans are second to none.

passages.title: Elune's Fire
passages.text:
We need special flame for ritual. We need Elune's fire.

Horoo's spirit wanders east of here. Horoo carries torch of Elune. Bring here so spirits rest.

Aroom thanks you.

passages.title: Elune's Fire
passages.text: You have torch?

passages.title: Elune's Fire
passages.text:
<Aroom lets out a long low-pitched hoot.>

Finally kin may rest.

passages.title: The Wildkin's Oath
passages.text:
Wildkin with Elune. Aroom in your debt now.

Aroom help you now. Return to Malfurion, I join you soon.

passages.title: The Wildkin's Oath
passages.text: The wildkin were once the guardians of the land.  It is good to hear they haven't all forgotten their old ways.

passages.title: Calming the Earth
passages.text:
I would be neglecting my responsibility if I abandoned my post just now, with so many elementals out of control in the ruins.

Let us deal with them first, before we see how we can aid Malfurion. What do you say, small one?

passages.title: Calming the Earth
passages.text: The land is deeply unsettled, <name>.  It'll be years before calm returns to these parts.

passages.title: Calming the Earth
passages.text: It's become clear, <name>.  The elements won't be calm until Malfurion succeeds in returning balance to the land.  Aiding him is, in a way, also fulfilling my task.

passages.title: Sworn to Protect
passages.text:
My duty here has been fulfilled as best it can. Send word to Malfurion that I'll be joining him soon.

Good luck to you, <name>. Good luck to all of us.

passages.title: Sworn to Protect
passages.text: Excellent job, <name>!  Selenn's help in holding back the vortex will be invaluable.

passages.title: The Emerald Dream
passages.text:
Our efforts in containing the destruction don't appear to be quite enough. I fear we're going to need aid from beyond the waking world.

Twilight cultists inside the Earthshatter Cavern to the east have opened a gateway to a nightmare-infested section of the Emerald Dream. They hold a green dragon prisoner named Thessera there.

Go through the nightmare portal and free her. She will be a powerful ally.

passages.title: The Emerald Dream
passages.text: Malfurion calls?  Yes... I can hear his voice through the dream...

passages.title: The Shatterspear Invaders
passages.text:
If we didn't have enough on our hands with the land and the elements turning against us, it seems something has riled up the trolls to the northeast, and they've started on a war path. I'm not sure what their aims are, but they've already attacked several of our scouts and have besieged the cultists at the Tower of Althalaxx.

We've sent a contingent of our best Sentinels to counter their attacks. If you would travel northeast to the ruins and join them, I'm certain that they could use the extra hand.

passages.title: The Shatterspear Invaders
passages.text:
Glynda sent you to lend a hand, did she? I'm glad she did - I could certainly use the help.

I'm working on our initial plans to start whittling away at their ranks. Please feel free to help Tysha and Balthule in the meantime.

passages.title: The Front Line
passages.text:
Their forces are weakened, their supplies destroyed, and their subleaders are dead. It is time for us to take this fight to their home, and their leader. I'm admittedly still in the dark as to what spurred their sudden aggression, but perhaps we will find some answers on their doorstep.

Take this arrow that Balthule prepared and report to Sandrya Moonfall deep in Shatterspear Vale to join the attack. It would be best to secure a ride on one of our nightsabers - going on foot would be dangerous.

passages.title: The Front Line
passages.text: Greetings, <class>. Did you bring the arrow?

passages.title: The Front Line
passages.text: It is good to meet you. Word has been sent to me of the efforts you have made to aid us against the trolls, and I must admit I am a bit impressed. The final fight is upon us now, I hope you are prepared.

passages.title: Disturbing Connections
passages.text:
The letter from Garrosh Hellscream makes clear the suspicions that were raised during the offensive on the Shatterspear. The presence of forsaken at the tower ruins and horde supplies and enforcers at the Shatterspear War Camp were only the start. Garrosh himself contacted the Shatterspear to spur their offensive towards Lor'danel, and it seems clear that he fully intends to push from the south as well.

Glynda Nal'Shea will need this information if the night elves are to be prepared.

passages.title: Disturbing Connections
passages.text: You're back! I hear the battle went well.

passages.title: Disturbing Connections
passages.text:
Well, this news is disturbing indeed. I will start dispatching messengers to Ashenvale immediately and see if we can't get some reinforcements prepared for them.

I cannot thank you enough for all the help you've lent us in these trying times. Such heroic deeds deserve reward. I think I might have something that will serve you perfectly.

passages.title: Don't Forget the Horde
passages.text:
Evenar and the other apprentices may not be much use in a battle, but you look like you can more than hold your own. The Horde scum across the road to the east at Bathran's Haunt need to be taught a lesson.

Their new warlord, Garrosh Hellscream, has them up to no good. Feel like teaching them a thing or two?

I'd come with you, but my assignment is to stay here and protect Orendil's apprentices, and that's exactly what I'm going to do.

passages.title: Don't Forget the Horde
passages.text:
<The sentinel eyes you appreciatively for a moment.>

A job well done, <class>. If you're any indication of the quality of the <race> adventurers we're going to be seeing more of, we should have this war against the orcs and their Horde taken care of faster than expected.

passages.title: Twilight Plans
passages.text:
We're not fully aware of the intentions of the Twilight's Hammer cultists to the southwest. We fear an attack on Lor'danel, however their motives might go well beyond that.

I need you to go to the Twilight Encampment and get your hands on their plans. Hurry, <name>. We might not have much time.

passages.title: Twilight Plans
passages.text: Have you obtained the plans yet, <name>?

passages.title: Twilight Plans
passages.text: Excellent job, <name>.  Now give me a moment to examine the plans you've brought me.

passages.title: Spirit of the Thistle Bear
passages.text:
In these woods reside three great spirits, that of the Stag, that of the Thistle Bear, and that of the Moonstalker. These spirits make powerful allies, but you can only align yourself with one of them.

If you wish to align yourself with the Great Thistle Bear Spirit, take this incense to a cave just east of the great whirlpool. Meditate before the great spirit while burning the incense on the ground between you, and face his trial to earn his blessing. Should you succeed, return to me.

passages.title: Spirit of the Thistle Bear
passages.text:
For countless ages I have walked these forests and lived in these mountains. Through snow and fire, I have watched civilizations crumble and nature press on. Now, the very earth turns against us, and it becomes very apparent that we must fight if our legacy is to continue.

Your heart is true, and I would choose you as our champion. If you value the thick hide and resilience of my kind, then accept my boon. Know that the other spirits will not accept you once this choice is made, so choose wisely.

passages.title: Unsavory Remedies
passages.text:
I have no doubts that Grimclaw will recover with the help of my healing magics, though I can't say the same for the poachers that attacked him. Still, I could use some salve to close his wounds and lessen his pain while he heals.

To the east you will find the Ruins of Lornesta. Among the crumbled stones, there is a variety of fuming toadstool that flourishes in the damp environment. Bring me some of the toadstools so that I can mix a salve for our friend here.

passages.title: Unsavory Remedies
passages.text: Grimclaw is quite the fierce combatant. I feel somewhat sorry for those poachers, despite their aims.

passages.title: Unsavory Remedies
passages.text: You have my thanks, young one. We should be able to speed Grimclaw's recovery dramatically with this salve.

passages.title: Grimclaw's Return
passages.text:
With the binding complete, the blessing has taken hold. It will most certainly make your travels in these lands easier.

Grimclaw made a full recovery. Before I could do anything to stop him, he bolted off towards Lor'danel. I suppose that means it's time for your departure.

It was a great pleasure to have met you. For now, farewell - send my best wishes to Volcor and Grimclaw.

passages.title: Grimclaw's Return
passages.text:
You've returned! It is good to see you again. I suppose we have you to thank for Grimclaw's return?

I'm afraid... I have some bad news. I've been unable to purge the toxin... their conditions worsen. Gershalla died shortly after you left, and Volcor... Volcor passed just before you came back.

He lived long enough to see Grimclaw come back safely, so he died with a smile on his face. I'm just sorry that I couldn't do more.

For now, I'm doing everything I can to save Shaldyn, so please excuse me.

passages.title: Naga of the Strand
passages.text:
There is evil lurking on the coast to the west.

The Zoram Strand is the resting place of the doomed city of Zoram, destroyed during the Sundering and submerged beneath the seas. It has been lost to the night elves for ages. Lost, and nearly forgotten.

Now, the naga have returned, and for what reason we do not know. But reason matters little; we must slay these fiends and throw them back to the depths!

passages.title: Naga of the Strand
passages.text:
Very well done, <name>. Your actions in the Zoram Strand against the naga are commendable.

I know your feat was not easily accomplished, for the strength and guile of the naga is well known to the night elves. We know this, for we share a history with them.

The naga are cursed Highborne night elves. Ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara made a pact of desperation with the Old Gods to save her surviving people from a watery grave.

The naga are the result of that pact.

passages.title: The Last Refugee
passages.text:
There was this massive earthquake and then everything went black. The next thing I know, I woke up here a prisoner. The whole place is overrun with air elementals!

I hope that everyone's okay. These Twillight's Hammer scum better not have hurt any of my friends!

Quick, <class>, use something sharp to jimmy the lock on this ball and chain. Together we should be able to make it to the refugee camp.

passages.title: The Last Refugee
passages.text:
Aye, you're the fine lad who saved my Hollee!

Well, I've got a fitting reward for you here, I'm sure. We really can't thank you enough for bringing her to safety, <name>.

passages.title: Rescue the Fallen
passages.text:
Our forces are holding up admirably, <class>.

Be that as it may, there are yet wounded to attend to - many still in the field of battle.

I have created a salve that should grant the wounded enough energy to return to the ramparts for treatment. Please administer it to any in need before they become lost to us.

passages.title: Rescue the Fallen
passages.text:
Thank you, <race>. I shall include your service to the Horde in my report.

I should have these troops fit to fight again in no time!

passages.title: West to the Strand
passages.text:
<name>, I have a friend who could make good use of particular talents. His name is Talen and he's an archaeologist of sorts. Recently he's been fascinated with the upheaval of the old city of Zoram and its treasures.

If you're willing to lend him a hand, you can find him at the Blackfathom Camp down the path to the west.

passages.title: West to the Strand
passages.text:
Hello, <class>.

What's that? You say that Shyela sent you?

Very well, let's get started.

passages.title: Respect for the Fallen
passages.text:
There were two humans here: Feero Ironhand and Delgren the Purifier. They were members of a holy organization known as The Argent Dawn. Both fell defending the post when the Horde first attacked.

I'm going to loan you my magical cloak. It was a gift from Cenarius that allows me to move invisibly.

Find both of their corpses and retrieve Feero's hammer and Delgren's prayer book. Feero's corpse is in the courtyard and Delgren's is atop the tower.

Beware, the warlock up there will be able to see you.

passages.title: Respect for the Fallen
passages.text: Our losses here have been staggering.

passages.title: Respect for the Fallen
passages.text:
I do not look forward to writing the letter to the Argent Dawn embassy in Darnassus. At least we'll be able to send their most prized possessions back for their loved ones.

I cannot thank you enough for your courage, <name>. Please accept this on behalf of the post.

passages.title: The Reason Why
passages.text:
The furbolg have descended from the heights and overrun the Ruins of Ordil'Aran to the north. I believe they did so because they were attracted to what the dead cultists there uncovered: three moonstones.

Liladris Moonriver will counsel you to deal with the furbolg in a more direct manner, and I will not gainsay her, but I would ask that you go to the ruins and deactivate the moonstones.

passages.title: The Reason Why
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

With the moonstones of Ordil'Aran deactivated, we should not need to worry about any further incursions of furbolg here.

However, my scouts have returned with disturbing news from the furbolg village. There is an imminent danger massing there.

I wonder, might I entice you to carry a warning to Astranaar for me?

passages.title: Rear Guard Duty
passages.text:
The moon priestess has a plan to make sure that no further furbolg descend upon us from the highlands. I am more concerned with those that are already at the ruins, some of which are massing just outside of the post.

Distasteful as it may be, I must ask that you head north into the Ruins of Ordil'Aran and slay the furbolg. We cannot fight on two fronts!

Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Rear Guard Duty
passages.text:
We are in your debt, <class>. If I know anything about the furbolg, they do not like their noses bloodied.

It won't be long now before they tuck tail and return to their village.

passages.title: Stormpike's Orders
passages.text:
I need to get some orders up to Mountaineer Stormpike at his post in Algaz Station. If you wouldn't mind taking them, just follow the road all the way up to the northwest and you'll be sure to see the main bunker.

If you'd like to lend a hand in accomplishing his tasks, we'd be glad to reward you for that as well.

passages.title: Stormpike's Orders
passages.text:
Orders! Let's see what we have here... hah! He wants me to deal with the infestation of rat men. We're already in the middle of that, so no real deviation there.

Care to lend a hand?

passages.title: Ram Delivery
passages.text:
The mountaineers at South Gate Outpost have requested a delivery of rams for their patrols. I didn't think we'd be able to spare any, but we can get them at least one thanks to you.

Mind riding it over and delivering it to Private Hammerfall for me? Just let me know when you're ready to go.

passages.title: Resupplying the Excavation
passages.text:
Ironband has an excavation to the southeast and he's been needing a hefty amount of explosives sent from the league for all the carving. Huldar, Miran, and Saean just departed with the most recent load and could probably use a hand.

They can't have made it very far, strong as they are. They can only move so fast laden down with those barrels.

They're taking the normal route to the site, leaving south out of town and following the curve of the Loch. Go catch up with them and help'm out, will ya?

passages.title: Resupplying the Excavation
passages.text:
Hmph, it'll take more than a Dark Iron ambush to stop the deliveries!

But Saean... I would never have suspected him to be one of their sympathizers. We've been working with him for almost a year now... maybe I missed the signs.

Well, I'll consider that later.

passages.title: Bathed in Light
passages.text:
The concoction is not quite complete; it must be bathed within the Light of Elune before we can even think about giving it to the child.

There is a known location just to the west at Lake Falathim where the goddess's moonlight always touches down, day or night. Please, <name>, I implore you for the sake of Relara, take the concoction and bathe it in Elune's radiance.

But beware, strange things have befallen the area of the lake, and I fear that it is no longer safe to go there.

passages.title: Bathed in Light
passages.text: Did you have any trouble getting to the Light of Elune at Lake Falathim?

passages.title: Bathed in Light
passages.text:
With the concoction blessed by the Light of Elune, it should be ready for delivery to Astranaar.

There is no time to waste, <name>!

passages.title: That Which Has Risen
passages.text:
When I sensed these... things... rising from below, I came to put them back down. I found the corpse of your friend and dragged him as far as I could before one of my fetlocks was broken. It is all that I can do to hold off these foul tendrils.

There is one that controls the tendrils and eyes. It calls itself Harbinger Aphotic -- I'm sure that you have heard it yelling from the south.

The harbinger stands out of range of my magic, but you could get to him. If you dare....

passages.title: That Which Has Risen
passages.text: The harbinger yet lives, <name>. I cannot begin to cleanse Lake Falathim until it is slain.

passages.title: That Which Has Risen
passages.text:
With the death of the harbinger, I can begin to cleanse the lake.

You have my deepest thanks, <name>. I mourn the loss of your friend, but know that his remains will fuel the reclamation of the forest hereabouts.

passages.title: To Raene Wolfrunner
passages.text:
I would ask you to deliver the gem directly to Raene Wolfrunner. Last I heard, she was still in Astranaar to the southeast.

At least the road between here and there is still relatively safe, so it should be a simple matter of following it there. Of course, if you'd rather, I believe that Sentinel Avana would be willing to loan you one of her nightsabers to swiftly make the trip.

Whatever you choose, good health to you, <name>. May our paths cross again soon.

passages.title: To Raene Wolfrunner
passages.text: I am Raene Wolfrunner. Who might you be?

passages.title: To Raene Wolfrunner
passages.text:
Teronis is dead?

<The lady weeps softly for the loss of her friend and then composes herself after a moment.>

We must see to it that his sacrifice was not in vain. Are you willing to see this through, <class>?

Very well, allow me some time to think about how we should proceed. I will know shortly.

passages.title: Astranaar Bound
passages.text:
You have been of great assistance to us, <name>. Without you, we would have been wiped out by now.

It would be my pleasure to offer you one of my nightsabers anytime to ride to Astranaar up and to the southeast. I'm sure that you have very important business to attend to there.

I would consider it a great kindness if you would speak with my sister, Sentinel Luara, when you arrive to tell her that I am well.

Just speak to me again when you are ready to go, and anytime that you need a ride it is yours.

passages.title: Astranaar Bound
passages.text:
Avana is alive?! I feared that she might be dead when we heard about the attack on Maestra's Post!

As you can see, we have our hands full with the Horde here as well.

You have given me the greatest gift by letting me know she is well. Any time that you wish to ride one of my nightsabers back to Maestra's Post, it is yours.

passages.title: Joining the Hunt
passages.text:
Well, you definitely have some fight in you.

You know, there are some hunter types at the lodge east of here, up in the hills - they might be right up your alley. Why don't you go pay them a visit and see if they have any work that you might be interested in?

passages.title: Joining the Hunt
passages.text: Hello there, laddy! The mountaineers sent you over, eh? I do suspect we might have just the sort of work you're looking for. Welcome to the Farstrider Lodge!

passages.title: WANTED: The Dark Iron Spy
passages.text:
A dark iron spy has infiltrated the town, stolen documents from the Explorers' League establishment, and is now in hiding somewhere nearby. He was last sighted near the top of the hill to the south of town.

A sizable reward awaits anyone who can bring this spy to justice. Dead or alive - dead preferred.

passages.title: WANTED: The Dark Iron Spy
passages.text: You brought that damned spy to justice! This is good news. We can all rest a little bit easier, not worrying about that one.

passages.title: Defense of the Stonewrought Dam
passages.text:
We appreciate all of your help. We'll regain control of the excavation with a little bit of time, I'm just glad to know that all of our work wasn't destroyed in the process of this occupation.

We've been greedy enough with your time. I have a friend who could really use some of your help if you have any to lend. Go to the far side of the Loch and you'll find Stonewrought Dam. Once you're there, seek out Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII.

passages.title: Stopping the Rituals
passages.text:
I could not help but overhear Illiyana's loss. I understand her need for revenge. I am wondering if while you are exacting it, you could do us a service?

No doubt you have already seen the satyr of Satyrnaar and Xavian conducting vile rituals. I believe that they are preparing their rituals to corrupt any of the night elves they capture, turning them into satyrs. We draenei also have problems with fel magic exposure.

Would you disturb their ritual gems while you are there?

passages.title: Stopping the Rituals
passages.text:
We are in your debt, <class>.

Unable to complete their nefarious rituals, the satyr are now fighting a losing battle where they are unable to replenish their numbers.

passages.title: Explosives Shredding
passages.text:
I hate to send you back in there, but based on your description of what's going on, we can't let them use all of those explosives they have stored up!

It's too dangerous for you to try to destroy them yourself, but if you were to steal one of their shredders, I'm sure they're tough enough to withstand the explosions.

After you've destroyed their explosives, return here with the shredder. There's no sense in letting them have it back.

passages.title: Explosives Shredding
passages.text: Time's running out, <name>.

passages.title: Explosives Shredding
passages.text:
I saw those explosions all of the way from over here! Those filthy orcs and their goblin lackeys are going to have a hard time doing anything to despoil the forest now!

We can't thank you enough, <name>. Will this do?

passages.title: Closure is Only Natural
passages.text:
Through the ground I can feel more demons being brought into our world. Soon there will be too many and we will be overrun without hope of turning them back.

Take this piece of me and return to Demon Fall Canyon and Demon Fall Ridge, south of Felfire Hill. Aim the bough at a demon gate and concentrate. I have stored a portion of the forest's life force in its wood, and it will close the gate.

passages.title: Closure is Only Natural
passages.text:
With their gates closed and no further reinforcements coming, it is only a matter of time now before the demons are no more.

You are a hero of the forest, <name>. I give you thanks on behalf of all of Ashenvale's creatures!

passages.title: The Forest Heart
passages.text:
You must get the Forest Heart to Gnarl at all costs!

Down at the bottom of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den it sits, corrupted by the Horde. Only Gnarl can cleanse it.

In order to move it, though, you'll need a Power of Nature. If you collect enough untainted spirits from the Severed druids and keepers, the spirits can be combined into a Power of Nature.

Good luck, <name>!

passages.title: The Forest Heart
passages.text: <name>, you have returned.

passages.title: The Forest Heart
passages.text:
The Forest Heart! It's corrupted!

<The great ancient creaks as its immense limbs begin to perform a ritual.>

Stand back, <name>, I will try to cleanse the heart before all is lost!

passages.title: Dirty Deeds
passages.text:
What Draaka requires is a magnet of sorts - something that her demonic missiles will be drawn to.

<Durak grins slyly.>

I happen to know of a method that should suit our purposes.

You scour the mines for fist-sized chunks of ore, while I prepare a special... enchantment.

passages.title: Dirty Deeds
passages.text: Have you collected the ore we need?

passages.title: Dirty Deeds
passages.text: Well done! These should hold a curse long enough for our purposes....

passages.title: Where Are My Keys?
passages.text: I can't find my keys -- I suspect my evil twin is at fault. "Take care" of him for me, <name>.

passages.title: Get My Keys!
passages.text: Get 'em!

passages.title: Dead Elves Walking
passages.text:
D-did you hear that? Ghosts! I hate ghosts!

Their eerie howls are coming from the barrows to the south. Ahhh! Make them stop!!

Please, <mister/missy> I'll pay good money to get those voices out of my head!

passages.title: Dead Elves Walking
passages.text:
Woohooo!!

You've silenced the voices! Thank you, thank you!

passages.title: Mission Improbable
passages.text:
I have a special mission that requires a well equipped, competent <class>. As I have no one else to spare, I suppose I'll have to settle for you...

The enemy has assaulted Warsong Lumber Camp and cut it off from the rest of our forces. An important blood elf diplomat en route to Orgrimmar is trapped there.

She must be liberated.

Take the road northeast and light the smoldering brazier to summon our operative there. Do whatever he might require of you.

Dismissed!

passages.title: Mission Improbable
passages.text:
You have your work cut out for you here, friend.

Let's hope that you're up to the task,,,,

passages.title: A Troubling Prescription
passages.text: A crude, hastily-assembled apothecary's workbench stands here, heaped with scrawled notes and noxious brews. It looks as though the Forsaken have also been studying Foulhoof's handiwork. You grab the most important-looking notes and prepare to smash the laboratory before notifying Treetender of your discovery.

passages.title: A Troubling Prescription
passages.text: What's this? You found something else in the cave?

passages.title: A Troubling Prescription
passages.text:
<Tharnariun Treetender pages through the notes as you relate your story, the lines in his face deepening with concern.>

So the Forsaken have been studying Foulhoof's work? My gut crawls at the thought of what they might have done were they able to weaponize his corruption. You've done well to destroy their work, but this raises deeper concerns. What brought the Forsaken to our doorstep? Are they working with the Shatterspear trolls to our north? Sorrows are heaping upon sorrows, <class>. I'm glad you're here.

passages.title: Dread Head Redemption
passages.text:
I sense that Durak is more than he seems. Demonic power is dangerous and it is easy to fall to its corruption - even for a trained warlock. 

I do not trust him, <name>.

Find this Durak and tell him that the Horde will have nothing to do with him.

passages.title: Dread Head Redemption
passages.text: Have you brought me the head of the enemy, <race>?

passages.title: Dread Head Redemption
passages.text:
Grah... very well.

I'll remove the bounty I had placed upon your head. Though I am sorely tempted to end your life anyway, just on principle.

Be sure that you never raise my ire again, <name>. Now, get out of my sight...

passages.title: Bad News Bear-er
passages.text:
No reports have made it out of here since the beginning of the siege on Splintertree. By now, Commander Grimfang must be getting anxious.

I am sending you to Zoram Strand to deliver our report. It's not pretty, but at least he'll have the facts.

Speak to Vhulgra when you're ready to make the trip.

passages.title: Bad News Bear-er
passages.text:
<Commander Grimfang's brow wrinkles as he reads the report.>

This is grim news, indeed.

May the spirits preserve them until we can fight our way to Splintertree....

passages.title: Astranaar's Burning!
passages.text:
<class>, Astranaar's burning!

Quickly, take this bucket of water and put out the fires before there's nothing left!

passages.title: Astranaar's Burning!
passages.text:
Thank you!

Now it's time to deal with the Horde!

passages.title: Culling the Furbolg Threat
passages.text:
Directly to the north of Astranaar are the Thistlefur furbolg. My scouts report that their numbers have grown greatly over the past few months. If they grow too great, they may find the courage to attack Astranaar directly!

Go to Thistlefur Village and kill as many of their kind as you can.

I shall remain here in Astranaar and await word from you. Elune be with you, <class>.

passages.title: Culling the Furbolg Threat
passages.text:
Well done, <name>.

We are under constant threat from the furbolg. Hopefully this will keep them at bay for a bit longer.

passages.title: Corrupting Influence?
passages.text:
As you search through the belongings of the dead furbolg lying before you, a small charm, very obviously created by trolls, spills out onto the ground.

Touching the charm, you immediately get a sense that something is not right about the wood. A feeling of unease, of corruption, permeates the object.

Wrapping it in some spare cloth, you put it in your pack and resolve to show it to Raene Wolfrunner when next you find yourself in Astranaar.

passages.title: Corrupting Influence?
passages.text: What's troubling you, <class>?

passages.title: Corrupting Influence?
passages.text:
A troll charm? What are the furbolg doing with such a thing?

You're right, it does have a feeling of corruption about it... even I can sense that.

There's someone here who might be able to help.

passages.title: Recover the Remains
passages.text:
While what the satyrs have done to the trees is horrible, nothing compares to the mass slaughter that the orcs have been engaging in!

<The ancient shakes with visible rage, his leaves falling all around you.>

<race>, I would have you head across the road here at the lumber camp and recover the remains of those trees, treants, and ancients that the Horde have hewn down in their prime.

passages.title: Recover the Remains
passages.text: Have you the remains, little one?

passages.title: Recover the Remains
passages.text:
I have lived a very long time in peace with the forest, but what these orc-things are doing makes me want to feed them back to the ground!

I will put this wood to rest now. Thank you for this kindness, <name>. I will never forget.

passages.title: Security!
passages.text:
It's not as like I haven't got enough to think about here!

Keeping this place operational is hard enough without constant elf and draenei harassment.

Now, on top of everything, there's an assassin lurking around the camp who's killed an important diplomat... on my watch!

Whoever it is couldn't have gotten far, <class>. Scour the camp until you find her and then avenge the diplomat!

At least I can bring the assassin's head with me when I have to answer to Hellscream.

passages.title: Security!
passages.text:
I want to know one thing, <race>.

Is that assassin dead?

passages.title: Security!
passages.text:
Well done, <class>.

One last request - it would probably be best if none of my laborers knew this assassin ever existed.

passages.title: Worgen Wisdom
passages.text:
The man standing right across from me is known as Hephaestus Pilgrim. He's one of the worgen.

He and his sister came to Astranaar not long ago looking for a place to live. From what little I've been able to glean, he's interested in trying to help the Earthen Ring with the Cataclysm. His sister is even more powerful. She's gone east to try and help the shaman deal with the volcano.

Perhaps he can help. Take the charm over to him and see what he thinks.

passages.title: Worgen Wisdom
passages.text: <The worgen gives you a blank look as you walk up to him.>

passages.title: Worgen Wisdom
passages.text: <Looking down at the wooden carving in your extended hand, the worgen reaches out to take it.>

passages.title: A Not-So-Charmed Life
passages.text:
The furbolg covet that which does not belong to them.

<Hephaestus turns the charm over in his hand and then discards it.>

There's a property to the carving that slowly corrupts those that aren't trolls. As I understand it, the furbolg have done this sort of thing before. Some never learn.

No doubt they hoard most of the charms in Thistlefur Hold above their village to the north.

passages.title: A Not-So-Charmed Life
passages.text:
Do you think that you retrieved all of the troll charms from Thistlefur Hold?

If any are left behind, the Thistlefur tribe will continue to be influenced by them, and eventually they will attack this place.

passages.title: A Not-So-Charmed Life
passages.text:
<Hephaestus nods slowly as he looks you straight in the eye.>

You've likely saved the Thistlefur from themselves, at least in the short run.  If they can keep from stealing objects of power that don't belong to them, that is.

I understand that the night elves are having problems with the other furbolg tribe to the south. That's something that Raene is going to want to speak to you about.

However, there are more immediate concerns that I would ask for your help with.

passages.title: Too Far Gone
passages.text:
Yes, I speak your tongue, <race>.

We furbolg have been through this kind of corruption before. Not long ago our leader stole the Idol of Remulos. The demon-tainted thing ensorcelled the entire tribe and our redemption was barely delivered by a druid known as Broll Bearmantle.

But this time, we did not steal. The trolls of Zoram'gar gave us the charms as a sign of friendship. A deadly friendship it would seem.

Our chief, Dal Bloodclaw, is too far gone. Enter the hold and return with his charms.

passages.title: Too Far Gone
passages.text: Well? The future of the Thistlefur rests upon your shoulders, <race>.

passages.title: Too Far Gone
passages.text:
What was done had to be done. As our leader, Dal's sickness from the troll charms was destroying us.

It was better for the health and dignity of the tribe that it was you, outsider. This way there will be no civil war amongst us and we will easily find new leadership... hopefully one that does not have a tendency to so easily trust outsiders. Perhaps I am guilty of this as well?

Here, allow me to repay the debt we owe you before we part ways forever.

passages.title: Go With The Flow
passages.text:
<The worgen stares at you intently before launching into his request.>

The volcano threatens to engulf all of Ashenvale if we do not act quickly. Let me assure you, this was no natural eruption.

My sister, Sabina, is powerful. She has gone east to the edge of Thunder Peak's lava flow, just north of the road to enlist the aid of the other elements against the fire lord that has caused this destruction.

<name>, go to her and give her what assistance you can.

passages.title: Go With The Flow
passages.text:
My brother must have sent you. He wouldn't have done so unless you are capable of doing what must be done.

For all of our sakes I hope that he's right.

The elementals here are now my allies. You must do as they ask if we are to prevent the destruction of the rest of Ashenvale.

passages.title: Thunder Peak
passages.text:
Greetings, <class>.

Congratulations on your victorious assault on Astranaar. The elves shall not soon forget the humiliation they have suffered at your hand.

But you must know, the elves are not the only obstacle to the Horde's conquering of Ashenvale....

To the east, a shaman of the Earthen Ring requires assistance with yet another crisis. You can find him near the base of the volcano, Thunder Peak.

passages.title: Thunder Peak
passages.text:
<The goblin stares at you and blinks several times before speaking.>

The spirits whispered that help would soon arrive.

Pardon my surprise, but I was hoping the spirits would guide someone a little more... heroic.

These elementals are trusted allies. Listen to them and do their bidding. If we fail, there will remain nothing in Ashenvale worth fighting for.

passages.title: Hot Lava
passages.text:
<The massive earth elemental gazes down upon you.>

The flow of the lava must be stopped if we are to prevail. I will grant to you a portion of my power. Use it to fill the lava fissures!

passages.title: Hot Lava
passages.text: Done?

passages.title: Hot Lava
passages.text: Well done, <race>. Lord Magmathar's fire is now trapped, restrained within the earth once more.

passages.title: Consumed
passages.text:
My first concern right now is for the thistle bear families who call what's left of these woods home. Just to our south, beyond the bear shrine, an entire generation has fallen ill. Gruesomely ill.

<name>, I don't know what they're suffering from, but it's consumed them from within. It pains me that a whole generation is beyond saving, but we've got to kill them off so that the earth can reclaim their bodies.

More importantly, we need to find the source. Investigate the shallow lake they drink from!

passages.title: Consumed
passages.text:
<Kathrena recoils at your description of the ravaged animals and the cruel device at the bottom of the lake>

<name>, this is terrible. What is that thing, and how did it get there? Something is devouring these animals, physically and spiritually. I had suspected the satyrs or some sort of disease was the culprit, but this is shaping up to be something ... unnatural.

passages.title: Lousy Pieces of Ship
passages.text:
Shoddy workmanship! There's no other explanation...

These ships must've been constructed in a hurry. Entire pieces of armor plating are falling off without even sustaining a direct hit!

I'll show them how it is to be done. But first, I need you to recover the pieces from the sea floor.

Return to me with the pieces and I'll do the rest.

passages.title: Lousy Pieces of Ship
passages.text: Were you able to recover that armor plating, <race>?

passages.title: Lousy Pieces of Ship
passages.text:
Good work, <race>.

I'll show them how an armored ship should be built!

passages.title: Put Out The Fire
passages.text:
Lord Magmathar's minions must first be dealt with if we're to retake this area and put a stop to the fiery destruction of the forest.

The lava ragers on the flow to the north are strengthened by being on their own element. I fear that on your own, you won't have much chance against them.

When you are ready, speak to me again, and I will summon one of my own to assist you.

passages.title: Put Out The Fire
passages.text: There are yet more lava ragers to be destroyed, <race>.

passages.title: Put Out The Fire
passages.text:
You acquitted yourself well in battle on the field. However, I'm afraid that Lord Magmathar has taken notice of you and the destruction that you've wreaked upon his minions.

You will have to deal with him or he is sure to burn you alive, <name>.

passages.title: The Slumbering Ancients
passages.text:
We may not have twenty stone giants to take on our enemy, but we giants of ancient lumber are as strong as any rock.

Look around you, <race>. My kindred sleep... yet they will heed the keeper's horn when the time of need is upon them.

You will find Aros, the keeper of the grove, beyond the bridge northeast of here.

Tell him the urgency of our situation.

passages.title: The Slumbering Ancients
passages.text: Aros's body appears to be lifeless yet still warm.  Perhaps his killers are nearby.

passages.title: Unearthed Knowledge
passages.text:
Listen, <name>. We need to learn more about what we're up against.

To the southwest, beyond the Master's Glaive, there is a group of dwarven prospectors who were excavating the nearby ruins.

Perhaps they have uncovered knowledge that is useful to us in this matter.

passages.title: Unearthed Knowledge
passages.text: Oh, we know a thing or two about this Soggoth.  The question is... do you really want to know?

passages.title: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text:
The ancients of the grove have come to our aid, <name>. I can see through their eyes even as we speak.

The Twilight's Hammer has been forced to hasten their ritual and have thus only managed to resurrect but a remnant of dread Soggoth.

Destroy it before it's too late, <name>. I am needed elsewhere.

Return to the druids at the Grove of the Ancients when it is all over they will direct you further.

passages.title: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text: We can finally rest here now, <name>.  It appears Darkshore has been saved -- and we have you to thank for it.

passages.title: The Tides Turn Against Us
passages.text:
We cannot let the naga get away with this, <name>. Slaying the keeper of the grove amounts to a declaration of war.

You'll find their den inside a cave on the island of Naj'vel, far to the southwest.

I want you to send them a clear message.

passages.title: The Tides Turn Against Us
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  The naga seek the destruction and subjugation of all surface-dwellers -- do not hesitate to drive them out of our lands and back into the shadowy ocean depths where they belong.

passages.title: The Darkscale Warlord
passages.text:
If the naga want to throw in their lot with the Twilight's Hammer, then may Elune have mercy on them.

Go into their lair in the island of Nazj'vel and find their leader, the naga warlord known only as Wrathspine.

Perhaps the horn of the ancients can still be saved.

passages.title: The Darkscale Warlord
passages.text: The walord doesn't seem to have the horn on him.  Perhaps he was telling the truth.

passages.title: Deep Despair
passages.text:
There is more to this naga problem than meets the eye, <class>. It appears that the issue will not be resolved by merely thinning their numbers. To humble them, a more severe impression must be made.

Travel to the northern end of Zoram Strand and enter Blackfathom Deep. Once there, demonstrate to the naga that their presence in this region will no longer be tolerated!

passages.title: Deep Despair
passages.text:
Excellent!

Let the naga retreat back into the seas where they belong!

passages.title: Mounting the Offensive
passages.text:
Our work in Darkshore is not yet done. We might have stopped the landmass from shattering, but our enemies still have a strong presence in the area.

I want you to contact a group of druids at the Grove of the Ancients, far to the south. They are led by an old friend of mine, Balren of the Claw.

Tell them that the time has come to take the battle to our foes. I will come to aid them as soon as we stabilize the area.

passages.title: Mounting the Offensive
passages.text:
If Malfurion placed his trust on you, then so shall I.  You'll find that our enemies greatly outnumber us this far south.

Where brute force and numbers fail us, strategy and guile will prove our biggest advantages.

passages.title: Swamped Secrets
passages.text:
Underneath Remtravel's forgetful exterior is the mind of a genius, an enigma cloaked in senility. But I'm not about to give up on the old man. Look at what I found in his notes... not there... no, that's a shopping list... Here, on the page where he's trying to figure out what year it is: The Disc!

We think this Titan artifact is some sort of encrypted storage wheel. We were carefully unearthing it when the disaster hit, but hopefully it's still in the ruins. Dive in and grab it for me!

passages.title: Swamped Secrets
passages.text: Did you find it? Groff wants to clear out of these ruins as soon as possible!

passages.title: Swamped Secrets
passages.text:
Spectacular! Good work, <name>. I'm sure Remtravel would thank you himself if he could remember your name.

Look at the surface of the disc - these microscopic etchings - this is amazing. I'm certain this strange wheel holds information, if only we could read it...

passages.title: Before You Go...
passages.text:
We have urgent need for good <class>s at Hellscream's Watch, <name>. But before you're dispatched, there remains something that needs doing here.

Most of our perishable goods were lost at sea due mainly to Alliance attacks. We must stock enough food to carry out our Ashenvale campaign.

Just east of here, you should find wildlife in abundance. Bring back the best meat you can find for our troops!

passages.title: Before You Go...
passages.text: Yes, <race>?

passages.title: Before You Go...
passages.text: These venison should make our soldiers' spirits rise for the coming battles. Here's something for your troubles.

passages.title: He Who Would Be Forgiven
passages.text:
<A voice from inside the moonwell flows over your mind, bringing you a perfect sense of peace.>

You seek to cure a child, but know that all things come at a cost. To the east lies Raynewood Tower. Standing outside the tower, next to my moonwell, is one who has fallen into corruption.

Avrus Illwhisper seeks forgiveness and redemption, <name>. Will you help him to attain that which he desires and in so doing achieve your own goal?

passages.title: He Who Would Be Forgiven
passages.text:
<The satyr sneers, but when he realizes you are not here to chastise him, he changes his expression.>

Finally, my redemption is at hand. I have waited long for this day and I think I know how to help you in turn.

passages.title: In the Hands of the Perverse
passages.text:
My former clan, the Felmusk of Night Run, raided Fallen Sky Lake some time ago, stealing the moonstones that were unique to the area.

Those moonstones are known to have great healing properties and surely can be used to cure the little girl that lies sick in Astranaar.

Night Run rests up the road to the east that runs north. There are multiple paths that lead up into the hills on its eastern side, and it is there that you will find my unrepentant brethren. They will have what you seek.

passages.title: In the Hands of the Perverse
passages.text: Five moonstones are required to assure that the girl is healed.

passages.title: In the Hands of the Perverse
passages.text:
You have all of the moonstones that are needed. And yet, it is said that a sacrifice of life is the only way to be ensure the saving of another.

I will ensure that no matter what, the moonstones will cure Relara.

passages.title: To Hellscream's Watch
passages.text:
Into the fray with you, <race>!

Hellscream's Watch is one of our most contentious fronts in Ashenvale. The experience should serve you well... assuming you survive.

When you've made ready, speak with Andruk. I've arranged for him to transport you directly to your station.

Once you've arrived, seek out Captain Goggath. He will guide you further.

Bring pain and death to our enemies! For the Horde!

passages.title: To Hellscream's Watch
passages.text:
You come here as a child, <race>.

You shall leave here a battle-hardened <class> of the Horde!

That, or a corpse....

passages.title: Recover the Fallen
passages.text:
I and my sentinels have been ordered by Keeper Ordanus to stay here and hold the tower. So far we've been able to repel the Horde, but now they're going around us to directly attack the retreat to the north.

The keeper sent out his dryads to defend the tree, but they do not seem to be much of a match for the vanguard of the Warsong orcs.

I need you to go out there and recover as many laughing sister corpses as you can. Take them to Halannia inside the tree at the retreat. She will know what to do.

passages.title: Recover the Fallen
passages.text: I'm amazed that you broke through the Horde lines and managed to get in here, <race>.

passages.title: Recover the Fallen
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>. We have our hands full defending the retreat, but when I can catch my breath, I'll see to it that these sisters are returned to life, the goddess willing.

You've demonstrated your prowess... we can use your help.

passages.title: Tweedle's Dumb
passages.text:
Delays, delays, delays! I'm at wit's end!

I was told that this goblin was brilliant - that he'd come up with gadgets sure to shock the enemy into submission. So far he's produced nothing but empty promises. If he comes up empty-handed again, I'm going to toss him off the cliff!

You go and speak to him, <class>. Let him know that my fuse is running short!

passages.title: Tweedle's Dumb
passages.text:
Let me tell ya somethin' <class>!

The bossman simply doesn't appreciate the art and craftsmanship that goes into making fine explosives.

passages.title: Fel Moss Corruption
passages.text:
I'd hoped to never return to Teldrassil for such grim business. I'd hoped that its corruption had been wiped away completely. Something fowl lingers.

The corruption of the wicked fel moss still threatens to turn peaceful creatures against us. The grells and gellkin still infest the area and threaten Shadowglen's residents.

Engage these grells and grellkin, <name>, and see if they are indeed caught under the enchantment of the wicked fel moss. Once we know for certain, we will know how to proceed.

passages.title: Leaving the Dream
passages.text: Hold on tight, <name>. The journey back to the waking world can be a little rough on unprepared minds and bodies.

passages.title: Leaving the Dream
passages.text: You're just in time, <name>.  I don't know how much longer we can hold.

passages.title: Resident Danger
passages.text:
The Gnarlpine aggression is limiting our options. None of our kind are eager to bring blade and arrow against creatures that were once our friends, but I grow fearful that they are going to set their sights on Dolanaar soon.

The biggest concern to me are the furbolg in Ban'ethil Hollow and Ban'ethil Barrow Dens. I need you to travel to the west, make your way into the Barrow Den, and kill as many of the Gnarlpine as you can. We probably won't have many more chances to limit their strength - be swift.

passages.title: Resident Danger
passages.text:
Impressive. I hope my huntress carried her weight.

If we continue with this fervor, we may yet still free Teldrassil from the corruption that Alexstrasza herself could not burn out.

passages.title: Nature's Reprisal
passages.text:
I'm glad you were willing to atone for your mistake - it speaks a great deal about your character.

I have another task for you. I have gathered some ireroot seeds. They are somewhat like fel cones, but quite a bit more potent. Nature often responds very negatively to demons, and these ireroot seeds prompt a very concentrated form of that reprisal.

To our north, in Fel Rock, there are grellkin that are far beyond redemption. Use the ireroot seeds to route them before they become a more serious threat.

passages.title: Nature's Reprisal
passages.text: Did you have any success in routing those grellkin for us?

passages.title: Nature's Reprisal
passages.text:
Good. I know this probably wasn't very pleasant work, but we greatly appreciate it.

I fear for our dear Teldrassil... it seems it is becoming more corrupt by the day, and our ignorance to the cause is plaguing me greatly.

passages.title: Naga In Our Midst
passages.text:
The creature appears to have had its skull broken in a fight with Aros. It looks like what you've heard described as a naga before.

It is said that despite their monstrous features, naga are night elves warped by the arcane magic of Queen Azshara.

It seems they've decided to stop you from obtaining the horn of the ancients.

passages.title: Naga In Our Midst
passages.text: The naga are in league with the Twilight's Hammer?  Just what we needed.

passages.title: Condition Critical!
passages.text:
We have the enemy on their heels. Victory is within sight!

It is not yet time to celebrate though, <class>. There remains much to be done before the Horde can lay claim to Ashenvale.

At Raynewood Retreat to the east a battle has been joined. Reports indicate many Horde wounded.

Take these medical supplies there and give them to Thagg. Tell him of our assault on Astranaar. It may help to bolster morale.

passages.title: Condition Critical!
passages.text:
<Thagg listens intently as you recount your assault on Astranaar.>

This is good news indeed, <race>. But right now, we need more than just good news here.

These triage kits will be put to good use!

passages.title: Stalemate
passages.text:
The triage kits will help us keep up the fight, but we are at a stalemate.

The dryads die easy enough, but their leader is resurrecting them soon after they fall. We face an endless stream of the vermin!

Keeper Ordanus hides in that mutated tree. Our efforts to fight our way to him have been in vain. Perhaps you could work your way to him while we contend with his dryads...

Surely, this is child's play for someone who has conquered Astranaar. No?

passages.title: Stalemate
passages.text: Well, <race>? Is Ordanus defeated?

passages.title: Stalemate
passages.text:
Very well, <name>.

You have succeeded where I could not. You have earned my respect.

passages.title: To the Spire
passages.text:
We've lost Silverwind Refuge! All that I know is that there was a surprise attack by the Horde and that they somehow turned Mystral Lake's elemental guardians against us.

The survivors have fallen back to Stardust Spire. <name>, they need your help.

Head south by southeast. You'll find the spire at the mouth of the Talondeep Pass, which leads into the Stonetalon Mountains. I'm sure that you'll find Sentinel Velene Starstrike helping with the counter-offensive there.

passages.title: To the Spire
passages.text:
Good to finally meet you, <name>. I've heard all about what you've been up to and let me just say that I'm impressed!

Think you can lend us your expertise?

passages.title: Check in on the Edunes
passages.text:
<name>, if you have a moment to spare, I would enlist your aid in a simple matter.

I have not heard from my friends, the Edunes, in some time. I was wondering if you could swing west and check in on them?

You have my thanks. Their cottage sits on a small plot of land just to the west of the Shrine of Aessina.

passages.title: Check in on the Edunes
passages.text:
You say that Faldreas sent you?  Good man.

As it happens, we could use your help.

passages.title: Grol'dom's Missing Kodo
passages.text: Friend, if you are traveling south to Thorn Hill, I was wondering if you could locate one of our missing kodos? Not every caravan has made it up the pass from Far Watch Post. Those Razormane brutes hijacked a pack animal yesterday morning. It may not still be alive, but if it is, we cannot afford to lose more of our livestock.

passages.title: Grol'dom's Missing Kodo
passages.text: This poor battered kodo looks to be on the verge of death, but is still breathing. The Razormane haven't even plundered its cargo yet. If it can be revived, you may be able to save the entire shipment.

passages.title: Animal Services
passages.text:
Kodos are resilient creatures. With some food, the big guy may come around.

The Razormane have stolen plenty of grain from previous caravans. You can gather up stolen grain from the nearby camps.

passages.title: Animal Services
passages.text: The creature doesn't lift its head, but looks at you imploringly with large, watery eyes.

passages.title: Animal Services
passages.text:
The Kodo is voracious! You might as well be pouring those sacks of grain into a hole!

Already the animal is beginning to perk up.

passages.title: Among Humans Again
passages.text:
Finally! It looks like Grennan's potion worked on at least one of you ferals.

You should be able to stay in control for the most part -- just watch your temper.

Major Arsmtead's going to want to speak to you. Gilneas is under attack and we need every able-bodied combatant to take up arms.

passages.title: The Grol'dom Militia
passages.text:
