Ah, my savior! I've heard that you're on a mission to save Lakeshire... and my bridge. Yep, worked too damned long on that thing to let it get destroyed by an army of marauding orc monsters!

Listen, if you're headed up north towards Render's Camp, would you do me a solid and get me some spyglasses from the Blackrock trackers up there? I could sure use 'em for my new surveying gear.

passages.title: Surveying Equipment
passages.text: Did you recover the spyglasses?

passages.title: Surveying Equipment
passages.text: Fantastic work, <name>! These will come in handy for our next project, the Lakeshire SUPER BRIDGE, meant to traverse the length of Lake Everstill. It should be done in 20 or so years. Give or take a decade or two.

passages.title: Render's Army
passages.text:
Heading up north, eh? How about you wage your own little war against those Blackrock monsters? What do you say, <name>?

Kill any Blackrock orc that you see at Alther's Mill or Render's Camp. Kill until your skin turns red from their blood splatter and then come back to me and I'll pay you handsomely.

It might not stop the Blackrock invasion, but it'll be sure to put a kink in their plans.

passages.title: Render's Army
passages.text: You've probably bought us another day, maybe two. Nice work, <name>.

passages.title: Weapons of War
passages.text:
What I'm about to ask of you isn't going to be easy to accomplish, <name>. Keeshan left everything back there in that orc prison, and I'm not just talking about his soul or his will to live.

If we're going to get Johnny ready for war, we need to recover his prized possessions. The orcs now hold Keeshan's bow and his survival knife.

Head to Alther's Mill, east of here and look for two orc lieutenants, Murdunk and Homurk. They've got Keeshan's gear. Get it back.

I'll be in touch via gnomecorder.

passages.title: Weapons of War
passages.text: Did you terminate Murdunk and Homurk?

passages.title: Weapons of War
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder buzzes with energy.>

Come in, <name>. Do you copy? Troteman here! Great job on getting Keeshan's weapons back! Now there's one final mission you have to run. Are you up to the challenge?

passages.title: His Heart Must Be In It
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder clicks.>

His gear alone won't be enough, <name>. His heart must also be in this battle. To capture that, we need items of sentimental value. The Blackrock orcs of Render's Camp, located in the north, hold two such items that belong to Keeshan.

Get up there and search their coffers for Keeshan's headband and a jade amulet left to him by his wife - who was brutally killed during a Blackrock orc invasion.

Bring them back to me should you succeed.

passages.title: His Heart Must Be In It
passages.text: Did you locate the headband and amulet?

passages.title: His Heart Must Be In It
passages.text: I hope with these items and with his crew all rescued he'll have a change of heart. We can't do this without Keeshan.

passages.title: Adella's Covert Camp
passages.text:
Lady Shandris has already asked for you to assist us further.

Adella has struck out to the east, among the woodpaw gnolls, and established a foothold south of Camp Mojache. You are to report to her if you wish to assist Lady Shandris and the Alliance further.

Don't stray too close to Camp Mojache... the Horde will not hesitate to attack. Keep to the south and look for our banners.

passages.title: Adella's Covert Camp
passages.text: Welcome to Shadebough, <name>. Lady Shandris sent word of you.

passages.title: Steady Hand
passages.text:
Nearby to the north, you will find Terrath the Steady. He has taken upon the task of pulling the stone dragons back into the fold. We find ourselves repeating this trial every few hundred years... the stone dragons are fickle, and bend only to strength.

Terrath is balanced and reasonable, but his goals may not be easily accomplished. Go to him. Appeal to the more balanced side of the Stonemother.

passages.title: Steady Hand
passages.text: Greetings, <race>. I have been told of your coming. If you wish to aid me, then perhaps I can be of aid to you as well.

passages.title: Rocky Upheaval
passages.text:
To the east, on the Crimson Expanse, you will find Gorsik. He embodies the more unstable and violent nature of our kind. He is neither friendly, nor trusting, but his word carries weight.

Proving yourself to Gorsik will go a long way towards proving yourself to the Stonemother.

passages.title: Rocky Upheaval
passages.text:
You are Diamant's chosen.

So small. So fragile.

Do you realize that your actions shall be the basis by which your entire, "Earthen Ring" is judged? You truly think you can stand for so many?

You are a fool. A confident fool. We shall see if you are a capable fool as well.

passages.title: Doomshrooms
passages.text:
The rift to your world has poisoned our home. Corrupted it. Polluted it.

This expanse festers and grows. It becomes difficult to even see the purity of the rock beneath this filth.

If you are here to lend your aid, then go about cleansing this overgrowth. Look for the brightly glowing mushrooms that are growing faster than the others. They are the worst of the offenders.

passages.title: Doomshrooms
passages.text:
You have appealed to Diamant. He is patient. Trusting. Perhaps too much so. You have much to prove if you wish my favor, <race>.

Still, this is a start.

passages.title: Gone Soft
passages.text:
The fungal behemoths that surround us have succumbed to a weakness very similar to that that affects your kind. Their skin has grown soft. They no longer belong with the stone.

Kill them. We do not wish to see this infection spread.

passages.title: Gone Soft
passages.text:
You carry with you a certain degree of potency. I can find some respect for such strength, especially in your kind.

My concerns are not yet abated. Not for the source of the overgrowth, and not for you.

passages.title: Familiar Intruders
passages.text:
Fleshling. Some of your kind skitter among the rocks. Too cowardly to approach, too swift to be crushed.

If you wish my favor, deal with them. I tire of these games.

passages.title: Familiar Intruders
passages.text:
It is good to see you again, brother. I see that your efforts go well. The Stone Lords appear to be showing you some degree of trust.

We've come to help. We might be of some aid in tracking down the source of this sudden growth. I highly suspect your giant friend's aggressions are focused in the wrong direction.

passages.title: Unnatural Causes
passages.text:
This is most definitely magic in origin. Not even druidic. I suspect one among the stone troggs to the north.

Go to Gorsik and point him in their direction. Hopefully this will help earn his favor.

passages.title: Unnatural Causes
passages.text:
The stone troggs? And I am to trust you at your word?

I have no love for the Verlok anyway. Suspicion is more than enough reason to lay waste to them. We shall see if your word is true.

passages.title: Wrath of the Fungalmancer
passages.text:
Their leader hides within his hole ahead. He is the one that has brought the plague upon the crimson expanse.

He must be killed.

One of your Earthen Ring companions is already inside. You should speak with her.

passages.title: Wrath of the Fungalmancer
passages.text:
I cannot fit inside. Our elementals are not up to the task.

You must see this done.

passages.title: Wrath of the Fungalmancer
passages.text:
Well done, <race>.

Gorsik shall hear of your deed. Therazane shall hear of your deed.

You are quite vicious for one so small... and so soft.

passages.title: Shaken and Stirred
passages.text:
I have sent my brothers to assault the Verlok village from below. The Verlok will gather on their rocky ledges, as they always do to avoid our ire. When they do, we shall make the earth itself shake them until they fall at our feet below.

That is where you prove your use. When they fall to the ground amongst my brothers, make sure that they do not rise again.

passages.title: Shaken and Stirred
passages.text: Well done fleshling. Your presence complimented my brothers well.

passages.title: Corruption Destruction
passages.text: If this disgusting growth is truly brought on by the Verlok, then their supplies will be in their village to the north. Bring them to me so that I can verify your claims.

passages.title: Corruption Destruction
passages.text: I await your proof, <race>...

passages.title: Corruption Destruction
passages.text: So your words prove true. You have my gratitude, <race>.

passages.title: In Search of Bravo Company
passages.text:
If you and Keeshan are going to defend Lakeshire, we're going to need to find his old battalion. Last I heard all of 'em - Messner, Jorgensen, Krakauer and Danforth - were captured by the Blackrock orcs. Now I don't know where they could possibly be or if they're even alive, but I'd be a damned fool if I didn't ask you to try and find 'em.

Search Alther's Mill, east of here, for any clues.

passages.title: In Search of Bravo Company
passages.text: Keeshan? You mean JOHNNY'S ALIVE? You bet your sweet behind I'll help, but first you gotta get me out of this damned cage.

passages.title: Breaking Out is Hard to Do
passages.text:
The key to this cage is stored in a pouch over at the worg den, just north of our location. The problem is that the pouch is resting safely atop a tree stump amidst a sea of bloodthirsty man-killing worgs.

You've got one shot to get that key without waking up any of those sleeping worgs. Head to the worg den and find a way into the center. Tread carefully and watch out for the Blackrock worg captain. Get the key and return to me.

If you got a pet, I'd recommend telling it to stay back!

passages.title: Breaking Out is Hard to Do
passages.text: Did you get the cage key?

passages.title: Breaking Out is Hard to Do
passages.text: IT'S PAYBACK TIME!

passages.title: The Wilds of Feralas
passages.text:
You are truly brave to help us protect these lands, hero. If you wish to do more for the wilds, there are others in need of your aid.

The verdant forests of Feralas lie to the south. There, in the shade of the mighty Twin Colossals, you must seek out Konu Runetotem. He has found signs of a disturbing illness.

Follow the road west around the Twin Colossals to find Camp Ataya. Go in peace, <name>, and walk with the Earth Mother.

passages.title: The Wilds of Feralas
passages.text: Peace, friend. I wish we could have met under less troubling circumstances.

passages.title: Battlefront Triage
passages.text:
You seem quick on your feet, <race>. I need someone to go out into the chaos of the front and patch up our injured.

Take my kit. It's simple enough to use.

Heal them before the stone troggs finish them off for good.

passages.title: Battlefront Triage
passages.text: If you ever get tired of your being a <class>, come look me up. You seem very good with those fleshy hands of yours.

passages.title: The Call of Kalimdor
passages.text:
I've been sent by the good people of Theramore to find loyal members of the Alliance who are willing to help Lady Jaina with some problems in Dustwallow.

You weren't really here working for the goblins, were you?

The path back to Dustwallow will take you through Ratchet. Wait on the end of this pier for the next boat. Once you get to Ratchet, speak with Gazlowe. He'll point you in the right direction from there.

Ugh, I think I stepped on a fish! And it flopped!

passages.title: The Call of Kalimdor
passages.text: Yeah?  Whaddya need?

passages.title: Protecting Her Royal Highness Poobah
passages.text:
These vicious jungle cats have been circling me for some time now. I watch them as closely as I can, but they seem to just... disappear into the grass.

How they snarl and hiss!

Don't get me wrong... I still want you to rescue me, but first, clear out some of these cats. I won't need to be rescued if I end up someone's dinner.

passages.title: Protecting Her Royal Highness Poobah
passages.text: Please, my hero, dispose of the stalking panthers!

passages.title: Protecting Her Royal Highness Poobah
passages.text:
It's about time you returned.  I was beginning to worry that I was going to be eaten while you hunted.

A cat eating a princess... wouldn't that be a fancy feast?

passages.title: Negotiations Terminated
passages.text:
Go now, go back to your fleet. Tell them what kind of a monster claims authority over the Dragonmaw.

Our "Warchief" is a traitor to his blood. Since his return from Outland he reeks of demon and leads what remains of our clan to ruin.

Help rid the Dragonmaw of Mor'ghor, and those of us with pure blood will be your allies forever. This I can promise.

passages.title: Negotiations Terminated
passages.text:
The Fel Orcs from Outland have laid claim to the Dragonmaw? Obscene!

If Hellscream knew what was happening here, he'd raze their city to the ground...

passages.title: It's Never Over
passages.text:
Those Blackrock orcs are gonna need an army to handle the Bravo Company and you, <name>. When you're ready to go, meet us at the dock facing Lake Everstill and we'll set off on my riverboat for Camp Everstill on the other side of the lake.

See you there, <name>.

passages.title: It's Never Over
passages.text: It's orc killin' time.

passages.title: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs
passages.text:
Seasoned wolf kabobs are a house favorite! Sure, I can make you some. But first I'll need the supplies.

Bring me five wolf skirt steaks. The dire wolves near the river north of town are good to hunt; I wouldn't stray too far into the woods if I were you.

passages.title: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs
passages.text: Were you able to find five wolf skirt steaks yet?

passages.title: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs
passages.text:
Mmm-mmm! The skirtsteak's the best part. It's not an efficient way to cook, though.

Here, have this recipe. It's a little different, but flank meat's easier to come by when you really need a meal.

passages.title: Dusky Crab Cakes
passages.text:
I'll let you in on a little secret - Dusky "Crab" Cakes are really made from spider meat! I know it's a bit disgusting, but the cakes have a nice, tangy flavor and make great snacks!

If you want to try some still, I'm afraid I'm out of meat. I need some lump meat to whip up a few more cakes.

Venom Web Spiders are a good source - they nest to the north, between the foothills and the river.

passages.title: Dusky Crab Cakes
passages.text: Hail, <name>.  Did you get that lump meat for me?

passages.title: Dusky Crab Cakes
passages.text:
Ah yes, a nice lump you have there!  Let me just get this seasoned with my secret spices (no looking!) and get them to skittering on a skillet for a while...

And, although Dusky Crab Cakes are my specialty and I won't give out the recipe, here's the recipe for a dish that's almost as good.

passages.title: Getting In With the Bloodsail
passages.text:
These plans are... interesting. Firallon, you're smarter than this!

Look, he has all three ships devoted to cannon fire, and only a few men coming in through the tunnel. He can never take Booty Bay with three ships and a dozen footmen. And he knows that.

No, they've got something else planned... and you're going to find out what it is. Speak to Yancey Grillsen, the Bloodsail Recruiter, just to the north of town.

That's right, <name>. You'd better hope that they don't recognize your face.

passages.title: Getting In With the Bloodsail
passages.text: Yarr, ya made a good decision, lad.

passages.title: We Have a Situation
passages.text: One of Clay's catapult teams is broken down on the front. I need you to get some parts from him and get that catapult back in the fight, <name>.

passages.title: The Hermit
passages.text:
I've been told there's signs of activity at Beggar's Haunt. People have reported seeing lights in the tower to the east of town.

Few would be bold enough to stay that close to Deadwind Pass. You're the first to report since I've learned about this; go check it out and make sure whatever's in there is human.

passages.title: The Hermit
passages.text:
Ah, welcome, stranger. I'd offer you something, but there's not much here...

Could I beg you to run some errands for a poor old hermit?

passages.title: Seeing Where Your Loyalties Lie
passages.text:
Thar be just one thing...

Yancey hears things. A few o' me hearties were pretty deep in their cups when they told me about some <race> <class> that came a-rollin' through the Southern Command lookin' for charts and orders. Even ran a couple o' good pirates through, <he/she> did.

Like I said, they were up to their eyeballs in grog, but still... a buccaneer's gotta trust his ears. So I've just got one small task for ye, one sent down from Firallon hisself...

Bring me the head of Fleet Master Seahorn.

passages.title: Seeing Where Your Loyalties Lie
passages.text: Firallon special-ordered this one himself.  Said the tauren's too much of a risk.

passages.title: Seeing Where Your Loyalties Lie
passages.text:
Well blow me down!  Now there's something ya don't see too often.

<Yancey reaches out and shakes your hand.>

Welcome aboard, <name>.  Plunder and booty await ye.

passages.title: Your First Day as a Pirate
passages.text:
Ye may be a slayer of Fleet Masters, but rules is rules and orders is orders. And MY orders say that all new pirates start out as swabbies. It's the rule.

You're to be working for Captain Keelhaul, the commander of the Riptide. It's the westernmost ship in the fleet, which is parked south of the tip o' the cape.

Find him in his captain's chambers, and bring yer papers.

passages.title: Your First Day as a Pirate
passages.text: I trust y'got yer papers, swabbie.  I'd hate t'send ye all the way back to Yancey.

passages.title: Your First Day as a Pirate
passages.text:
Yes... yes... I see... well, everything appears to be in order.

Slayer of the great Seahorn, eh?  That doesn't matter on MY ship.  Only thing you're gonna be slaying is deck stains.  Grab a mop.

passages.title: The Bane of Many A Pirate
passages.text:
Gum disease. It's a real problem, <race>.

I know you're new and all, and probably haven't ever needed your gums cut, but the rest of us pirates have to deal with a little thing called SCURVY. It's why we keep so many limes around here.

Well... we used to keep limes around here. Someone made off with our last shipment, but they can't have gone far - maybe to the nearby islands? Bring them back, and maybe I'll see what I can do to get you promoted from swabbie.

passages.title: The Bane of Many A Pirate
passages.text: I've seen too many good men die to such a preventable disease, <race>.  We need those limes.

passages.title: The Bane of Many A Pirate
passages.text: I'll distribute these right away, <race>.  And I'll see what I can do to put in the good word for you.

passages.title: Cannonball Swim
passages.text:
Help out a fellow swabbie?

Keelhaul asked me to gather up some cannonballs at the bottom of the ocean. Let me tell you why this doesn't work for me.

- One: I have tiny arms. Look at them! Do you really think I can pick up a cannonball, even underwater?

- Two: I have a weak respiratory system. I start to white out after holding my breath for more than ten seconds.

- Three: There are sharks.

You gotta help me, <name>! I've been demoted as far as I can... I don't want to see what comes next!

passages.title: Cannonball Swim
passages.text: I wasn't always a swabbie, you know.

passages.title: Cannonball Swim
passages.text: Thanks, <name>.  I'd been hearing whispers about "Pretty Boy" and a "boo-box".  I don't think I want to go in the boo-box.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Camouflage
passages.text:
We're gonna need some supplies before we take out the Blackrock army and save Redridge. That's where you come in, rookie.

Keeshan put me in charge of getting camouflage together for the Bravo Company field kit. What I need you to do is head south and do a little "gardening." There are two parts to this little adventure that you should know about: (1) Leaves and (2) Fox poop. We need 'em both.

What did you think camo was made of?

Head south and gather what I asked for, <pal/lady>.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Camouflage
passages.text: Leaves and poop - that's what I need.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Camouflage
passages.text: Nice job, rookie. I'm gonna go ahead and put the camo in the box. We should be ready soon.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Chloroform
passages.text:
The first part of this mission is all covert ops, <name>. To that end, we need to be able to incapacitate the enemy without making any sounds. To do that we're going to need chloroform.

The muckdwellers at the bottom of Lake Everstill hold chloroform in their glands. I'm going to need you to go underwater and recover muckdweller glands. Think you can handle it?

Come back to me once you've recovered enough glands.

Where's the lake you ask? Open your eyes, dummy. Directly west.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Chloroform
passages.text: Did you recover the glands?

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Chloroform
passages.text: Perfect. Those orcs won't know what hit 'em - literally. I'll need a few minutes to get these in working order and then I'll put them in the Bravo Company field kit.

passages.title: Hunting the Hunters
passages.text:
Just south of here on the Lakeridge Highway are a group of Blackrock orcs that stalk the forests under cover of darkness and ambush the uninitiated. That group is the first line of defense for the Blackrock army. They're scouts, reporting everything they see back to their central command. They need to be taken OUT or our mission here could be compromised.

Head south and kill every Blackrock hunter that you see.

passages.title: Hunting the Hunters
passages.text: Great work, <name>. We need to move quickly before they send for reinforcements.

passages.title: Point of Contact: Brubaker
passages.text:
Before we do a damned thing we need to get a field kit together. You'll help with that, <name>. There's also a matter of scouting. Thankfully for that we got some help from Stormwind. An old war buddy of mine, Brubaker, was sent here by SI:7 to scout around for us. You're to meet him in the field, just south of here.

Meet up with Brubaker and find out what he knows.

passages.title: Point of Contact: Brubaker
passages.text: Brubaker is dead. It looks like the orcs are attempting to send a message with this grisly display. Upon closer examination you notice something in Brubaker's pouch.

passages.title: Starvation Diet
passages.text:
The Creeping Ruin to the east is crawling with fully-grown Shadraspawn spiders. They're large enough to drag off an entire dwarf in the night, and you'll see evidence enough of that when you get there... bodies are cocooned all through the ruins.

They don't keep them alive for long, <name>, but they feed off the bodies for days. It's too late to save the victims, but we can't let those spiders grow fat and thrive. Make sure you get rid of those cocoons.

passages.title: Starvation Diet
passages.text: A grim task for sure, <name>, but it'll keep the spiders left alive from recovering. I thank you.

passages.title: The Night Watch
passages.text:
I'm afraid you're all I've got to help here, <name>. Stormwind's forces are so taxed by greater evils that they can't spare a single footman to protect Darkshire. It's up to me and the rest of the Night Watch to keep our homes safe.

There's more threats here than just wolves, unfortunately. Rotting horrors roam near Blind Mary's Haunt, on the southeast outskirts. If they're not kept in check, they'll be visiting our homes in the night.

Deal with the undead and report back to me for your bounty.

passages.title: The Night Watch
passages.text: I don't have authority to order you around, <name>. But at least think of the citizens here who'll be suffering if those undead are allowed to lurk.

passages.title: The Night Watch
passages.text: Splendid, <name>.  For your service to the people of Darkshire you shall be rewarded.

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
There is a poor, sad spirit, Blind Mary, who haunts an old farm house in the hills south of Darkshire.

Here, take this Spectral Comb and ask Blind Mary to comb her hair. Then bring back the comb and I will glean from it the Ghost Hair I'll need for the thread.

And take care, for dark things now lurk near that house...

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
<Sob> Oh please, don't look at me!  I tore out these eyes with my own hands, but I can still feel your gaze!

I'm hideous!  Hideous!  Please, look away!!

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
What is this?  A comb?  It's lovely!  And it glides through my hair as if it weren't the stiff, stringy horror that it is.

Oh, if only I had a mirror...

passages.title: Supplies from Darkshire
passages.text:
Oh, what is a poor old man to do? I need some supplies from Darkshire, but the village is so far away and I am so old and feeble...I would never make the trip.

Can you go to Darkshire and bring me back some ghost hair thread? You can get it from Madame Eva at her home on the Darkshire square.

passages.title: Supplies from Darkshire
passages.text: Ah, ghost hair thread is what you need, is it?  I'm afraid I have none in stock, but I can make some for you...if you can supply the ghost hair.

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text:
NO!!!!!

Take it, take this comb away from me!

I'm a monster, and no one will ever think me lovely again!

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text: I sense that you have seen Blind Mary.  You have my comb...?

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text: I can make a spool of ghost hair thread with this, and have a few strands to spare.  Here are some coins for those extra strands.

passages.title: Hard Falls
passages.text:
Stone Dragons bow only to strength. When we have punished them enough, they will bend back to our will.

I have sent many of my strongest giants onto the fields in the west. They will bring the drakes to the ground. You will see to it that they do not take wing again after they fall.

passages.title: Hard Falls
passages.text:
Not just fast it seems. You have some bite in you.

Well done, <class>.

passages.title: Fragile Values
passages.text:
It is now time to draw the Broodmother's attention. To do so, we will need a mallet that the troggs use when making offerings to her.

Seek out the Stone Trogg Beast Tamers that are attempting to tame basilisks in the southern portions of the Pale Roost. You will find a mallet on one of their corpses.

passages.title: Fragile Values
passages.text: Did you find a mallet?

passages.title: Fragile Values
passages.text:
Glorious.

Now we will deal a blow to the stone dragons that they will remember for the next hundred years.

passages.title: Zombie Juice
passages.text:
I need a bottle of a certain liquor - Zombie Juice. Tavernkeep Smitts at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire should have some.

And please hurry, <name>. These nights get cold, and I need that drink to put fire in my veins again!

passages.title: Zombie Juice
passages.text: You need some Zombie Juice, do you?  Hmm...that's some strong stuff - I don't usually get requests for it.

passages.title: Gather Rot Blossoms
passages.text:
If you bring me some rot blossoms then I can brew you up a batch of zombie juice.

rot blossoms grow in strange places. They tend to flourish on dead things, and Duskwood has its fair share of those!

I've seen a few of them growing at Tranquil Gardens Cemetery lately. Check near the graves... but mind the dead that are walking about near there.

passages.title: Gather Rot Blossoms
passages.text: Hi, <name>.  Do you have those rot blossoms for me yet?

passages.title: Gather Rot Blossoms
passages.text:
Good,  you got the rot blossoms.

I'll whip up the zombie juice... it's strong stuff, I warn you.

passages.title: Making Mutiny
passages.text:
Before returning to Booty Bay, you should do everything you can to weaken the Bloodsail Buccaneers. Unfortunately, even as captain, you're prohibited from killing other buccaneers in cold blood. Only a Fleet Master can do that.

You can, however, put mutineers to the sword... and mutiny can be awfully hard to disprove.

Speaking of which, those Bloodsail corsairs that hang out on the lowest level of the ships have been acting awfully suspicious...

passages.title: Making Mutiny
passages.text: The fewer Bloodsail Buccaneers that Booty Bay has to fight, the better.  However, it might be best to stop slaughtering your supposed allies before you draw suspicion to yourself.

passages.title: The Legend of Stalvan
passages.text:
I'm here because I received a letter from my brother Stalvan, who I haven't seen in years. On arriving here, I was told he was dead...

The entire town refuses to offer any further explanation. Any mention of his name is met with terror and suspicion. As if I didn't have enough of that myself!

I'm afraid of what will happen if my frustration and anger grows any further. I beg you, help me get to the bottom of this. Implore Clerk Daltry for any information he may have on my brother.

passages.title: The Legend of Stalvan
passages.text: Can I help you?

passages.title: The Stolen Letters
passages.text:
You want to know about Stalvan...

You're not the first, you know. We get outsiders coming through asking about him every so often. Always outsiders. Everyone who lives here knows better.

You're out of luck, anyway. I'm missing half the archives. Feral worgen broke into the town hall not a few nights ago and tore the place to shreds.

The documents you'll want are probably strewn all across Brightwood Grove by now, deep in the woods to the west. Not worth it if you ask me.

passages.title: The Stolen Letters
passages.text: Look, sir, I really don't want any trouble...

passages.title: The Stolen Letters
passages.text:
By the Light... you actually went and got it?

I'm shocked. I suppose I owe you thanks for returning it to the archives.

passages.title: Detonation
passages.text:
Those explosives you planted were high yield, <name>. When I push this button on the Bravo Company field kit, that whole valley is gonna be consumed by a massive fireball of death.

You know, I think you should do the honors. You did all the hard work, after all.

Ready?

passages.title: Detonation
passages.text: Did you see those orcs explode? THAT'S HOW WE DO IT IN BRAVO COMPANY! Now to clean up the rest of these jackasses.

passages.title: In A Dark Corner
passages.text:
If you're that serious about this, I'll help you, <name>. I know where the other documents must be. I'm just too terrified to do anything about it.

There's only a few places that those horrible Nightbane beasts gather when they're not prowling the forest. One of them's the Rotting Orchard to the south. They use the buildings there as their dens, so if they haven't just eaten the other documents, you might find one there... but you'll have to search their lairs thoroughly, I wager.

passages.title: In A Dark Corner
passages.text: You're back in one piece, I see.

passages.title: In A Dark Corner
passages.text:
This was all you found?

That's bad news, I'm afraid...

passages.title: Roland's Doom
passages.text:
This isn't all of it...

You should let it go, <name>. The only place left to look is Roland's Doom. That's the mine south of town, and the largest lair of worgen in Duskwood. Nobody in Darkshire has ever made it back from that place alive. In fact, some of the records I have here imply that's where the monsters first came from... who knows what evil's lurking in there?

Please, <name>, just give it up. Let's just forget about this whole thing, and never speak of it again.

passages.title: Roland's Doom
passages.text: I told you, <name>, it's not worth pursuing...

passages.title: Roland's Doom
passages.text:
You actually went and got it?!

I don't know whether to call you brave or insane. But once again, my archives thank you.

passages.title: The Fate of Stalvan Mistmantle
passages.text:
You've recovered everything. Everything except the last page...

...which I've got right here. Don't look at me like that. You'll understand when you read it. Some even say it's cursed, you know. In fact, I was relieved when the worgen broke in and made off with these!

Take it. Take all of it, in fact. I thank you for recovering my archives, but I don't want anything to do with this ever again. Please, just leave me be.

passages.title: The Fate of Stalvan Mistmantle
passages.text: You're back! Did you find anything about my brother?

passages.title: The Fate of Stalvan Mistmantle
passages.text:
I can't thank you enough... I had hoped for this to be a joyous reunion, but the more I learn, the less glad I am to have asked.

But I must know.

passages.title: Clawing at the Truth
passages.text:
This can't be. My brother was strong-willed, but such vileness... such sickness and violent, bloody evil...

<Tobias brings a hand to his face, averting his gaze.>

I must have answers. I need to know how I got that letter. I need to know if Stalvan really did this.

I need to know why...

Take my ring, <name>. Bring it to Madame Eva. That woman is a follower of old arts and makes no secret of it... call it madness, but I'll try anything at this point.

passages.title: Clawing at the Truth
passages.text: What dark whispers guide you to my door, <class>?

passages.title: Clawing at the Truth
passages.text: How interesting. It's been quite a while since I've seen such a ring...

passages.title: REUSE - BREADCRUMB
passages.text:
This can't be. My brother was strong-willed, but such vileness... such sickness and violent, bloody evil...

<Tobias brings a hand to his face, averting his gaze.>I must have answers. I need to know how I got that letter. I need to know if Stalvan really did this.

I need to know why...

Take my ring, <name>. Bring it to Madame Eva. That woman is a follower of old arts and makes no secret of it... call it madness, but I'll try anything at this point.

passages.title: Mistmantle's Revenge
passages.text:
I'm afraid I cannot give Tobias the answers he seeks. But I can help you find the only person who can...

Stalvan Mistmantle.

Take the ring into the woods to the north, to Manor Mistmantle, where Stalvan's body was buried. Enter, and hold the ring before you. Let the waning moon pour its light through the ring, and the spirits will answer your call.

Take heed, <name>. The questions of the living can offer more comfort than the answers of the dead.

passages.title: Mistmantle's Revenge
passages.text:
Master Harris may have been right. I would have been better to leave the past behind.

I've got a new life now. Whether it's that of a monster or a man is up to me.

As for you, I cannot thank you enough for your assistance, regardless of the outcome. Please, take this with my thanks.

passages.title: The Value of Trust
Ghoulish Effigy
passages.text:
Out here on the outskirts of town, it's a wonder the walking dead haven't eaten me! In fact, just yesterday a pack of ghouls was pounding on the walls of my tower!

I want to make an effigy - a kind of "scarecrow" for ghouls. To do that I need some ghoul ribs. You can find plenty of them on the fetid corpses wandering Manor Mistmantle's grounds, north of Darkshire...

Get the ribs for me, and I will repay you with some coin.

passages.title: Ghoulish Effigy
passages.text: I'm sure you could find plenty of ribs in Raven Hill as well, but you might not want to wander so far at night...

passages.title: Ghoulish Effigy
passages.text: Ah, thanks.  These will do just the trick!

passages.title: Return to Revilgaz
passages.text:
Something is happening outside. Could the Bloodsail already be here?

You'd better get Revilgaz his doublerum. Quickly.

passages.title: Return to Revilgaz
passages.text: Guess who showed up while you were gone?

passages.title: Return to Revilgaz
passages.text:
<The Baron quickly empties his cup.>

AH!  Much better, <name>.  Now, let's get down to business.  I believe that you and I have a town to save.

passages.title: Ogre Thieves
passages.text:
A few weeks ago I was picking herbs far from my house, and a band of ogres attacked me! I ran, and I was forced to leave behind a crate of precious tools and herbs.

After they chased me off, the ogres swaggered back to the ogre mound in southern Duskwood. I'm sure my crate is somewhere near the mound.

Please, <name>, retrieve this crate for me for I miss it sorely.

passages.title: Ogre Thieves
passages.text: Do you have my crate?  If so, then please...give it to me quickly!

passages.title: Ogre Thieves
passages.text:
Thank the Nec-...well, thank YOU, <name>!  You have more than earned your reward.

Aha!  Happy!  Happy nights ahead!!

passages.title: Note to the Mayor
passages.text:
Take this note to Ello Ebonlocke, the Mayor of Darkshire.

He and I are old friends...and when he reads it and discovers what you did for me...I'm sure he'll be just as happy as I am! Hahahaha!

passages.title: Note to the Mayor
passages.text: A letter? What's this all about?

passages.title: Note to the Mayor
passages.text:
<Ello looks at the letter, and immediately pales.>

You fool! You've doomed us all!

passages.title: Look To The Stars
passages.text:
My gnomish friend, Cog, has promised to help me build a device which will let me peer towards the stars. According to Cog's blueprint, what I need first is a way to reflect light.

I remember a woman by the name of Mary who became well known around these parts for always carrying a looking glass. Perhaps you can track Mary down and see if she might lend us a reflective surface for this project? I believe she once resided in southern Duskwood. . .

passages.title: Look To The Stars
passages.text: Why yes, I used to own a looking glass.

passages.title: The Insane Ghoul
passages.text: The looking glass was one of my finest treasures until. . .the incident. After that happened, I discarded it behind the barn. There was an insane ghoul who used to roam back there. Perhaps he picked it up. Rumor has it the devilish beast resides in the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery.

passages.title: The Insane Ghoul
passages.text: I showed Cog the beginnings of our star-viewing machine.  He was impressed.  Did you happen to find a reflective device?

passages.title: The Insane Ghoul
passages.text: Most superb!  This will work perfectly.  Many thanks!

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Darkness seems drawn inexorably to Duskwood. Master Carevin's quest is the expulsion of evil and heresy. Through our efforts are the people of Darkshire kept safe.

You believe yourself worthy to join us?

I once thought as you. Disillusioned by the complacency of the Watch, I joined Master Carevin. If you wish to prove yourself, it will not be through words.

Test your skills against the Nightbane worgen in Brightwood Grove. We'll see if you have what it takes to hunt these monsters.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text: Impressive, <name>. It would seem that you are capable enough to handle yourself. Perhaps a more suitable challenge could be found for one of your abilities.

passages.title: The Rotting Orchard
passages.text:
The worgen infestation stretches further than Brightwood Grove. To the south, on the very edges of Darkshire itself, the Rotting Orchard is host to even more of the savage beasts.

The worgen there are more cunning, <name>, but just as savage and evil. They conjure foul shadows to tear their enemies apart from a distance. Go to the Rotting Orchard, and slay the Shadow Weavers to keep the town safe!

passages.title: The Rotting Orchard
passages.text: Back so soon, <name>? I hope you haven't come to tell me you've given up.

passages.title: The Rotting Orchard
passages.text:
You performed well against the Shadow Weavers, <name>. But even now, years after their first arrival, there seem to be so many to replace the ones we kill.

I will put my faith in Master Carevin. No doubt he will get to the bottom of the problem.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Here you go, <name>. Bring this message to Master Carevin.

<He quickly removes a piece of faded parchment and offers it to you.>

A few more like you, and we will outnumber the Night Watch! Perhaps then we could complete the work that we few carry on today.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text: Yes, what is it? Make it quick, I've pressing matters to attend to.

passages.title: Worgen in the Woods
passages.text:
Excuse me for my cold reception, <name>, but as I'm sure you can tell, I am an extremely busy man. I see that you have impressed Calor--and I assure you, that is no small feat--and that he has given his recommendation.

There are unsavory types afoot, <name>, and we can use the help of all who have proven themselves. We battle against demons, the undead, and those who would provide them aid. Be vigilant, be wary, and trust none who would not give aid to our cause.

Glory under the Light.

passages.title: Shadowhide Extinction
passages.text:
Now that every Blackrock orc south of Lake Everstill is nothing more than ash and cinder, we can turn our attention to the Shadowhide gnoll army of Galardell Valley, directly north of here.

I want you to head out there and kill 'em all, <name>! Initiate Operation: Extinction, soldier. For Bravo Company and for the Alliance!

passages.title: Shadowhide Extinction
passages.text: We're closing in on the Blackrock high command. There's nowhere left for those dogs to run.

passages.title: The Dark Tower
passages.text:
We got lucky with some vital intelligence from the locals of this valley. Those two behind us, the Ranthals, have informed me that the gnolls in Galardell Valley are being controlled by a powerful magus in the tower of Ilgalar. The problem is that the tower is sealed by a magical force field.

The first thing we need to do is get the key that will get you inside. The gnoll general, Fangore, has your ticket inside. Kill General Fangore and get the key.

I'll be in touch.

passages.title: The Dark Tower
passages.text: I hear you loud and clear, <name>.

passages.title: The Dark Tower
passages.text:
<Keeshan comes in over the Bravo Company field kit.>

Now that the easy part is over, it's time for phase two.

passages.title: The Grand Magus Doane
passages.text:
<The Bravo Company field kit vibrates.>

Good work, kid. I've got some vital intel for you. The magus in the tower is a human named Doane. Damned traitor is working for the Blackrock orcs. I want him dead.

Use the key of Ilgalar and get inside that tower. Work your way to the top and show Doane what Bravo Company does with traitors.

Rendezvous back at Shalewind Canyon when the deed is done.

Keeshan, over and out.

passages.title: The Grand Magus Doane
passages.text: I hear you loud and clear, <name>.

passages.title: The Grand Magus Doane
passages.text:
He teleported away? Mentioned Darkblaze? What the hell is going on here.

Looks like it's time to strap in and finish this nonsense.

passages.title: The Call of Kalimdor
passages.text:
Say, you haven't seen a fish about this long? Short fins? Responds to the name Steve? He's blue?

Never mind, I'll keep looking.

Actually... there was another reason I came here to Booty Bay. Boss Krog, over in Dustwallow, is looking for new blood. Someone to help us Stonemaul from getting overrun. You look strong enough.

Wait on the edge of the pier for the next ship, then ride to Ratchet. Gazlowe should be able to help you from there.

Steve? Steve!

passages.title: The Call of Kalimdor
passages.text: Yeah?  What can I do for ya?

passages.title: Seeking Seahorn
passages.text:
When the Brashtide pulled in, Seahorn grabbed the nearest weapon he could find and jumped off the ledge here. You'll find him down below, probably pounding new holes into those worgen's skulls.

Help him out down there. I can handle the motivation from up here.

passages.title: Seeking Seahorn
passages.text: I should have known these Brashtide were alive and up to no good.  I'd written them off years ago.

passages.title: Turning the Brashtide
passages.text:
The Brashtide are everywhere! The Baron's Booty Bay Bruisers are no match for their sheer numbers, I'm afraid.

While you're down here in the fray, why don't you help me get rid of a few of them?

When you're done, don't bother coming back here. I'll probably be pretty busy.

passages.title: Turning the Brashtide
passages.text: We need to keep moving, <name>.  Booty Bay won't hold out for much longer.

passages.title: The Damsel's (Bad) Luck
passages.text:
I heard that this ship here is the Damsel's Luck. Didn't you used to be the captain of that thing? You must know your way around it, then.

The Brashtide are our main concern, but we still don't want to take an unnecessary pummeling from those cannons of theirs. Grab this rope behind me and take out some of those angry-looking corsairs. Check in with the Baron when you're done.

passages.title: The Damsel's (Bad) Luck
passages.text:
Attacking your former crewmen...

You really have grown into a real pirate, <name>!

passages.title: Endgame
passages.text:
We need to get rid of that flying gunship if our people have any chance of escaping.

Here's the plan. Keel Harbor had its share of rebel sympathizers in the old days. I've managed to round up a hefty amount of incendiary explosives from one of our storehouses.

We're going to hit the enemy with a force small enough to fly undetected. The night elf hippogryphs should do the trick.

Tobias will give you the signal when we're ready to go.

passages.title: Endgame
passages.text: The only risks worth taking are the ones that lead to victories worth having.

passages.title: Endgame
passages.text: We did it, <name>.  We've started the evacuation.  If we leave soon we'll leave the Forsaken fleet in the dust.

passages.title: A Deadly Vine
passages.text:
I need large amounts of corpseweed for Master Harris's concoctions. It's difficult to obtain, but we can't let our supply dwindle.

corpseweed is tough stuff to tangle with... the plant will get you before you get it, if you're not careful! But if you'd like to help out, I'll eagerly pay you for any you gather yourself.

You'll find plenty of it all over the Yorgen Stead to the southeast.

passages.title: A Deadly Vine
passages.text: Do you have the corpseweed?

passages.title: A Deadly Vine
passages.text: I thank you, <class>... and I'm sure the worgen that may be returned to sanity with the potion this will make would thank you too.

passages.title: The Stone Throne
passages.text:
I am returning to my throne. I've no desire to see any more of these Earthen Ring, but you remain welcome here, <race>. If you wish to help us rebuild our realm, perhaps we can help you in return.

All things in time.

passages.title: The Stone Throne
passages.text: You returned. This is good. The Stone Lords have been asking after you.

passages.title: Off to the Bank
passages.text:
Yo, baby. Wassup? You ready for the party?

No?! You know I love you, so I don't know how to say this, but check it... I think you need to swing into town to buy a new outfit for the party.

Don't look at me like that... you want to look gooood, right? Don't you want to look super fine for me? I am your contractually-obligated boyfriend after all!

Swing by the bank first and pull out plenty of macaroons. You don't want to buy any of that cheap stuff!

passages.title: Off to the Bank
passages.text:
Oh, it's you, ma'am! Sorry, I didn't recognize you at first with all of these commoners milling about.

You people cool your heels! <name> is here!

Here are your macaroons, ma'am. Come back anytime if you need more.

passages.title: Off to the Bank
passages.text:
Hi, babe. Are you ready for the party?

No?! You know I love you, right? I think you need to swing into town and buy a new outfit for the party.

Don't look at me like that... you want to look your best? Don't you want to look good for me? I am your contractually-obligated girlfriend after all!

Make sure you swing by the bank first and pull out plenty of macaroons. Don't buy any of that cheap stuff!

passages.title: Off to the Bank
passages.text:
Oh, it's you, sir! Sorry, I didn't recognize you at first with all of these commoners milling about.

You people cool your heels! <name> is here!

Here are your macaroons, sir. Come back anytime if you need more.

passages.title: Showdown at Stonewatch
passages.text:
Only the Blackrock high command remains, <name>. They're all holed up in Stonewatch Keep, directly south of our position here at Keeshan's Post. I want you and the rest of Bravo Company to enter Stonewatch and put an end to the Blackrock orc invasion.

<name>, no survivors.

passages.title: Showdown at Stonewatch
passages.text: This doesn't look good.

passages.title: Showdown at Stonewatch
passages.text:
<The Bravo Company field kit beeps loudly.>

Come in, <name>. Are you there? If you can hear me: Blackrock has the upper hand. I repeat. Blackrock has the upper hand. GET BRAVO COMPANY OUT OF TH...

passages.title: A Bit of Privacy
The Yorgen Worgen
passages.text:
My kinsmen at Raven Hill are concerned with curing the feral worgen in these forests. The condition itself cannot be lifted, but sanity can be restored to those not too far gone.

While most here have proven beyond help, we keep an eye out for those that retain vestiges of their minds... attachments to their old lives.

I've seen a lone worgen lurking the Yorgen Farmstead, digging in a pile of dirt between the buildings...could you check out that pile and see if he's left anything?

passages.title: The Yorgen Worgen
passages.text: Did you go look yet?

passages.title: The Yorgen Worgen
passages.text:
Sounds like a close call! But he ran off without harming you further...

He might be still fighting it. Master Harris must know!

passages.title: Breadcrumb to Badlands
Delivery to Master Harris
passages.text:
Master Harris will want to know of this immediately.

Here, take this package of corpseweed down the road to the camp at Raven Hill. Tell him what we saw at the Yorgen Stead.

passages.title: Delivery to Master Harris
passages.text: What brings you out this way, my good sir?

passages.title: Delivery to Master Harris
passages.text:
Welcome to our humble camp. I wouldn't call it pleasant, but it's at least somewhat private.

Beg your pardon? A worgen at the farm?

passages.title: The Jitters-Bugs
passages.text:
M-Master Harris requires many reagents for his serums. He has me gather them for him.

Most of it's not so bad... I mean, the corpseweed is pretty bad, but it's not as bad as the widow venom. Have you seen the widows around here? The hatchlings are the size of a man. Even with a gun, I can't stand to go out hunting them!

It's just too terrifying. If you'll go do it for me, I'll gladly pay you! Just bring me back some widow venom! You'll find them all in the woods to the east, just north of the road.

passages.title: The Jitters-Bugs
passages.text: Did you get it? Please tell me you got it...

passages.title: The Jitters-Bugs
passages.text:
Oh thank you, thank you! You've saved me from having to go out in the woods with those awful things!

At least for a day, that is...

passages.title: Buried Below
passages.text:
<You attach the arch to the rod, and the artifact is nearly complete. A large gap still sits at the center of the holy symbol's head.>

<Once again you feel it tug your arm, urging you towards the hole in the wall and the winding tunnel ahead. The last piece must be through there.>

passages.title: Buried Below
passages.text: <In the darkest depths of this earthen tunnel, you spy the faintest gleam. The last piece is found!>

passages.title: The Fate of Morbent Fel
passages.text:
Before I was lost to the woods, the last thing I remember is Morbent Fel. He was a vile necromancer, and the reason this land swarms with so many vile undead.

I asked an adventurer to help me put an end to him. I thought they did! But Sister Elsington tells me the land still crawls with ghouls and spectres ripped from the grave.

Morbent Fel should have breathed his last in the house on Forlorn Rowe, north of Raven Hill Cemetery. Go there and see what's become of him...

passages.title: The Fate of Morbent Fel
passages.text: What did you find?

passages.title: The Fate of Morbent Fel
passages.text: His clothes and bloodstains? If it's not tricks, it's something worse...

passages.title: The Lurking Lich
passages.text:
The others here share my suspicion. Morbent Fel lives on in undeath...and may be even more powerful than before. A necromancer was struck down, but a lich may have risen in his place. And now he continues to ruin this land.

I remember Duskwood before all this, <name>. I remember bright skies and peaceful woods. This can't stand! Morbent Fel must be stopped for good.

Speak to Sister Elsington. Her vision might guide you to where Morbent Fel is, and how he can be defeated.

passages.title: The Lurking Lich
passages.text: It's heartening to see one so recently recovered be so concerned with the plight of others. Sven spares himself suffering by not dwelling on his own misfortune.

passages.title: Guided by the Light
passages.text:
Sven is correct. I can feel the presence of a powerful evil deep beneath the Raven Hill Cemetery. Evil lurks in its catacombs, and Morbent Fel must be the source.

You will need the power of the Light to strike him down, <name>. Sven told me the heroes who first slew Morbent Fel wielded an artifact of lightforged iron, imbued with holy power. That artifact is still here!

I can feel it as well, a glimmer of light amidst the darkness. Search Raven Hill for it, and let the Light guide you through it.

passages.title: Guided by the Light
passages.text: <Buried in the cold dirt, you find a brilliant metal shaft. But there are holes where pieces of the artifact are clearly missing.>

passages.title: Triumphant Return
passages.text:
Return to Lakeshire and let Solomon know that the Blackrock invasion has been stopped. Make sure he understands the cost at which our freedom came - that we lost five of our finest heroes to save Redridge and ultimately, Stormwind.

You are the last surviving member of Bravo Company, <name>. It is up to you to keep its legacy alive.

Dismissed.

passages.title: Triumphant Return
passages.text:
They will never be forgotten, <name>. What you and the rest of Bravo Company sacrificed in order to save Redridge will be a tale told for ages to come.

While I can in no way make up for the loss of your friends, I feel that you must be rewarded for such a heroic deed. These are Keeshan's possessions - the only things we found when we dredged the lake for his body. Troteman has informed me that Keeshan would have wanted you to take something as the lone surviving member of Bravo Company. Remember them, <name>!

passages.title: The Embalmer's Revenge
passages.text:
You're not the first fool to be manipulated by Abercrombie! That doddering old man is known as The Embalmer to us. He's a vile necromancer and a blight upon this town.

And now, sewn together and given life by the very materials you brought him, his horrible creation approaches!

That hideous creature will be upon us in mere moments! If you have any heart, <name>, you'll help the Night Watch drive off the abomination and save our town!

passages.title: The Embalmer's Revenge
passages.text: Don't just stand there! He's right outside! By the light, man, do something!

passages.title: The Embalmer's Revenge
passages.text:
Thank the Light, he's gone...

I'll say you've made amends by helping save the lives of those here, <name>.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Duskwood!
passages.text:
<name>, the citizens of Duskwood are in dire need of your assistance! I have here a letter from Commander Althea Ebonlocke, leader of the Night Watch, pleading for help.

To reach Darkshire you should travel across the bridge located in the southwest corner of Redridge. Once you cross the bridge you will be in Duskwood. Then you just follow the road to Darkshire. Beware of the savage beasts that stalk the countryside!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Duskwood!
passages.text:
You are the help that we requested?

<Althea sighs.>

I suppose you will have to do.

passages.title: Water Elementals
passages.text:
I arrived in Stranglethorn to study a feature known as the Altar of Naias, but made the unfortunate choice of denying Colonel Kurzen's advances, which earned me several years in that cage. Now that I'm out, I figure I might as well continue with my original studies.

The altar is on an island to the west, south of Zul'Kunda. Gather some of the bracers from the island's water elementals.

Oh, and you can use this device when you're finished. No need to make you walk all the way back here.

passages.title: Water Elementals
passages.text: Yes, <name>?

passages.title: Water Elementals
passages.text: These will do for my purposes.  Though we can't activate the altar with bracers alone...

passages.title: Bad Medicine
passages.text:
I have a feeling that Kurzen's Medicine Men are distributing more than just medicine. Kurzen needs some way to quelch insubordination, and an elixir under the guise of "medicine" would be the perfect way to do that.

We need those remedies for research. Search the Kurzen Compound to the southeast - his medicine men and jungle fighters should carry the remedies on their bodies.

passages.title: Bad Medicine
passages.text: I'm a little bit of an alchemist in my spare time, you know.

passages.title: Bad Medicine
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  Now, let's see what they've got in this elixir of theirs...

passages.title: Control Sample
passages.text:
<Brother Nimetz analyzes the samples you've given him.>

This... this is just basilisk blood!

No, it's mostly basilisk blood. They've added something to it though. I'll need a control sample to perform a proper comparison.

They most likely obtained the blood from the crystal spine basilisks, found to the east of their compound. Bring me back some pure samples, and I'll have this elixir figured out.

passages.title: Control Sample
passages.text: There's something not quite healthy about this elixir, <name>.  Even though I haven't completed my analysis, I can sense it.

passages.title: Control Sample
passages.text: This will do.  Please hold on for a moment while I test this out.

passages.title: Krazek's Cookery
passages.text:
I do most of the cooking at the camp. It used to be a lot of work, until I bought a mechanical cooking pot from a goblin merchant. The pot is a wonder! It saved me countless hours...until it broke!

Can you take the pot back to the goblin for me so he can fix it? His name is Krazek. Last I heard, he was staying with Nesingwary in the hunters' camp just to the south.

passages.title: Krazek's Cookery
passages.text: Hello!  You brought me something?

passages.title: Krazek's Cookery
passages.text:
Oh I see, it's a Krazek's Crock Pot!  An ingenious piece of work, but it can break a spring or throw a gear now and then.  Let me see what's wrong with this one...

Aha!  Its steam charger is rusted out, it has a cracked knuckle-gasket and its fobulator is missing teeth.  I'm surprised the pot could even boil a turnip in this state!

Can I fix it?  Of course I can fix it!

But there's a price.  Oh yes, there is always a price...

passages.title: Bloodscalp Insight
passages.text:
I never got to properly thank you for saving me.

Thank you, <name>.

I'm still a little fatigued from my captivity, so I thought you might help me with my studies. As a shaman of the Wildhammer clan, I'm very interested in the shamanic practices of the Bloodscalp tribe.

Their magic seems to have diverged in an interesting direction. If I had one of the totems that their shaman use, I could begin my studies. You'll find them at the Bal'lal ruins, on the coast to the southwest.

passages.title: Bloodscalp Insight
passages.text: Beware: they may put up a fight.

passages.title: Bloodscalp Insight
passages.text:
<Berrin studies the inscriptions on the totem.>

I think I can read this text... Fascinating!

Tsul'kalu, Mahamba, Pogeyan... what are these names?

passages.title: A Nose for This Sort of Thing
passages.text:
<Osborn looks at the skull again.>

In life, he was strong, powerful, a lord among trolls. With our help, he can be a lord once more.

The Bloodscalp scavengers that wander the ruins to the southwest hoard magical fetishes that can help us. They hide these artifacts under the ground. Use your hatchling to find these artifacts, <name>... then bring them here.

passages.title: A Nose for This Sort of Thing
passages.text: How many did you find?

passages.title: A Nose for This Sort of Thing
passages.text:
These will provide a bit of... what's the troll word?  Voodoo?  Juju?  Tiklabang?

It doesn't matter.  If we're going to re-build a troll, we need troll magic, and these fetishes are full of it.

passages.title: At the Stonemother's Call
passages.text: It is time. The Stonemother will speak with you. You can find her throne in northern Deepholm, above the Scoured Reach.

passages.title: At the Stonemother's Call
passages.text:
So you've come.

Fleshlings just like you killed my daughter... my only daughter. With no provocation.

Not sated at stripping me of my family, more of you flocked to Deathwing to serve him in ravaging my home.

You're quite arrogant to come before me asking for MY help. I'm tempted to crush you where you stand.

passages.title: The Halls of the Dead
passages.text:
<In front of you, the bare earth slopes down towards the dark entrance to the crypts.>

<You can feel the tug of the lightforged artifact urging you towards it. Perhaps the other piece is down there?>

passages.title: The Halls of the Dead
passages.text: <In the dirt of this alcove, your eye catches the shine of brilliant metal. You've found another piece of the artifact!>

passages.title: Morbent's Bane
passages.text:
<The pieces fit, and the holy artifact is restored, gleaming with sacred light. This should let you defeat Morbent Fel's dark magic.>

<Further down the tunnel, away from the direction you came from, a heinous cackle rings out. It's the clattering laugh of a lich. Morbent Fel is just ahead!>

passages.title: Morbent's Bane
passages.text:
May the disgusting monster stay dead this time!

I'll head down there and scatter his remains to ash myself, <name>. You've done a great thing; perhaps in time Duskwood can return to its former peaceful state.

passages.title: Keep Them off the Front
passages.text:
Oh good, you brought another catapult with you! Clay might be older than dirt, but he makes a mean war machine.

Well, you didn't bring it all the way out here for your health, flesh bag. Get in one of those things and bombard the fungal terrors and reinforcements streaming out of Needlerock Slag.

We have to keep them off the front!

passages.title: Keep Them off the Front
passages.text: Get back in a catapult and put those things back in the ground. The line's barely holding!

passages.title: Keep Them off the Front
passages.text: That's a great start, <name>, but we're going to need you to fly over into the town and stir up some trouble.

passages.title: Nessa Shadowsong
passages.text:
A friend of mine, Nessa Shadowsong, is a fishing merchant in Rut'theran Village. She needs a parcel taken to Darkshore, and is looking for someone to help her.

If you're interested, then to reach Nessa you must take the portal in Darnassus to Rut'theran Village. You will find the portal west of the Temple Gardens.

passages.title: The Bounty of Teldrassil
passages.text:
The fishermen of Rut'theran village do very well, for the fish here are extremely large and abundant. I would like to compare the bounty here with that of the mainland.

I have a collection of fish bones and scales that I would like taken to a colleague of mine in Darkshore. His name is Laird, he is a fish vendor in the village of Auberdine.

Bring my collection to our hippogryph master, Vesprystus, and speak to him about traveling to Auberdine.

passages.title: Return to Nessa
passages.text:
I must send a response to Nessa. She'll be very interested to know how different the fish here are from those along Teldrassil's coastline. We can only guess the cause, but it is my suspicion that the world tree itself is affecting the wildlife around it!

Please, take this response to Nessa. If you wish to take a hippogryph back to Rut'theran then speak with the hippogryph master Caylais Moonfeather. If you wish to take the ferry, then one regularly departs from the dock to the northwest.

passages.title: Cry For The Moon
passages.text:
I'm hopeful, but let's remain professional. It's business as usual for this one.

Into the guillotine he goes... and if the alchemy doesn't take, he won't be getting back out of it.

Jitters and I will attend to this. Please, just stand back and watch from a safe distance.

passages.title: Cry For The Moon
passages.text:
Success... Finally! I can't thank you enough for giving me the chance to work the cure myself.

Our new friend may be in need of some help as well. You might want to speak with him.

passages.title: Threat to the Kingdom
passages.text:
There is no doubt that the Defias pose a great threat to the kingdom, but we certainly cannot enter their hideout and hope that everything will work itself out. No, an assault against the Defias is going to take time and planning. I want you to leave the logistics to me. Our kingdom has other threats that must be dealt with immediately!

Travel east through Elwynn to Redridge and report to Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire. I will call for you when we are ready to attack the Defias.

passages.title: Threat to the Kingdom
passages.text: I heard about the Defias making a return. Terrible news. I wish I had better news, but it would appear that Lakeshire is under attack! We are losing citizens left and right. Our own guards are spread far too thin to handle the situation. We need a hero to step up!

passages.title: Reactivate the Constructs
passages.text:
We sent a number of our war constructs north into Needlerock Slag, but none of them ever returned. We know that the stone trogg mystics have done something to them.

What we're concerned about is that the mystics will control and turn them against us, like they have with the fungal giants.

<name>, go into the stone trogg town and reactivate the constructs.

passages.title: Reactivate the Constructs
passages.text:
That was a nice bit of work, <name>.

With our constructs back up and running behind their main lines, it's only a matter of time now before we make the big push through and rescue the Stonefather.

passages.title: A New Low
passages.text:
You may notice that the Venture Company has completely clear-cut all the trees around their Base Camp to the east. Not one to miss out an opportunity for profit, their foreman has enslaved druids, and is forcing them to re-grow the forest so they can chop it down again!

Personally, I find this abhorrent, and not just because I didn't think of it first.

Release a few of these druids from their captors. I'm sure they'll appreciate it.

passages.title: Figuring out how to make quests
passages.text: Whee! You get to make a breadcrumb quest! Now figure out what to do next.

passages.title: To Catch a Dragon
passages.text:
Having a dragon guard the fragment was a smart move on the enemy's part. They can keep moving its location any time we get close to it.

Catching Abyssion will be extremely difficult, but I have a plan that might help.

The Twilight's Hammer uses magical traps to bind stone drakes to the ground while they drain their energy.

If we can get our hands on one of these, we might be able to ground the Twilight Dragon for just long enough.

Go east of here, to the Alabaster Shelf, and obtain a trap.

passages.title: To Catch a Dragon
passages.text: If the snares are good enough for stone drakes, they might work on Abyssion.

passages.title: To Catch a Dragon
passages.text: Let's see if the snare can ground something larger than a drake.

passages.title: Mind Control
passages.text:
Mind Vision is not enough, no.

Mind Control, much more powerful magic, yes.

Powerful magic needs powerful reagents, and troll brain is a powerful reagent.

Braddok in Zul'Mamwe, very smart, yes.

Head south, and check out the big brain on Braddok.

passages.title: Mind Control
passages.text: Extra-big spells need extra-big brains, yes.

passages.title: Mind Control
passages.text:
Hold on, next part is tough, yes.

Lots of chances to fail, yes.

But <name> and <name>'aka going to be reunited... yes they will.

passages.title: Soothing Spirits
passages.text:
This is a tragic land, with a history of violence and despair. While many of the dead roam in the flesh, some are simply lost souls, wandering in confusion.

They deserve to be put at ease.

Many of these souls gather at the Addle Stead to the south, appearing before travelers. Take this censer of holy incense. Sway it before the forlorn spirits, and let the offering of its gentle scent give them peace.

passages.title: Soothing Spirits
passages.text: You have brought peace to those who knew only misery, <name>. Be proud.

passages.title: The Cries of the Dead
passages.text:
Can you hear them, <name>? There's so many of them. They wander their graves, shuffling across the cold ground on rotting limbs.

The dead cry out in the still air. They suffer in their own flesh, forced from sleep! Every night I venture to the graveyard to put more of them to rest, but it's never enough.

Help me, <name>. Put the ghouls that swarm Raven Hill Cemetery out of their misery. Strike down as many as you can.

passages.title: The Cries of the Dead
passages.text: The cries grow softer for now. Light bless you, <name>.

passages.title: Zul'Mamwe Mambo
passages.text:
The Skullsplitters are an embarrassment to the troll empire. Their petty squabbles with the Bloodscalps have torn Northern Stranglethorn apart. Where tribes like the Darkspear and the Zandalari thrive, the Skullsplitters fight over ruins.

I have been authorized to issue rewards to mercenaries who are willing to deliver punishment to the Skullsplitters. I encourage you, and anyone you know, to travel east into Zul'Mamwe and cull their wayward tribe.

passages.title: Zul'Mamwe Mambo
passages.text: Zul'Mamwe, though ruined, is still a defensible stronghold.  Take heed, <race>.

passages.title: Zul'Mamwe Mambo
passages.text: As promised, your reward.  You do the troll nation proud.

passages.title: Muddied Waters
passages.text:
The elemental powers are strong here in the Highlands, <name>. It is why the Twilight's Hammer chose to build their stronghold here.

In the right hands, we can channel this energy into something productive... like a portal directly to Orgrimmar.

Northwest of here, at the Verrall River Delta, water elementals have been stirred up by the actions of our foes upstream. Destroy them and gather 5 whirlpool cores. You'll not only calm the river, you'll power up our portal.

passages.title: Muddied Waters
passages.text: I hope the fighting within the river wasn't too dangerous.

passages.title: Muddied Waters
passages.text:
These are perfect! The restless waters of that troubled river will now do much more than move silt or stone... They'll move you across continents.

Finish up the rest of your business here in Dragonmaw and then we should be able to proceed.

passages.title: Part of the Pack
passages.text:
I've been trying to keep my true self hidden away from the people of Darkshire... they seem to react poorly to worgen. There are more of us here, though, beyond the city.

The companions I first traveled here with search the woods for wild worgen. They believe some of them, ones with telltale signs, can still be returned to sanity.

I'm not quite ready to rejoin them. Please send word to Apprentice Fess at the crossroads west of town that I'll be staying in Darkshire a while longer.

passages.title: Part of the Pack
passages.text:
Tobias is staying in town still?

Master Harris warned him not to pursue his brother's fate. We all lead new lives now, after all. But the past is hard to let go of...

passages.title: Securing the Beach Head
passages.text:
Something troubles me, <name>. The Twilight dragons knew just where and when to strike our airfleet. It's as if they knew our plans.

Twilight spies cower within our midst!

I'm going to take one of our remaining ships back to Orgrimmar to roll some heads. I need you to stay behind and secure this front. The Dragonmaw shaman are powerful; I have asked them to open up a portal to Orgrimmar, and I need you to help.

So. Start helping!

passages.title: Securing the Beach Head
passages.text:
Your Warchief is decisive, <name>. He makes things happen. I like him.

Let's talk about this portal that he wants!

passages.title: Bear In Mind
passages.text:
I'm afraid that... well, I'm just plain afraid, but I'm also sorry to have to ask for another favor.

Master Harris needs brains. Bear brains. They're part of the serum apparently, or at least a proper substitute.

There's plenty of black bears in the woods to the west, and along the riverbank, but... I can't do it! I'm too terrified to go out there and face those huge things, even with a rifle. Please, let me pay you to bring back some!

passages.title: Bear In Mind
passages.text: Did you get them? Did you?

passages.title: Bear In Mind
passages.text:
Thank you! Oh, thank you. I never thought I'd be happy to smell those brains, but I am now that I didn't have to get them!

Here's your reward as promised...

passages.title: Cementing Our Victory
passages.text:
Our alliance with the Dragonmaw is secured, but this port is far from combat ready. These flimsy wooden walls are an embarrassment to the Warchief.

When water elementals carve their way through rock, as they have in the Verrall River, they create a peculiar kind of muck. It spreads easily and dries harder than the hardest stone. It's the perfect mortar for large-scale construction.

Go to the river delta northwest of here and collect some Verrall River muck. Even a little will go a long way.

passages.title: Cementing Our Victory
passages.text: Do you have the mud? Construction of the new walls has already begun!

passages.title: Cementing Our Victory
passages.text:
<Ornak allows the muck to drip from his fingertips.>

Now that's the stuff! I'll start mixing and diluting this with gravel and water. Just a few handfuls of this can enhance enough cement for an entire stone tower.

We've got big plans for this port, <name>. You'll see!

passages.title: You no take axe!
passages.text: <Name>, we have a problem! I've tracked down the demon-hound Magmadar to this clearing, but when we resting a band of kobolds took our battle axes! I need you to retrieve them, lest Magmadar catch us off guard! Hurry, he could awaken at any moment!

passages.title: Magmadar Must Die!
passages.text: There he is, <name>. The foolish beast fell asleep right out in the open! Good news for us, eh? Come, hero, we fight now! You can even have the honor of severing his head from his massive body. What's that? Too big for your bags? Why, carry it, of course! <Thrall grins.>

passages.title: Sprout No More
passages.text:
The stone trogg mystics are creating those fungal monstrosities from the giant mushrooms to the north.

I want you to take a war guardian to help deal with the giants and stone troggs. Make your way to the giant mushrooms and target them. I and my geomancers will sink them into the ground before the mystics have a chance to finish their ritual.

passages.title: Sprout No More
passages.text: They won't have any more of those fungal giants to throw against us!

passages.title: Fungal Monstrosities
passages.text: Grab yourself a war guardian, and destroy those fungal monstrosities while you're out there.

passages.title: Fungal Monstrosities
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. We've never had such a problem in Deepholm before the destruction of the World Pillar.

Your Earthen Ring must repair the damage before it's too late.

passages.title: The Weathered Grave
passages.text:
The weathered grave marker reads simply:

MORGAN LADIMORE

<Upon further examination, you notice that dirt over the grave has been recently disturbed, and that a good amount of the dirt seems to have been displaced...>

passages.title: The Weathered Grave
passages.text:
Morgan Ladimore?

Ahh, yes, of course. His was a long and sorrowful tale. I knew him, well, before he left for the war, but that was the last time I saw him. A noble and good man, he was, but he suffered a bad end.

Here, I should have something here that can tell the tale better than my own recollections...

passages.title: Morgan Ladimore
passages.text:
<He searches through the shelves and comes up with a leatherbound book.>

If you would like to know more, you might ask Althea, she's been the one to handle the... trouble... with him of late.

passages.title: Morgan Ladimore
passages.text:
Morgan Ladimore? Never heard of...

Oh, you mean Mor'Ladim! I guess you haven't heard the story?

Well, I'll give you the short version. A powerful undead calling itself Mor'Ladim has been wandering Duskwood. From what we've gathered, it appears to be the undead body of Morgan Ladimore, of whom you apparently know. He's been causing us all sorts of problems, attacking Watchmen on patrol and killing people.

<She sizes you up.>

You seem to be capable enough, maybe you could lay him to rest.

passages.title: The Daughter Who Lived
passages.text:
I should have told you this earlier...

How do I put this...

Morgan may have believed that his family was all dead, but, in fact, his daughter Sarah Ladimore is now a Watcher. She's always been troubled by the... circumstances... surrounding her father's death. Perhaps you could go to bring the news to her.

passages.title: The Daughter Who Lived
passages.text:
Yes? My father...

<Her eyes become downcast.>

I wish... there was something I could have done for him... If only I had talked to him before he...

passages.title: Those That Couldn't Be Saved
passages.text:
The val'kyr raise hundreds of corpses every day. Agatha raised you just a few moments ago. Not all are as lucky as you, however.

Some maintain their free will, but live in constant fear and confusion. They usually run off into the woods, cowering at their own reflections.

Others lose their minds completely, shambling about aimlessly. They often turn to violence, and must be destroyed.

This is your task, <name>. Destroy them, our former brothers and sisters though they might be.

passages.title: Those That Couldn't Be Saved
passages.text: You will not go far in this new life if you are unable to kill even the weakest, most brainless creatures, <name>.  Do not return until you have success to report.

passages.title: Those That Couldn't Be Saved
passages.text:
Not even the power of the val'kyr was enough to save these creatures.  They were doomed from the beginning.

I have obtained some equipment for you, <name>.  It's not much, but it will help.  Please, take your pick.

passages.title: The Damned
passages.text:
First of all, look at your armor. You're a mess, <class>.

If you'd like to stay in one piece--and I've no doubt you do--perhaps I can help. If you can gather some paws and wings from the wolves and bats nearby, maybe I'll find some armor for you. You'll find the creatures to the north and to the west of here.

passages.title: The Damned
