passages.text:
I can't help it if I feel sorry for ol' Jim there. He wasn't always like that. Ran an inn out in the marsh for a while, wonderful place.

Look, I don't really want to talk about it. Bring it up with Captain Vimes if you really have to. He's stationed on the top floor of Foothold Citadel, the large barracks to the east of Lady Jaina's tower.

passages.title: They Call Him Smiling Jim
passages.text:
James Hyal's his real name. He opened an inn at the edge of the Barrens. Wanted to make a nice place for travelers to stop over...

Might be he was thinking too big, but the inn did do well for a while. Then we lost control of the roads in the marsh, and the ogres took over.

James was too stubborn to give up his dream for safety within our walls, and the Shady Rest Inn was burnt to the ground. We're investigating, but haven't had much luck. If you want to help out, see what you can find in the rubble.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
An iron shield, blackened by the fire that raged through the inn, is affixed to the crumbling chimney, one of the few remaining parts of the structure that once made up the Shady Rest Inn.

The shield can be removed from the brick of the chimney.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Have you found evidence from the site of the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Hm, I'm no expert with the construction of arms and armor. Their use, yes, but not their making.

This shield seems as ordinary as any, excepting the damage from the fire that engulfed the inn.

passages.title: Inspecting the Ruins
passages.text:
If you follow the road south from the village, and then west toward the Barrens, you'll come across the ruins of the Shady Rest Inn.

Theramore has sent an investigator to discover how the inn met its fate. I had a man placed in that inn as a spy and I don't trust in the competence of these humans to uncover what happened.

Whatever you find, don't give a scrap of it to that investigator. We'll handle this ourselves.

passages.title: Inspecting the Ruins
passages.text:
<The inspector regards you with what can only be disdain and distrust.>

Leave this place be, errand boy, or I'll be sure to bring a contingent of guard with me next time to sink the lesson home.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
An iron shield, blackened by the fire that raged through the inn, is affixed to the crumbling chimney, one of the few remaining parts of the structure that once made up the Shady Rest Inn.

The shield can be removed from the brick of the chimney.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: What's that you have there, <name>? Evidence from the remains of the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
I grant that humans have strange decorating tastes, but would they use a plain iron shield to adorn their fireplace? Perhaps this shield was placed there by the ones who burned the inn.

A warning? A threat?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Hmm... I don't see anything out of the ordinary with this shield. We should have Do'gol, the blacksmith, take a look at it, and see if he can tell us more about it, but I wouldn't hold out hope...

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Something for me, <class>?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
This is good shield. Very strong, heavy, good. But Do'gol don't need it. I make shields, not buy them, <name>.

You should know that.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Hmmm, there's writing right here on the rim of the shield, but it's hard to read from all the burned stuff.

I need acid to make it clear. Venom from the darkmist spiders would do good. The spiders have taken over an old mine, the Darkmist Cavern, northwest of the village. Get me some of their sacs and I can clean this up.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Did you get them sacs from the spiders?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
I don't like spiders that are so big I can't sit on them and squish them.

Thanks for getting them, <name>. Now I rip them open and pour them onto the shield...

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Oh, I think I might have dropped too much acid onto the shield. Let me just rub a little...

Hm, kind of hard to read, but it looks like the name Mosarn. Never heard of him. Maybe Krog knows. Krog knows many people.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Mosarn? Sounds familiar... I can't put my finger on it. Maybe it'll come to me later.

It probably isn't important. A shield can come from anywhere and not mean anything...

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Ah, I remember now! Mosarn is a well-respected blacksmith in Thunder Bluff. I knew I had heard his name somewhere, before.

In thanks, the Earthen Ring awarded me with a set of armor crafted by Mosarn. Very good work.

Perhaps he can tell you more about the shield he crafted.

It's not much of a lead, but since we didn't get anything useful out of Reethe, it's all we have.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Hello there, <class>. Something I can help you with?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Yes, you are certainly correct. This is a shield that I made.

I'm afraid there's not much more I can tell you though, <name>. I craft so many different shields and sets of armor, I can't keep track of them all.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
A glint of light on the ground catches your eye from underneath the rubble. Brushing debris and ash caked onto the object reveals the insignia of a gold anchor on white, enameled on the surface: the sign of Theramore.

Underneath the anchor is embossed the name "Lieutenant Paval Reethe".

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text: Have you found any leads on what happened at the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text: Hmm... now this is interesting.

passages.title: Questioning Reethe
passages.text:
It took a long time, but I found Reethe. He hide good for a human.

Ogron worried that he might be crazy after so much time in swamp. You come with me for we go get answers from him.

passages.title: Questioning Reethe
passages.text:
Hmph. It is good that Reethe will no longer be lurking around the swamp, but it is a shame that humans are built so frail that he could not recover from a little arrow wound.

It seems that this thread of the mystery has led nowhere, and we must look elsewhere.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
A glint of light on the ground catches your eye from underneath the rubble. Brushing away debris and ash caked onto the object reveals the insignia of a gold anchor on white enameled on the surface: the sign of Theramore.

Underneath the anchor is embossed the name "Lieutenant Paval Reethe".

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text: Have you found anything of interest at the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
It's never good news when a guard's badge is brought to me.

Sometimes it's a man or woman who's fallen in battle, and I'm left to bring the news to the grieving family. Other times we never find out what happened to them. And other times it's even worse than that.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
I don't recognize the name of Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Your best bet would be to check with Adjutant Tesoran. He keeps track of all the records for the Theramore guard, from personnel to their equipment.

He should be able to tell you who this Reethe is with a quick check of his books.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
Hello, <name>. You'd like information about a specific member of the Theramore guard? Reethe, was it?

Just give me a moment to find the right book.

passages.title: Ezul'aan Calls
passages.text:
Ezul'aan, one of the foremost paladins in the realm, has asked to speak with you personally. I do not know what he has planned, but it sounds like he has been impressed with your rapid progress.

You should make your way to Stormwind immediately and meet him at the Training Hall in the Old Town district.

passages.title: Ezul'aan Calls
passages.text: It heartens me to see that my message found you, <name>. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: Dalgrun Calls
passages.text:
Dalgrun Steelpine oversees the training and coordination of hunters in the service of Stormwind. He has asked to speak to you personally. As soon as you are able, travel to Stormwind and meet with Dalgrun at the Training Hall in Old Town.

I have no idea what he has planned, but it sounds like he has been impressed with your rapid progress.

passages.title: Dalgrun Calls
passages.text: Ah, you've arrived. Make yourself at home, <name>. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: Make Contact with SI:7
passages.text:
It seems that the leaders of SI:7 have taken an interest in your progress and your service to the Alliance. Veruca Darkstream, a high ranking member of SI:7, has asked to speak with you. Veruca is awaiting your arrival at the Training Hall in Stormwind.

I'm not sure what she wants with you, but it seemed important.

passages.title: Make Contact with SI:7
passages.text: I hope my message didn't unnerve you, <name>. I have called you here to recognize your accomplishments.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: I have an urgent message for you from Stormwind, <name>. It seems that Speak to Patrice Lancaster has asked to speak with you at the Training Hall in Stormwind's Old Town district. The messenger did not say what the matter concerned, but that you should travel to Stormwind with all haste.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: It heartens me to see that you received my message and responded so quickly.

passages.title: The Temple of the Moon
passages.text: I have an urgent message for you from Darnassus. The message is from the High Priestess of Elune, Tyrande Whisperwind, herself! The messenger did not say what the matter concerned, but that you should travel to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and meet with the high priestess at once.

passages.title: The Temple of the Moon
passages.text: Welcome to the Temple of the Moon, <name>. I am glad that you chose to answer my summons so quickly.

passages.title: An Audience with Mulric
passages.text:
I have an urgent message for you from Stormwind, <name>. It seems Mulric Boldrock has asked to speak with you the next time you're in the city.

The messenger gave no explanation for the shaman's invitation, but you should travel to Stormwind and find Mulric Boldrock at the Training Hall to the south of Old Town as soon as you can.

passages.title: An Audience with Mulric
passages.text: Welcome, <name>. I am glad that you decided to accept my invitation.

passages.title: Frazzle's Request
passages.text:
I just received a message from Stormwind, <name>. One of Stormwind's most renowned mages, Frazzle Frostfingers, has requested that you visit him at the Training Hall in Stormwind. The Training Hall is located in the Old Town district of Stormwind.

I do not know what he has planned, but it sounds like he has been impressed with your rapid progress.

passages.title: Frazzle's Request
passages.text: Welcome to the Wizard's Sanctum, <name>. I have been watching your progress with interest.

passages.title: A Message From Evelyn Thorn
passages.text:
It seems that the elders in our ranks have taken notice of your progress and dedication, <name>. Evelyn Thorn, one of the oldest and most respected members of our circle, has sent word that she wishes to speak with you. You should not take such an invitation lightly. Most only speak with her in the course of their lessons, but if she has asked to see you personally, it must be an important matter.

Hurry back to Stormwind and look for her at the Training Hall to the south of the Old Town district.

passages.title: A Message From Evelyn Thorn
passages.text: I see that my message managed to reach you. Good. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: An Invitation from Moonglade
passages.text:
You just missed the messenger from Moonglade, <name>. He said little, except that he carried an urgent message from Loganaar, one of the honored trainers of the Cenarion Circle. Head to Moonglade as quickly as you can, <name>. The matter sounds important.

Look for Loganaar in the village of Nighthaven.

passages.title: An Invitation from Moonglade
passages.text: I'm glad to see that you have arrived safely in Nighthaven, <name>. I offer you the welcome and the hospitality of the Cenarion Circle.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: I have an urgent message for you from Stormwind, <name>. Patrice Lancaster has asked to meet with you in Stormwind. The message didn't say what the priest trainer wanted to discuss, but you should make your way to Stormwind as quickly as you can. Look for Patrice Lancaster at the Training Hall in the Old Town district of the city.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: I see that you received my message. Excellent!

passages.title: An Audience with Feenix Arcshine
passages.text: I've received an urgent message from Orgrimmar for you, <name>. The renowned mage, Feenix Arcshine, wants you to meet with him in Orgrimmar. I'm not sure what this is about, but if I was you, I would travel to the capital as fast as possible and seek out Feenix Arcshine at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: An Audience with Feenix Arcshine
passages.text: Ah, good. It seems my message did find you.

passages.title: Tamanji's Call
passages.text:
A courier from Orgrimmar just delivered a message for you. I'm to tell you that Tamanji, master of the hunters in Orgrimmar, has asked to meet with you.

Travel quickly to Orgrimmar and present yourself to Tamanji at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Tamanji's Call
passages.text: Good, you're here. Let's get started.

passages.title: The Shattered Hand
passages.text:
A messenger just arrived from Orgrimmar bearing a communication for you. Thega Graveblade, the senior rogue trainer in Orgrimmar, has sent for you. You must head to Orgrimmar immediately and meet with her at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

When Thega Graveblade summons you, the prudent thing to do is obey. Do not keep her waiting, <name>.

passages.title: The Shattered Hand
passages.text: Now that you are here, we can begin.

passages.title: The Riverspeaker Calls
passages.text: News travels upon the winds, young shaman. Your deeds have not gone unnoticed! It seems Hretar Riverspeaker wishes to discuss something with you. Make your way to Orgrimmar as quickly as you can and speak with him at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor. He will be among the others who offer training.

passages.title: The Riverspeaker Calls
passages.text: I see you are both obedient and talented, <name>. Stay that way, and you will go far in the Horde.

passages.title: Gormok Ogrefist
passages.text:
I just received word that you are needed in Orgrimmar, <name>. Gormok Ogrefist, the honored trainer of warriors in the city, has sent for you. It would not be wise to ignore such a summons.

Travel quickly to Orgrimmar and visit The Barracks in the Valley of Honor where Gormok awaits your arrival.

passages.title: Gormok Ogrefist
passages.text: I see you are both obedient and talented, <name>. Stay that way, and you will go far in the Horde.

passages.title: Kazak's Behest
passages.text:
<name>, I have received word that you are needed back in Orgrimmar. Kazak Darkscream, one of the senior warlock trainers, has something important that he wishes to discuss with you. It seems like the kind of thing that cannot wait.

Make your way back to Orgrimmar and speak with him as soon as you can. You will find him at the Training Hall in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Kazak's Behest
passages.text: Ah, you're here at last.

passages.title: A Journey to Moonglade
passages.text:
As you have heard, Moonglade is the home of the Cenarion Circle, the brotherhood of druids. All who dwell there do so in the peace of Cenarius. It is in that spirit that the trainer Loganaar has extended an invitation to visit him in Moonglade.

You will find him in the village of Nighthaven.

passages.title: A Journey to Moonglade
passages.text: Welcome to Moonglade, <name>. I have been looking forward to meeting you.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
I'm sorry I can't be of much help, <name>, but I can refer you to someone who would be. Caz Twosprocket, one of our best blacksmiths, works the forge at the smithy.

Take the shield to him, and see what he can tell you.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Something for me to look at?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Hm... interesting piece of iron you have here. Definitely not made by any of the blacksmiths I know over on this side of the sea, and it's certainly not my work.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Ah, I almost missed this... The leather strap on the back must have burned off, but it seems like it was made to fit a large person. I'd guess a tauren, actually.

That's about all I can tell you. Tell Captain Vimes I'm sorry I couldn't be of more help.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: That's not much information to work on, but we'll have to keep it in mind. Hopefully some of the other pieces of this mystery will fall into place, and paint a more helpful picture of what happened.

passages.title: Daelin's Men
passages.text:
Reddon... Redpath... Ah, here it is! Lieutenant Paval Reethe.

Joined the Theramore guard along with most of the recruits that came across the sea with Lady Proudmoore. Enlisted with the marines of Kul Tiras at the age of sixteen. Distinguished service, promotions...

Listed as missing.

passages.title: Daelin's Men
passages.text:
Missing? That would be Tesoran's kind way of saying traitor.

No doubt he's one of those fools so blindly loyal to Admiral Daelin that he turned traitor.  Isn't that a delicious irony? The deserters accuse us of betraying the Alliance.

passages.title: The Deserters
passages.text:
Reethe? That coward?

We threw him out of camp because he insisted on raiding the supplies of the ogres up at Brackenwall Village. We're not so many in number that we could stand up to those mindless brutes.

He crossed the line one too many times, so we left him to fend for himself.

Now, I helped you out... So, why don't you help us out and forget you bumped into us?

passages.title: The Deserters
passages.text: I will send Lieutenant Caldwell to deal with the deserters at Lost Point. In addition, I will instruct him to find Reethe. The marsh is not so big and trackless that he should be unable to find him.

passages.title: Vimes's Report
passages.text:
You've done some good work, <name>, best I've seen from an amateur.

Lady Proudmoore asked that I keep her apprised of this delicate situation, and I haven't spoken to her for some time now.

I was going to deliver my report to her later, but it seems more fitting that you should be the one to speak with her about it. You can probably answer her questions better than I could.

passages.title: Seek Out Tabetha
passages.text:
The arms you captured in Blackhoof Village have not seen any combat beyond mere training exercises, which means the Grimtotems who destroyed the Shady Rest are still at large.

To the south, in the heart of the Quagmire, lives the witch Tabetha. Though she is a human, she has dealt honorably with us and trained some of our mages.

Ask her for assistance in tracking down the band of Grimtotem responsible for burning the inn. The Alliance must not be allowed to think we were complicit in the attack.

passages.title: Seek Out Tabetha
passages.text:
<Tabetha smiles slightly.>

Krog wishes me to scry for the Grimtotems, eh? Well, I have no need of magic in this case.

It seems we have a mutual enemy. The Grimtotems have built an outpost nearby and are a constant thorn in the side of me and my students.

passages.title: Justice Dispensed
passages.text:
I doubt the Grimtotems will give up their campaign to drive humans from the marsh, though I get the impression you probably don't mind that. At least we have dealt with the perpetrators of the crimes at the Shady Rest Inn.

Go tell your leader that his vengeance has been sated.

passages.title: Justice Dispensed
passages.text:
<Krog listens to your report.>

I'm impressed, <name>. I would've thought that the Grimtotem criminals would've been more difficult to locate. The Alliance are truly incompetent.

In truth, I just sought to answer the death of one of my men, but this situation has been more fortunate than expected. If the Grimtotem choose to retaliate, it will likely be against the Alliance. Perhaps we will soon have the manpower to drive the scum from these shores once and for all.

passages.title: Seek Out Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text:
Avaros Dawnglaive, a senior Blood Knight and advisor to the warchief, requires your presence in Orgrimmar. He has taken an interest in your training, <name>, and it is imperative that you speak with him immediately.

The message I received didn't mention the reason he requested your visit, but you should set out for Orgrimmar right away. Avaros Dawnglaive can be found at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Seek Out Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text: I've heard much about you, <name>. You have a bright future ahead of you in the Horde.

passages.title: Torn Ground
passages.text:
It won't be takin' much convincin' to turn us against da Twilight - dat's already our goal. We've already come to battle here though, so we may be needin' ya help before we can turn towards dere fortress.

Da Twilight have already brought Iso'rath up from da ground to the south, I'm sure ya noticed. Its tentacles have been burstin' from da ground all around us. We could use a hand beatin' them down if you be willin'.

passages.title: Torn Ground
passages.text: Did ya have any luck with dose tentacles?

passages.title: Torn Ground
passages.text: Tank ya, <class>. A bit of breathin' room helps a lot.

passages.title: Pushing Back
passages.text: Da Twilight's Hammer have destroyed a Dragonmaw town to the south and are performin' dey're summonin' rituals from there. Offer dem no respite to continue wit dey're incantations. Bring tha battle to dem!

passages.title: Pushing Back
passages.text: Revenge is bittersweet, but I'm glad we be havin' someone as powerful as you do see dis done.

passages.title: Unbroken
passages.text:
We are preparing a ritual that may be of use in destroying Iso'rath, the old god bred abomination that the Twilight's Hammer have brought up from the depths. We are delayed though, for one of our strongest was captured during an assault on their encampment.

Earthcaller Yevaa is within the ruins to the south. She is not dead. I am sure of it. Please, rescue her. If any of us is deserving of your aid, it is her.

passages.title: Unbroken
passages.text: Thank the elements that you've come. Did my brothers send you?

passages.title: Simple Solutions
passages.text:
I'm new to this gig. Very new. But ya know what? That gives me perspective!

These shaman buddies of mine have come upon somethin' great, but they're too single minded! They lean on the elements and they forget to make use of the common materials all around them.

In the ruins to the south, I saw those Twilight goons tote in barrels of flammable oil! They used it when they razed the town. I say we use it when we raze them.

passages.title: Simple Solutions
passages.text: I wonder what happens when you douse an elemental with that stuff. Jumbo-super-bonfire-elemental? I'm thinkin' so. We'll have to try.

passages.title: Simple Solutions
passages.text: Now that's what I'm talkin' about! Can you think of all the uses for this stuff? I definitely can't. But I can think of a lot, and I'm liking the possibilities.

passages.title: Meet With Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text:
Avaros Dawnglaive sends word from Orgrimmar -- he wishes to speak with you when you're in the city. I needn't remind you that Avaros is an honored member of our order and his requests should not be ignored.

Next time you are in Orgrimmar, travel to The Barracks in the Valley of Honor and speak with him.

passages.title: Meet With Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text: I've heard much of your contributions to the Horde, <name>.

passages.title: Of Love and Family
passages.text:
Inside the Scarlet Bastion is a painting of great personal value to Highlord Tirion Fordring. Search for a painting of our twin moons. Chip away at the paint until you uncover the master work, 'Of Love and Family.'

May the Light guide your actions, and please handle the painting with the utmost care.

passages.title: Of Love and Family
passages.text: The painting, <name>. Do you have the painting?

passages.title: Of Love and Family
passages.text: Master Fordring will be glad beyond measure to see this painting again.

passages.title: Talk to Ogron
passages.text:
I know this human, Paval Reethe. Pathetic, even for his kind. He deserted his fellow soldiers and is now hiding out in the woods.

I sent Ogron out to track him down. Some of the others suspect he's been stealing from our supplies. I think I saw Ogron heading off to the southeast.

passages.title: Talk to Ogron
passages.text:
Ogron? Yeah, that me.

Shh. Keep voice down. Crocs hear you.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: Do you feel it, <class>? The elements are uneasy. We members of the Earthen Ring have struggled to find the cause of the unrest. Thus far we have been unsuccessful and now turn to others that may aid us. Speak with Erunak Stonespeaker in Stormwind and see how you might be able to aid us.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: I'm glad you've come, <class>.  These are troublesome times and we could use all the help we can get.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: Do you feel it, <class>? The elements are uneasy. We members of the Earthen Ring have struggled to find the cause of the unrest. Thus far we have been unsuccessful and now turn to others that may aid us. Speak with Earthmender Norsala in Orgrimmar and see what tasks she may have for you.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: I'm glad you've come, <class>.  These are troublesome times and we could use all the help we can get.

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text:
Alright, these cowards want to fight? Let's see how well they do without any weapons.

I'm sure you must have a torch, or something. Burn their weapon racks.

Burn them all!

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text: Let's see them wage their war now!

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text:
The Grimtotem want to fight? Let us see how well they do without their weapons.

I'm sure you must have something that burns. Set their weapon racks ablaze, my <class> friend.

Let nature take its course.

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text: We shall have to burn more of their weapon racks than that if we are to put a dent in their ability to fight.

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text: Let us see how well they fight without their weapons.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text:
There's no way around it. If you want to win a battle, you have to spill some blood. In this case... a lot of it.

You know what we have to do.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text: That put a dent in their numbers! Can't say that they didn't deserve it.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text:
There is no alternative: if you intend to win a battle, you must spill the enemy's blood. In this case, unfortunately, a lot of it.

You know what we have to do.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text: While the Earth Mother does not condone such violence, we had no choice. The Grimtotem have ignored Her teachings for too long and are reaping what they have sown.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text:
Sentinel training 101: take out their leaders and your enemy's forces will soon fall apart. We're going to do just that, <class>.

Isha Gloomaxe is the closest of the Grimtotem chiefs. Let's see if we can't take her measure.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text: She was tougher than I thought. We worked well together, but we're going to have to make sure not to underestimate the other Grimtotem chiefs.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text:
Basic brave philosophy dictates that if you kill the leaders of your enemy's forces, they will soon fall into disarray. We are going to do just that, <class>.

Isha Gloomaxe is the closest of the Grimtotem chiefs. We will test her and her axe, and she will be found wanting.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text: She was more formidable than her reputation suggested. Although we worked well together, we must make certain not to underestimate the other Grimtotem chiefs.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text:
Elder Stormhoof is a shaman of immense power. Supposedly, he is a direct disciple of Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone, leader of the Grimtotem clan.

We know that he's here and that he's been training their geomancers. We have to kill him, <class>.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text:
That's two of them. Two more to go.

I wonder what he meant about being "chosen"?

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text:
Elder Stormhoof is a shaman chief of immense power. He was taught by Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone, leader of the Grimtotem clan.

We know that he is here and that he has been training their geomancers. We have to kill him, <class>.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text: That was not pleasant. I wonder what he meant by calling you, "the Chosen"?

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
In shu'halo myth, the Rattle of Bones is connected with the Writ of History and the Drums of War. They are supposed to be powerful tauren artifacts.

We must keep our eyes peeled if we're to find the other two. The writ will most likely look like some kind of pictographic scroll if the stories are to be believed.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text: We'll need the actual writ, not just any tauren scroll hanging.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
I'm fairly certain that's it. This is very intriguing, <name>. What are they doing here? Are they being used as a weapon?

The wind serpent flew northwest to that next bluff. Maybe that's where the drums are?

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
The Rattle of Bones is a part of shu'halo ancient myth. It is always connected with the Writ of History and the Drums of War. They are supposed to be powerful tauren artifacts; gifts from the Earth Mother if the tales are to be believed. I cannot imagine Her being connected with the drums, though.

We must be vigilant if we are to find the other two. The writ will look like a pictographic scroll if memory serves.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text: We will need the actual writ, and not just any scroll hanging.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
This is very exciting and also worrisome, <name>. What are these artifacts doing here? Are they being used as a weapons against us by the Grimtotem?

The wind serpent flew northwest to that next bluff. Maybe that's where the drums are?

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
One of the infamous Grimtotem leaders of the Stonetalon Mountains has returned home.

We should take this opportunity to make sure that he doesn't go anywhere else.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text: We need to find and slay Grundig Darkcloud, <name>.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
<The sentinel gives you an appraising look.>

What is it with you? Why do they all seem spooked by you being here?

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
One of the most accomplished Grimtotem leaders of the Stonetalon Mountains has returned home.

We must make the most of this chance and put an end to his campaign of terror once and for all.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
<The brave gives you an appraising look.>

There is something special about you, <name>. That much is certain.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Whatever the Grimtotem are doing with these Drums of War, we don't want them to have them.

Don't worry, <name>, we'll figure it all out. But first, we need to gather all of the pieces of the puzzle.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text: The tauren love their drums. I can only imagine the Drums of War will be somehow different from the others.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Surely that was the voice of the Elder Crone!

We must be very careful, <name>. Great danger lies ahead if Magatha Grimtotem has taken notice of you.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Whatever it is that the Grimtotem are doing with the Drums of War, we do not want them to keep them.

Do not worry, <name>, we will figure out what is going on here. But first, we need to gather all of the artifacts.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text: War is not an activity to engage in for those who are faithful to the Earth Mother's teachings.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Surely that was the voice of the Elder Crone!

We must be very careful, <name>. Great danger lies ahead if Magatha Grimtotem has taken notice of you.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
And now the time has come to take out the leader of all of the Darkcloud Pinnacle Grimtotem: Arnak Grimtotem.

It is said that he's the disgraced nephew of Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone and matriarch of the Grimtotem clan. Supposedly, his indiscretions have left him in a state of disfavor with her.

But none of that matters right now. All that matters is that we kill him. For good this time.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text: We have to kill Arnak, <name>, if we are to win the battle for the tauren of Freewind Post.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
For some reason they all think that you've been sent by Magatha Grimtotem. I know it must have something to do with that wind serpent that's been hanging around.

Doesn't matter. Their leader is dead. It's only a matter of time before the tauren of Freewind Post regain their home.

If I were them, I'd push back a little to teach the Grimtotem a lesson, but they probably won't. They're tauren.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
The time has come to deal with the leader of the Darkcloud Pinnacle Grimtotem: Arnak Grimtotem.

He is the disgraced nephew of Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone and matriarch of the Grimtotem clan. His indiscretions have left him in a state of disfavor with her.

None of that matters now. All that matters is that we deal with him. Once and for all.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text: Arnak must fall, <name>, if we are to win the battle against the Grimtotem.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
They all believed that you have been sent by Magatha Grimtotem. There is no arguing that her pet, Arikara, has been lurking about.

<The brave gives you a long look.>

It does not matter. Arnak is dead. It is only a matter of time before we take back Freewind Post.

Perhaps now we will be able to establish a lasting peace with the Grimtotem?

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text:
I am familiar with these artifacts. I believe that they were brought here by Magatha Grimtotem herself. But she's not amongst the Grimtotem on Darkcloud Pinnacle. She disappeared right after she arrived, and no one knows where she is now.

Maybe we can find out.

Take the rattle, the writ, and the drum out to Arikara's Needle. If my guess is correct, the wind serpent will appear again. You'll have to defeat it to gain knowledge of where Magatha is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: Only by subduing Arikara will you discover where Magatha Grimtotem is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: So, she's been taken prisoner by the Twilight's Hammer. I can't say that I feel sorry for her, but she might prove even more dangerous in their hands.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text:
I am familiar with these artifacts. I believe that they were brought here by Magatha Grimtotem herself. But she's not amongst the Grimtotem on Darkcloud Pinnacle. She disappeared right after she arrived, and no one knows where she is now.

Maybe we can find out.

Take the rattle, the writ, and the drum out to Arikara's Needle. If my guess is correct, the wind serpent will appear again. You'll have to defeat it to gain knowledge of where Magatha is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: Only by subduing Arikara will you discover where Magatha Grimtotem is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: So, she's been taken prisoner by the Twilight's Hammer. I can't say that I feel sorry for her, but she might prove even more dangerous in their hands.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: Thank you for coming to see me, <name>.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: The spirits knew that you would answer my call, <name>.

passages.title: Losing Ground
passages.text:
I don't know how much longer we can hold out for, <name>. Crowley and Bloodfang's worgen know every hidey hole and safe spot in Gilneas. One minute they're standing in front of you and the next minute they're gone! We're gonna lose this war to attacks of opportunity, even though we have a superior military presence.

But momma didn't raise no quitter! Forsaken until the end, my friend.

Head west into the headlands and help our soldiers on the front line. Kill the attacking worgen rebels!

passages.title: Losing Ground
passages.text: Kill the rebels!

passages.title: Losing Ground
passages.text:
If I could still breathe I'd let out a sigh of relief.

Don't get too comfortable, though, <name>, your mission here has just begun.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: There you are, <name>. I was beginning to think my message hadn't found you.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: Welcome, <name>. I'm glad that you accepted my invitation. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: In Time, All Will Be Revealed
passages.text:
The Dark Lady has sent you and Arthura here for a very specific purpose. Before I tell you more, we must make preparations.

Head east into the forest of Gilneas and search near the trees and rocks of the region for a special plant known as wolfsbane. Gather as much of the wolfsbane as you can carry and return to me.

Our mission here goes far beyond the scope of the battlefield, <name>. In time, all will be revealed.

passages.title: In Time, All Will Be Revealed
passages.text: Did you gather the wolfsbane?

passages.title: In Time, All Will Be Revealed
passages.text:
<Belmont takes the wolfsbane from you.>

Good. Now just do as Forward Commander Onslaught commands. Try your best to fit in with the rest of the soldiers. We don't want the Gilneas Liberation Front to get suspicious.

Oh, you didn't know they were watching us? Right now there are five different worgen spies looking down on our position. Just be calm and follow orders. I'll let you know when we are ready to proceed.

passages.title: The F.C.D.
passages.text:
Communications are down with all of our frontline outposts, <name>. As of right now I don't have a damn clue as to the status of our troops in Gilneas. We need to re-establish communications.

I need you to head west into the headlands and find our outpost on the coast. By now the soldiers there are likely all dead, but their F.C.D. might be operational. Grab the device and get back to me.

passages.title: The F.C.D.
passages.text: Recover the F.C.D.

passages.title: The F.C.D.
passages.text: With this device I will be able to communicate with you in the field. Now to check the rest of our frontline outposts.

passages.title: The Zeppelin Crash
passages.text:
Not long ago, a goblin zeppelin crashed to the east. A representative of the Steamwheedle Cartel passed through here a few days ago.

She was looking for information about the zeppelin's cargo and its pilot, Beezil, but none of us really got a good look at the crash. I doubt she'll be able to clean up after the wreck by herself, much less recover whatever cargo the vessel might have carried.

If you have time, you may want to check up on her out at Beezil's Wreck, due east of here, near the mountains.

passages.title: The Zeppelin Crash
passages.text:
So those hermit mages sent you? How can I be sure that I can trust you?

I suppose I can use the help. There's not much here a mage would be interested in, anyway.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Dreadwatch Outpost
passages.text:
I'm not gonna lie to you, <name>. What I'm about to ask you to do is suicide. Chance of failure is about 95%.

All communication from Dreadwatch Outpost has been severed. With the worgen constantly rushing us we have no means by which to get to Dreadwatch to check on our soldiers. I need you to head south to the outpost and check on our soldiers. I'll keep in contact through the Forsaken communication device - F.C.D. - from here on out.

KEEP CLEAR OF THE MAIN ROAD.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Dreadwatch Outpost
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. crackles with static.>

Dreadwatch is lost? This is bad, <name>. Real bad.

If Dreadwatch is compromised it means we've lost Gilneas City.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Rutsak's Guard
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. hums.>

Our next outpost is Rutsak's Guard, located due east of Dreadwatch. Make your way to Rutsak's while avoiding the worgen rushers, <name>. You don't want to deal with those monsters by yourself.

If you make it there in one piece, look for Captain Rutsak.

Just be prepared for the worst.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Rutsak's Guard
passages.text:
Th... Af... After we lost Gilneas City, the port fell.

HU... HUM... HUMANS ARE HERE! Reinforcements from Stormwind! They slaughtered my men. Left me alive to witness their strength. To tell high command... To tell them that the 7th Legion are here...

passages.title: Liquid Gold
passages.text:
As the Scourge swept through Stratholme like a plague, the Knights of the Silver Hand manufactured holy water to use against the invaders. They stored it inside small crates along with other vital supplies, and distributed them throughout the city. Unfortunately, the citizens turned into Scourge reinforcements before the supplies could ever be used!

These supply crates will prove extremely useful to our efforts. Bring me a vial of Stratholme Holy Water, we need to have it replicated in mass quantities.

passages.title: Liquid Gold
passages.text:
Is that the vial of Stratholme Holy Water?

Wait, is that just regular water? Don't play games with ol' Stonebruiser!

passages.title: Liquid Gold
passages.text: Excellent! I think the holy water will prove devastating in large volumes.

passages.title: Argent Reinforcements
passages.text:
The Scourge have some sort of ward in place that's preventing me from opening a portal so that our reinforcements can help us take the city! It's like a neverending screaming inside of my head! Agh!

I'm doing all I can to retain my sanity from that noise with this barrier. My best guess is that the banshees are maintaining the defense. If you could bring me some of their essences, I think I can use them to counteract the ward and get our boys in here!

passages.title: Argent Reinforcements
passages.text: Were you able to obtain the essences? Be careful, they're deadly spellcasters.

passages.title: Argent Reinforcements
passages.text:
Oh my... the banshees are very tortured souls indeed. Merely holding their essence is emotionally painful...

Enough of that for now. I'll get to work on counteracting their magic, then we'll have a portal up and running in no time. Stratholme will be ours soon, I just know it.

passages.title: Vengeance for Our Soldiers
passages.text:
7th Legion... They rushed us in the dead of the night. Their captain barked orders as the submariners slaughtered my men. Then he came to me, put his face in mine, and said something I'll never forget:

"The name's Master Sergeant Pietro Zaren, officer in the 7th Legion. When you see your soldiers being slaughtered in your nightmares - if you even still dream - remember my name and tremble."

Avenge my soldiers! Kill the 7th Legion occupying the Cathedral Quarter of Gilneas City, southwest of here.

passages.title: Vengeance for Our Soldiers
passages.text:
Though we were shamed in battle, the enemy was not victorious. I will not soon forget this, <name>.

If I make it back to Silverpine I will likely retire from the service. War is not in my blood.

passages.title: On Whose Orders?
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. buzzes.>

The 7th Legion are an elite special ops regiment. They've been there, behind the scenes, for almost every major offensive and military engagement the Alliance has ever done. This is bad news. How did they get past our warships? And on whose orders are they here?

We need to get our hands on their orders. This Pietro character will undoubtedly have vital information. Find him at the Cathedral Quarter in Gilneas City and take him out. Search his corpse for clues.

passages.title: On Whose Orders?
passages.text: Status?

passages.title: On Whose Orders?
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. crackles with electricity.>

An Alliance armada is en route? How could this have happened?

<Forward Commander Onslaught cuts out for a moment. You hear worgen howling in the background.>

You've got to hurry, <name>. We're being overrun up here at Forward Command.

passages.title: Gidwin Goldbraids
passages.text:
I love my boys, don't get me wrong. But I TOLD them that I needed FIVE MINUTES to water and brush the horses, and what did they do? They made a stupid bet with each other and ran off! I should have known better... this always happens.

Gidwin's the short one. He headed north, along the river. If you're headed that direction, would you tell him to come back? We've got to get to Light's Hope Chapel, and I'm not against leaving without him.

passages.title: Gidwin Goldbraids
passages.text:
Tarenar?  Is that you?

Whoever you are, would you mind helping me out of this thing?

passages.title: Just Encased
passages.text:
You should have seen me fight! I must have killed six of those beasts, when...

Oh wait, you can count the bodies, can't you? OK, fine. I killed four of them, when the fifth one shot me with this web. To make things even worse... when he blasted me with web juice, my mouth was open!

I can't seem to break these webs, and I doubt you'll be able to, either. No, you'll have to get some of the stomach juice from those undead spider-things. That'll do the trick.

passages.title: Just Encased
passages.text: Oh boy... Fiona is going to be madder than a wet harpy.  You'd better hurry.

passages.title: Just Encased
passages.text:
You're back?!  Thank the Light!

Before you throw that acid on me, I need to ask: Are you the guy who was here before, or are you one of those eight-legged cowards?  I need to know whether or not I should smack you on my way out.

passages.title: Tarenar Sunstrike
passages.text:
As soon as we stopped, they made a bet about "who could kill the most undead in five minutes."

It's been an hour, and I'm still waiting for them to come back.

I saw Tarenar run off to the southeast. Unfortunately, I can't leave the caravan here by itself. If you end up traveling in that direction, could you find him and send him back to me?

passages.title: Tarenar Sunstrike
passages.text: I've found them, <race>.  The Scourge.  How I've longed for this day.

passages.title: What I Do Best
passages.text:
I remember when I was young, I would sneak off into the Ghostlands and just beat up zombies for hours on end. Nobody even PAID me. I just did it.

Now, look in front of you. Those are some serious zombies. I was just about to start beating them up, too. Care to join me?

passages.title: What I Do Best
passages.text:
Five should be good enough.

Yikes, look at the time!  I need to head back to camp.

passages.title: Onward, to Light's Hope Chapel
passages.text:
Now that the boys are back, we can head out. You headed east?

Please, join us! I insist! Yesterday, we were in the Menders' Stead, and I was telling Tarenar, "We have two paladins and a shopkeeper, but you know what we really need? A <class>!"

Don't look at me that way! I'm serious! Come on, hop in the cart.

passages.title: Onward, to Light's Hope Chapel
passages.text:
Hope the ride wasn't too bumpy for you.

Have a look around the tower while the horses rest.  It's no Light's Hope Chapel, but I'm sure you can find some way to keep yourself busy.

passages.title: The Maw of Iso'rath
passages.text:
We are ready to attack the beast. First, we need to destroy it's tentacles, then Yevaa will perform a ritual to summon a powerful fire elemental that we will drop into its maw.

I want you to fly out with our first group attack. Hold steady until an opportunity presents itself, then join the battle with the rest of the shaman in cutting the tentacles down.

Take any one of the gryphons when you're ready to join the assault.

passages.title: The Maw of Iso'rath
passages.text:
The tentacles swept us off of our gryphons as well! They were far more nimble than we anticipated.

No matter. We were prepared for this possibility. I can summon the elemental from here if you can keep me safe.

passages.title: The Worldbreaker
passages.text: There's no time! Deathwing struck before we could form against him. If you do not stop him, the Earthen Ring will end this day!

passages.title: The Worldbreaker
passages.text: You're awake! Thank the elements. I'd almost lost all hope.

passages.title: Nightmare
passages.text:
Iso'rath's brain is revealed! The shaman you've saved should keep you somewhat safe amidst his defenses.

Strike at the brain and destroy Iso'rath!

passages.title: Nightmare
passages.text: You saved many of my closest allies today, <name>. I can only imagine what horrors you witnessed within Iso'rath, but you have the thanks of all of the Earthen Ring.

passages.title: Traveling Companions
passages.text:
While we're waiting here at this tower, we might as well see if anybody else is headed to Light's Hope Chapel. The more, the merrier, I say!

Ask around to see if anybody wants to join us on our trip. I'm sure you can find somebody who's headed to Light's Hope.

passages.title: Traveling Companions
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Traveling Companions
passages.text:
Argus Highbeacon... that old guy on the top of the tower?  Great!

A man his age must have been in the Argent Crusade for a long time.  Maybe he can put in the good word for us at Light's Hope.

passages.title: Little Pamela
passages.text:
The battle for Darrowshire still haunts me, <race>. I wake up in cold sweats, convinced that I'm still there; that it is happening all over again.

I've coped with the loss of my comrades, but the loss of my family members is still cripplingly painful. One of my kin lost during the attack was my young niece, Pamela.

If you are brave enough to enter Darrowshire, will you search for any sign of Pammy? Darrowshire's ruins are due south of here.

passages.title: Little Pamela
passages.text: Hello.  I'm Pamela, what's your name?

passages.title: Pamela's Doll
passages.text:
My auntie Marlene told me to stay here in our house because my father had to go and fight. My father's the bravest man in the whole world!

But I've been here for a long time, and he hasn't come for me. Sometimes bad people come and whisper to me and I want my dad to make them go away, but he's not here!

And sometimes when it gets dark I want to play with my doll but I can't because I left it in town.

Will you find my doll for me?

passages.title: Pamela's Doll
passages.text: Did you find my doll?

passages.title: Pamela's Doll
passages.text: You found it!  You found my doll!  Oh, thank you!

passages.title: Marauders of Darrowshire
passages.text:
I require a rare reagent for the powerful spell I intend to cast: skulls from the scourge who took part in the battle of Darrowshire.

Take this crystal and hunt scourge champions for their skulls. The crystal is enchanted; if a champion took part in the battle, then when you pass the crystal over its skull it will resonate. Bring me those resonating skulls.

Go, <name>. You'll find scourge champions in the Fungal Vale to the north. Go.

passages.title: Marauders of Darrowshire
passages.text: Do you have the skulls?  They are critical for my spell, which will give us the chance to save Darrowshire.  Maybe.

passages.title: Marauders of Darrowshire
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  Are you certain you haven't done this before?

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: I sense a strong power calling to me from the ruins. Can you check again on that southern battle site for me? I'm certain that there's something there.

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: The Wavespeaker was right. There's something here.

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: I sense a strong power calling to me from the ruins. Can you check again on that southern battle site for me? I'm certain that there's something there.

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: The Wavespeaker was right. There's something here.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text:
We've defeated the enemy's forces here, <name>. But Hyjal is not the only place where our foes are moving against us.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Naraat the Earthspeaker at the Eastern Earthshrine in Stormwind City for further instructions.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text:
We've defeated the enemy's forces here, <name>. But Hyjal is not the only place where our foes are moving against us.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Farseer Krogar at the Western Earthshrine in Orgrimmar for further instructions.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: What Tomorrow Brings
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. buzzes.>

Look around the Cathedral Quarter. There should be a telescope nearby that the 7th Legion uses for spying. Find it and use it to scout the harbor. We need to find out how the 7th Legion got past our fleet.

Hurry, <name>. We can't hold these beasts back much longer.

What does tomorrow bring?

passages.title: What Tomorrow Brings
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. crackles with electricity.>

TORPEDOED! We had everything at the water line covered, but nothing below the line. They must have snuck in beneath our defenses and then blown our warships to smithereens.

And now the rest of the Alliance fleet is nearly here...

passages.title: A Man Named Godfrey
passages.text:
Lord Vincent Godfrey spent his life defending the kingdom of Gilneas. When the worgen curse ravaged this land, Godfrey was one of the first Gilneans to take up arms against the beasts. It is said that upon discovering that his king was afflicted by the curse, Godfrey took his own life. He would rather be dead than serve the very creatures that he had defended his home against.

We are going to give him a second chance, <name>. Together we will battle southeast towards Tempest's Reach to collect his corpse.

passages.title: A Man Named Godfrey
passages.text: Lord Vincent Godfrey. The name itself evokes feelings of dread in the hearts of worgen.

passages.title: A Man Named Godfrey
passages.text: Here we are, <name>. He is a little rotted, but no worse for the wear. We must hurry before the Alliance finds us!

passages.title: Bloodfen Feathers
passages.text:
Are you startled by Brogg's presence here, little <race>? Don't worry. Goblins at Mudsprocket are Brogg's friends and you can be, too.

Brogg left Brackenwall Village when new overlord not take revenge against black dragonkin for destroying old home and killing many of Brogg's old friends. Brogg come here to lay friends spirits to rest and avenge them, but Brogg need help preparing. For ritual, Brogg need feathers with strong magic, like ones worn by raptors at Bloodfen Burrow to the west of town.

passages.title: Bloodfen Feathers
passages.text:
<Brogg looks at you hopefully.>

You bring Brogg feathers?

passages.title: Bloodfen Feathers
passages.text:
<Brogg accepts the feathers.>

Brogg pleased with these feathers. Very strong magic. Brogg not know what raptors do to give feathers power, but raptor feathers always best for ritual.

passages.title: Banner of the Stonemaul
passages.text:
When the dragons came and took over Brogg's old home, Stonemaul ogres fled and left everything behind, including clan's banner.

Brogg knows banner was kept deep in Stonemaul ogre mound, but these days it's called Den of Flame. Brogg must have clan banner to get his revenge on dragons who killed his friends.

Brogg's clan's old mound, Den of Flame, is northwest of Mudsprocket and crawling with dragonkin. Banner will be deep inside the cave. Be careful, <name>.

passages.title: Banner of the Stonemaul
passages.text: You bring Stonemaul banner?

passages.title: Banner of the Stonemaul
passages.text: You have Brogg's thanks, <name>. Brogg has big plans for clan banner.

passages.title: The Essence of Enmity
passages.text:
To make the totem Brogg will need for his ritual, he must use the essences of the creatures who killed his friends. The hate and anger of Brogg's enemies will fuel the magic of his vengeance.

Track down Firemane ash tails, scouts, or scalebanes and use Brogg's totem on their corpses. Only when the dragonkin die will they give up their essences.

The creatures you seek swarm over the Den of Flame to the northwest and the Stonemaul Ruins to the north.

passages.title: The Essence of Enmity
passages.text: Do you have the essences? Brogg must have them to avenge his friends!

passages.title: The Essence of Enmity
passages.text: You have Brogg's thanks, <name>. Once Brogg adds their magic to the totem, it will be able to redeem the spirits of Brogg's fallen friends.

passages.title: Spirits of Stonemaul Hold
passages.text:
Brogg has completed the totem that will put the spirits of his friends to rest. When the dragonkin came, they killed all Stonemaul who did not flee. Brogg fled with Overlord Mok'Morokk, hoping to lead a counterattack with other Stonemaul survivors.

The counterattack never came and the spirits of the Stonemaul dead still haunt Brogg and the others. Take this totem north to Stonemaul Ruins and use it near ogre skeletons to draw the spirit to you. Defeat the spirit to give it rest with its bones.

passages.title: Spirits of Stonemaul Hold
passages.text: Brogg must know, have you brought peace to the violent spirits of the Stonemaul?

passages.title: Spirits of Stonemaul Hold
passages.text: Brogg thanks you for your help, although he knows Overlord Mok'Morokk never will. At least surviving Stonemaul can finally focus on problems with the living and leave dead where they belong. Only one thing remains for Brogg to do.

passages.title: Catch a Dragon by the Tail
passages.text:
With the zeppelin crash delaying supplies, we've run out of medicines and bandages.

We're making use of what we can, but between all the insects, the injuries, and the enemies we're encountering here, I can barely keep up! I've found one herb that seems to help heal wounds and dull pain, but it, too, is in short supply.

It's called wyrmtail, and it's abundant in the Dragonmurk and Wyrmbog areas east of town. The plants themselves are made of coiled stalks, and seem to pulsate when you look at them.

passages.title: Catch a Dragon by the Tail
passages.text: Did you find any of the wyrmtail?

passages.title: Catch a Dragon by the Tail
passages.text: Thank you! This will help keep our guys going out in the field until Moxie returns with the rest of the supplies from the zeppelin crash.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
Onyxia's brood has been scattered across the Dragonmurk. It is imperative that no more whelps be permitted to hatch.

Make haste to Wyrmbog in the south of Dustwallow Marsh. Surely, she has made her lair there. Track down the evil dragon's eggs and destroy them.

We will never reclaim Stonemaul Village if the surrounding area remains a breeding ground.

As for Mok'Morokk... I have other plans for the sod.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
You must hurry to the Dragonmurk, <name>. With Onyxia's eggs riddled around the Wyrmbog, we face overwhelming numbers unless something is done quickly.

Destroy her eggs! Don't let the black dragon plague spread across our homeland!

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
Splendid! It will be sometime before Onyxia can produce more eggs.

On behalf of my people, I thank you, <name>.

I have asked much of you so far. Perhaps you can do the Stonemaul Clan one last service.

Mok'Morokk is not fit to lead us. Tharg would make an excellent leader but is hindered by his injuries and age. Drive Mok'Morokk from this place by force. Only then can we appoint a new leader to return us to our proper home in the south.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
Stonemaul Village was invaded by the brood of Onyxia. But why would the daughter of the black dragonlord, Deathwing, descend upon our lands?

This is most troubling. Surely, Onyxia was driven here for a purpose beyond laying siege to a small band of ogres.

Notify Mok'Morokk at once! Action must be taken.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text: Why you tell me 'bout dragons? Me no like dragons. Me like it here. No dragons here.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text: You leave me alone now. Go tell Draz'Zilb we stay here. No black dragon here.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
That lazy coward!

Mok'Morokk displayed strength when Rexxar was our leader. But soon after Rexxar's departure Mok'Morokk fell prey to temptations of power. Rather than lead, he demanded. He does not serve his people but rather expects us to serve him.

Something must be done.

passages.title: A City Under Siege
passages.text:
We will never control the Eastern Plaguelands if we do not control Stratholme. Not only is it a point of incredible strategic importance, it also houses our enemies' leaders - Balnazzar and Lord Aurius Rivendare. Their Risen and Scourge armies threaten to erase all the progress we've made.

The Argent Crusade is well-suited to this task. Travel west through Stratholme's main gate and speak with Packmaster Stonebruiser. He will direct you further.

passages.title: A City Under Siege
passages.text: What a relief it is to see an able-bodied soldier that's on our side! There's plenty for ye to do around here, <race>.

passages.title: Resistance is Futile
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. buzzes.>

This is Commander Lorna Crowley of the Gilneas Liberation Front. If you are hearing this message then you know that the Alliance once again controls Gilneas. Lay down your weapons and surrender. Failure to comply will result in your death.

Our forces have locked on to your position and will arrive shortly. Resistance is futile.

passages.title: Resistance is Futile
passages.text: Surrender? Coward talk...

passages.title: Resistance is Futile
passages.text: No time to bask in the battle glory, <name>. We have a job to do. I have no doubt more of those beasts are on the way.

passages.title: A Grim Connection
passages.text:
I've spoken with Inspector Tarem regarding the evidence you gathered from the ruins of the Shady Rest Inn. He seems certain that the hoofprints and the shield you found there point to the Grimtotem clan of tauren.

With reports of Grimtotem activity on the rise in the marsh, this has to be more than a mere coincidence. I'm sending you to speak with Captain Darill, who is something of an expert on the Grimtotems. Follow the road north out of town to North Point tower. It's the second outpost on the road.

passages.title: A Grim Connection
passages.text: Captain Vimes thinks the Grimtotems are behind the destruction of the Shady Rest Inn? They wouldn't have been first on my list of suspects, but if Captain Vimes sent you here to follow up on a lead, he must have his reasons. Regardless, the Grimtotems have been a thorn in our side for some time and we're always glad to have the extra help.

passages.title: Tabetha's Assistance
passages.text:
I can't spare any men to help search for a second Grimtotem outpost, but I think I know of someone who might be able to help you.

Deep in the Quagmire, to the south, there is a small farmstead owned by Tabetha. She may seem little more than an old hermit, but the truth is that she's a mage and scryer of some renown. Follow the road south to her farm and seek her help in finding the culprits responsible for the massacre at the Shady Rest Inn.

passages.title: Tabetha's Assistance
passages.text: So you want me to scry for Grimtotems, eh? And what will you say when I tell you there's no need?

passages.title: Justice for the Hyals
passages.text:
Although these Grimtotems were simply a nuisance to me, Captain Vimes will want to know of your deeds. Bring him the news that you have tracked down and dealt with those responsible for the burning of the Shady Rest Inn.

It's too late to save Jim Hyal's family, but perhaps the Grimtotems will think twice before attacking anyone connected to Theramore.

passages.title: Justice for the Hyals
passages.text:
<The captain listens to your report intently.>

We have avenged James and his family, but not even that can restore what was destroyed.

passages.title: Tipping the Balance
passages.text:
<Harrison grins.>

That's it, <name>. The pieces we need are hidden in these statues!

They look to be a bit off balance as is. Maybe just a little nudge...

I must say, your field work is coming along nicely. If you applied yourself, you could make a fine archaeologist one day.

passages.title: Tipping the Balance
passages.text: Talk about bringing the house down...

passages.title: Zaeldarr the Outcast
passages.text:
Can you believe that, after all the trouble we have in the Plaguelands... we have to worry about thieves too? And not just normal thieves, troll thieves.

And not just normal troll thieves. Dead troll thieves!

They're led by this big, dead troll named Zaeldarr the Outcast, and they come here at night and steal bodies from our graveyards, then take them back to their evil, dead troll hideout--the Undercroft to the southwest.

Go there and take out Zaeldarr, <name>. I'm sick to death of his mischief!

passages.title: Zaeldarr the Outcast
passages.text: Did you find the hideout, <name>?  Did you take care of Zaeldarr?

passages.title: Zaeldarr the Outcast
passages.text: Great, you got him!  And I hope you taught his gang a lesson too!

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text:
We find ourselves in a much better position against our enemies in Vashj'ir than before you arrived. Don't get me wrong, your aid is still needed here, but perhaps other fronts are in an even more urgent situation.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Farseer Krogar at the Western Earthshrine in Orgrimmar for further instructions.

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text:
We find ourselves in a much better position against our enemies in Vashj'ir than before you arrived. Don't get me wrong, your aid is still needed here, but perhaps other fronts are in an even more urgent situation.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Earthspeaker Naraat at the Eastern Earthshrine in Stormwind City for further instructions.

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: The False Warchief
passages.text:
Rend Blackhand was the son of an Orc Warchief. His father was slain by Orgrim Doomhammer, who became the new Warchief over the young orc. Rend now stands as the supposed leader of a false Horde of Blackrock orcs, backed by Nefarian and his army of dragons.

The fool claims that the Horde is also his by birthright, and threatens to take it by force! We cannot allow this to occur in light of his master's influence. Find him in the Upper Spire and bring an end to the false warchief, <class>.

passages.title: The False Warchief
passages.text:
You saw Nefarian when you fought Rend?

<Acride sighs.>

I wish I had accompanied you, then. I could have faced him unaware, outside his lair...but no matter. Nefarian will die by my claw.

You've done well.

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text:
Heya, <name>, Kelsey Steelspark down in Tanaris left a message for you. She says that the gnomes down there in Gadgetzan heard about what you've been doing up here.

Anyway, the Cataclysm hit them hard, too. Not as hard as us, but I'm certain they could use your help.

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text: Greetings and salutations, friend. Welcome to Tanaris!

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text:
Heya, <name>, Megs Dreadshredder down in Tanaris left a message for you. She says that the goblins down there in Gadgetzan heard about what you've been doing up here.

Anyway, the Cataclysm hit them hard, too. Not as hard as us, but I'm certain they could use your help.

Besides, that Megs is a hottie!

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text: Well hello there, <class>. Welcome to Tanaris!

passages.title: The Trek Continues
passages.text:
I believe the horses are ready. Argus Highbeacon, the gentleman who works with the Argent Crusade, spoke with me earlier. I understand he will be coming with us... that's great! I'll make room for him.

I know that you are busy, so there's no hurry. Whenever you're ready, hop into the caravan, and we will proceed to the next tower.

passages.title: The Trek Continues
passages.text: Once we get to Light's Shield Tower, the boys can head over to Light's Hope Chapel.  It's close enough that they can walk.

passages.title: The Trek Continues
passages.text: We've enjoyed having you ride with us, <name>.  Hopefully, once Gidwin and Tarenar join the Argent Crusade, we can continue to travel together.

passages.title: Honor and Strength
passages.text:
My name is Vex'tul, and I have watched you fight, <race>. You are strong.

You killed my master, Zaeldarr, but this does not bother me. I value strength over any loyalty that I held for him. I value strength over anything else.

Prove to me one final time your strength, <race>. Do so, and I will lend you MY strength for whatever purpose you may desire.

passages.title: Honor and Strength
passages.text: Honor means nothing.  Strength is everything.

passages.title: Honor and Strength
passages.text:
Yes, you are indeed strong... and I submit to you.

I will join you and your friend, the worgen.  My strength is yours.

passages.title: Boys Will Be Boys
passages.text:
As soon as we arrived here at Light's Shield Tower, those two lunkhead paladins ran off to Light's Hope Chapel. It's still a ways away, but if we're going to follow Argus along his tour of the towers, this is about as close as we're going to get.

Check in on them and make sure they're alright? I know they can handle themselves, but still, it'd make me feel better to know that you were watching over them while I'm stuck here with the caravan.

passages.title: Boys Will Be Boys
passages.text:
I can't believe it.  We're literally FEET away from becoming sworn members of the Argent Crusade.

We'd be in there already if it weren't for Tarenar's dallying.  If he doesn't quit chatting with the locals soon, I'm going to head in there myself.

passages.title: An Opportune Alliance
passages.text:
With your contributions to the food stores, my current assignment is complete.

I will be heading north, to the Plaguewood, next. I understand you may be headed in the same direction.

Do you mind if I join you on the road?

I will head northwest, to Eastwall Tower. If you're interested in teaming up, you can meet up with me there.

passages.title: An Opportune Alliance
passages.text:
You brought us a shaman!  From the Earthen Ring, no less!

I have no idea how we'll fit him in the caravan, but we'll find a way.  Welcome aboard, Rimblat Earthshatter!

passages.title: Smokey and the Bandage
passages.text:
Hey there! Interested in makin' a buck?

I need to get a bandage. Well, actually, I got a friend who needs to get a bandage. Well actually... let's just say it's complicated, but if you go get this bandage, you make money. And so do I. And my friend. Possibly other people.

Stephen Browman used to own the mill to the north, now he's dead. A zombie. The guy at the top wants to have the wrappings from Browman's body.

What's the matter, you don't like money?

passages.title: Smokey and the Bandage
passages.text: You've been fightin' undead.  Did ya find Browman?

passages.title: Smokey and the Bandage
passages.text: Well well well!  Someone who goes and gets things done!  Here's your cut, chief.  I'll be seein' you around.

passages.title: Argent Call: Northdale
passages.text:
Tyrosus has given us our next task: slaying more undead in Northdale. Gidwin is excited to move forward, but I think we should show a little more caution.

Let's meet up with Fiona. She should be at the next tower by now... Eastwall Tower, I think it's called. It's close by, to the northwest of Light's Hope. We can rest there, and plan our attack on Northdale.

passages.title: Argent Call: Northdale
passages.text:
Hello, <name>!  Glad to see you've rejoined the caravan!

Tarenar and Gidwin arrived here before you.  Tarenar's just right there, and Gidwin's... well... he's in a little bit of a mood right now.  I think he's in the tower.

passages.title: Friends on The Other Side
passages.text:
I come with news from Blackrock Spire. We have a new visitor. His name is Acride.

He seeks people of strength, people of intelligence, of dexterity. You ought to go to Blackrock Spire and speak with him.

passages.title: Friends on The Other Side
passages.text:
Hello, what is your business in a place like this?

I'm sorry, who sent you? I'm afraid I've never heard of such a dwarf.

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text:
It is no secret that we aren't fans of the orcs in Blackrock Mountain, but we do carefully watch their every move. Nothing happens in that Mountain without me knowing about it, <class>.

Recently, a different sort of orc came into Blackrock. He resides just inside Blackrock Spire, and I know he's somehow planning to overthrow Nefarian and his whole army of orcs. Normally I wouldn't trust their kind, but we share a common goal for the time being. Find him, he's called Acride.

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text:
Hello, what is your business in a place like this?

So Overseer Oilfist sent you? Listen carefully, we have much to discuss in little time.

passages.title: Blackrock Anomaly
passages.text:
There is an orc inside Blackrock Spire much unlike the others. He speaks with the intelligence and wisdom of one beyond his appeared years, and does not fight against our soldiers like the others do.

You must travel northwest to Blackrock Spire and find this orc, known only to us as Acride. Perhaps he is the key to stopping the orcish army. Perhaps we can stop Nefarian before it is too late...

passages.title: Blackrock Anomaly
passages.text:
Hello, what is your business in a place like this?

So you come at the will of Miss Brightwing, do you? Very interesting indeed.

passages.title: What's Shaking in Ironforge
passages.text: Things have grown worse in Ironforge, <name>. Please, speak with Stormcaller Mylra in Ironforge and see if you can lend a hand in some way.

passages.title: What's Shaking in Ironforge
passages.text: It is good that you've come, <name>.  We need all the help we can get with the situation here.

passages.title: Breaking the Barrier
passages.text:
While Godfrey and I make preparations for our assault upon Gilneas, I want you to lead our attack upon Ambermill, directly east of here.

The former Dalaran magi of Ambermill have erected a magical barrier that somehow cloaks them from vision. They currently reside within some type of pocket dimension, awaiting orders from the Alliance to begin their attack. We must prevent their assault by making a pre-emptive strike. Venture to Ambermill and find information that would grant us access to the mages.

passages.title: Breaking the Barrier
passages.text: Have you found anything yet?

passages.title: Breaking the Barrier
passages.text:
Clever mages. The codex is sealed by a magical ward.

Pity that they weren't clever enough to realize that former archmages of Dalaran are now Forsaken.

passages.title: Unyielding Servitors
passages.text:
The magi of Ambermill have employed foul magic to keep us away. Elemental servitors, created with immunities that we cannot breach, protect their territory.

Venture east to Ambermill and slay the unyielding elemental servitors that guard the town and recover their cores. Bring their cores back to me so that I may devise a method by which we are able to destroy them all!
