passages.title: Unyielding Servitors
passages.text: Have you recovered the servitor cores?

passages.title: Unyielding Servitors
passages.text: Well done, <name>. The praise the Banshee Queen lavishes upon you is apparently not unfounded.

passages.title: Relios the Relic Keeper
passages.text:
The Dark Lady is correct in her assertion that I am able to unlock the codex. Unfortunately, I need a signet ring from a Dalaran archmage to do it. My own ring was taken when I died many years ago, but there still might be a way.

While Dalaran has floated away, the outskirts of the city remain. Far to the east lie the ruins of Dalaran. It is there that you will find an archmage known as Relios. "Take" his signet ring and bring it back to me.

You may use the portal behind me to get to the crater.

passages.title: Relios the Relic Keeper
passages.text: Did you recover a Dalaran Archmage's Signet Ring?

passages.title: Relios the Relic Keeper
passages.text:
Perfect. I hope this wasn't too much trouble to come by, <name>. Relios was a pupil of mine back when I was a mortal man thereby making him a competent and formidable adversary. I suppose I could have warned you ahead of time.

Now, let us see the ring.

There we are...

passages.title: Ley Energies
passages.text: The arcane remnant pulses with strange energy. Perhaps you should search for more remnants. Surely Dalar would be interested in such a find.

passages.title: Ley Energies
passages.text: What's that you've got there, <name>?

passages.title: Ley Energies
passages.text: Smart boy! I can most definitely use these arcane remnants in my studies. Indeed, Dalaran was built upon a massive ley line. It's no wonder, then, that such things exist at the crater.

passages.title: Out of the Ziggurat
passages.text:
It is time that I asked a favor of you, <name>.

Far to the north of Eastwall Tower, hidden among the hills, is the Mossflayer capital city of Zul'Mashar. It was here that I was born, and here that I died.

The traitor, Thresh'jin, sits atop Zul'Mashar's ziggurat. It was my every right to be there, but he took the seat from me with treachery and deceit. He is not strong. He is weak.

I will meet you in Zul'Mashar, and we will kill him. Your strength and mine. Together.

passages.title: Out of the Ziggurat
passages.text: I have waited long for this day.

passages.title: Out of the Ziggurat
passages.text: My duty is not over yet.  In many ways, this was the easy step.

passages.title: Practical Vengeance
passages.text:
Under ordinary circumstances I am not a vengeful man. In fact, I am somewhat of a pragmatist. You see, practicality is a paradoxical notion to vengeance. Most revenge ploys are highly impractical.

BUT... in this case - since you're already going to the ruins of Dalaran - you might as well kill every Dalaran affiliated human that you see. The reasons that I want them dead range from hatred to anger to betrayal, but I assure you they are all legitimate gripes. Do this for me and I will pay you handsomely.

passages.title: Practical Vengeance
passages.text: I thought for sure that with the death of a dozen of my most hated enemies I would feel a great burden lifted from my shoulders. Sadly, I do not feel a thing. Perhaps I am a psychopath.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text:
I'm glad you're back! Saving the world or something, I'm sure.

I was dispatched to establish relations with the red dragons in the area, but I'm finding this bunch somewhat less accommodating than the ones at Wyrmrest were. I have, however, been told that you are the type that solves problems.

A problem solver as it were.

Care to take a crack at earning a bit of trust with Lirastrasza at Vermillion Redoubt to the southwest? Anything that might soften her up a bit for me would be lovely.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I believe Lira wanted a word with you.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I'm glad Lira didn't scare you off. I won't say her concerns aren't warranted, but we have a common enemy. She is perhaps a bit overzealous.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text:
Good. You're back. Saving the world again I assume.

I was dispatched to establish relations with the red dragons in the area, but I'm finding this bunch somewhat less accommodating than the ones at Wyrmrest were. I have, however, been told that you are the type that solves problems.

A problem solver as it were.

I need you to gain the trust of Lirastrasza at Vermillion Redoubt to the southwest. Our association with the Dragonmaw has complicated things, but I'm hoping you can ease relations.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I believe Lira wanted a word with you.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I'm glad Lira didn't scare you off. I won't say her concerns aren't warranted, but we have a common enemy. She is perhaps a bit overzealous.

passages.title: Impatience
passages.text:
Damn that dwarf. He's always getting me in trouble with Fiona. Look at her! She won't even TALK to me!

I'm going to stay here and try to mend my friendship with our worgen friend. Would you mind going out and making sure Gidwin is alright? I'm sure he's fine; he knows how to take care of himself. He headed north, and he can't have gone far.

passages.title: Impatience
passages.text: Northdale is home to a few ghosts and banshees.  Nothing ol' Giddy can't handle.

passages.title: Impatience
passages.text:
You didn't see him?  Where could he have gone then?

His... his prayer book?  Why would he leave that behind?

Oh...

By the Light, what have I done?

passages.title: Nobody to Blame but Myself
passages.text:
This is my fault. I... I ignored his warnings, his complaints, everything. I couldn't help myself - I saw those Scourge just beyond the tower, and I... I HAD to go kill them.

Argus says that Gidwin was taken northwest, and that's our only lead, so that's where we'll head.

Northdale and the Argent Crusade be damned! We're getting Gidwin back from those Scourge trash.

passages.title: Nobody to Blame but Myself
passages.text: We have no time, <name>!  We must press on!

passages.title: Nobody to Blame but Myself
passages.text:
Time is wasting, <name>.  Every minute we waste gives the Scourge another chance to kill Gidwin.  If he isn't dead already.

Not that I think he is.  Giddy may be a stick-in-the-mud, but when it comes down to it, he can swing the Light like a champion.

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text: As with any offensive, you first need to soften them up. We've been having a heck of a time getting in there. But someone like you... well, let's just say I have no doubt in my mind that you can get into the Twilight Gate to the southwest and teach the Bloodeye Clan ogres and ettins a thing or two!

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text:
What's the matter? You Alliance boys don't have the stomach to get the job done?

<Kurdran gives you a wink.>

Need me to fly over there and kill them for you?

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text: That's the spirit, lad! Today's already shaping up to be a good one.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
Now while the attack upon the Twilight Gate is launched, there is one last loose end to tie up: Za'brox and Beeble'phod, the disciples of Cho'gall.

Intelligence has placed them within the Den of the Disciples, a small ogre cave at the southwest corner of the Twilight Gate.

You're fairly certain that Cassius and Kurdran will want proof of their deaths.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text: Is that blood dripping from your pack?

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
<The paladin frowns.>

That's quite a gruesome trophy collection you have there. I would have believed you if you had simply said they were dead. Regardless, thank you for having the foresight to take care of them.

The Twilight Gate will soon be ours. Time to move up to the Twilight Citadel.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
Now while the attack upon the Twilight Gate is launched, there is one last loose end to tie up: Za'brox and Beeble'phod, the disciples of Cho'gall.

Intelligence has placed them within the Den of the Disciples, a small ogre cave at the southwest corner of the Twilight Gate.

You're fairly certain that Lady Cozwyn and Zaela will want proof of their deaths.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text: Is that blood dripping from your pack? I hope that it's not yours.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
<The noble lady grins wickedly.>

That's quite a gruesome trophy collection you have there. I would have believed you if you had simply said they were dead, though I do appreciate the extra effort. Thank you for having the foresight to take care of them.

The Twilight Gate will soon be ours. Time to move up to the Twilight Citadel.

passages.title: Even Dragons Bleed
passages.text:
I won't be so impolite as to refuse your aid if you're offering it.

We're locked in constant battle with the twilight drakes and dragons to the south. Our strikes have not been entirely without success, but the dragons coming out of Grim Batol have been breathing some kind of corruption upon us that takes time to cleanse.

Velastrasza and Baleflame are attending to our injured brothers. Go and see if you can be of help to them.

passages.title: Even Dragons Bleed
passages.text: Calen has become very trusting. It is not often that strangers are permitted within the redoubt.

passages.title: Life from Death
passages.text:
<race>, I have a task for you.

Take these ruby seeds and plant them at the corpses of any dragonkin that you come across. Twilight or Vermillion, whelping or dragon, it matters not. We need to see that their bodies are returned to the earth so that life can continue to flourish.

In death, there should always be new life. This may be our one consolation during times of war and great tragedy.

passages.title: Life from Death
passages.text: Have you done as I asked?

passages.title: Life from Death
passages.text: In this, we deny Deathwing the destruction that he so passionately seeks. In this, life continues.

passages.title: Encroaching Twilight
passages.text:
Fragile Twilight invaders litter the redoubt. They're pouring in from somewhere to the west.

There can be no mercy offered to them within this hallowed place. Whatever violence grips your moral heart, release it upon them.

passages.title: Encroaching Twilight
passages.text: You have a talent for killing I see. In times like these, that has its place.

passages.title: A Wolf in Bear's Clothing
passages.text:
These worgen take us for fools! One would think that only an idiot would mistake one of their druids in bear form as a real bear. Unfortunately, there are many idiots here at the Forsaken Front. We've already lost a few battalions to organized worgen bear attacks. Yes, it's even more idiotic than it sounds.

Directly east of here, heading towards Hillsbrad, you will find worgen druids roaming the woods, masquerading as bears. Kill them and make our southern supply line safe again.

passages.title: A Wolf in Bear's Clothing
passages.text: I only hope that we don't end up getting beat down by inconspicuous birds, cats and trees next... or seals. Could you imagine it?

passages.title: The Thrill of Discovery
passages.text:
What a find! And somehow it's all remained untouched by plunderers...

Listen, <name>. I need to document this site before we disturb anything. While I do, why don't you have a look around - you know, explore a bit. You've earned it.

Keep your eyes open for anything unusual.

Oh! And please... don't break anything, ok?

passages.title: The Thrill of Discovery
passages.text: Your exploration of the Chamber of the Stars has yielded more questions than answers...

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter I
passages.text:
<Sylvanas hands you the signet ring.>

Take the ring and make your way to Beren's Peril, southeast of here, located in a cave in the hills. Once there, search the cave for the portal to the pocket dimension that conceals the Ambermill magi.

I will communicate with you through your thoughts, <name>. Once you have reached the portal I will give you your marching orders.

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter I
passages.text: <The portal hums.>

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter I
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's voice invades your thoughts.>

Yes, this is it. Now run the ring along the runes of the portal and you should become attuned for transdimensional travel.

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter II
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's words float in your head.>

You are now ready to use the portal. Be warned, <name>, once you step through you will appear in another dimension at Ambermill. There will be a hundred, perhaps a thousand, magi waiting to kill you.

You must persevere and kill all in your path.

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter II
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's voice invades your thoughts.>

Excellent work, <name>. Now to eject them into our waiting hands!

passages.title: Roots'll Do 'Er
passages.text:
Look here, mate. She's on her last legs! If me bird dies, I'm as good as worthless.

So make yerself useful. Here on the peninsula you can dig up thorny stankroots. Oh the smell will knock you on yer patoot but steeped in water it'll boil up into a right powerful cure-all.

Gather some while I defend me bird. An' hurry! You Alliance wanks don't have a reputation for timely intervention, right?

passages.title: Roots'll Do 'Er
passages.text: Didja get me roots, <class>? Well?

passages.title: Roots'll Do 'Er
passages.text: Oh, that's the stuff all right! Hope ya didn't eat any. Gives you the cramps something awful but it does wonders for birds.

passages.title: Under the Choking Sands
passages.text:
No... it cannot be.

Orsis is all but buried beneath the desert sands.

The enemy will pay for this.

But first we must aid my people. Quick, <name>. We do not have much time before the last of my brethren are buried alive!

passages.title: Under the Choking Sands
passages.text:
I thank you, <name>.  Orsis was punished for not joining the forces of Deathwing.

Prince Nadun has offered my people refuge in his city.  I must go there and tend the survivors.

passages.title: Wretched Hive of Scum and Villainy
passages.text:
<race>... please, I ask your help.

Something's happened to my people. Our commander, Ranger Lord Hawkspear, came upon an item of magical energy, and my friends, my family... they succumbed to its seductive power.

They're corrupted, <race>. All of them.

My Ellaria wouldn't want to live like that, nor would any of my brothers. Please, put them out of their misery. Quel'lithien Lodge is not far; it's just up the hill, to the northwest.

passages.title: Wretched Hive of Scum and Villainy
passages.text: You have no idea how difficult it was for me to pull myself away, <race>.  I nearly ended up one of them.

passages.title: Wretched Hive of Scum and Villainy
passages.text: Do not feel sorry for me.  Those were my friends that you saw at Quel'lithien Lodge, but they were already as good as dead.

passages.title: Blind Fury
passages.text:
Tarenar wasn't joking when he said that he didn't care about judgment and caution. He nearly took off that high elf's head as he ran into the Plaguewood, looking for Gidwin. You should go after him.

The Plaguewood is a big place, <name>. Good luck. I hope to see you <boys/three> come out of the woods in one piece.

passages.title: Blind Fury
passages.text:
I haven't found anything but brainless undead, and plenty of them.  I was just about to kill my way into Stratholme when you arrived.

Did you have any more success?

passages.title: Guardians of Stratholme
passages.text:
Baroness Anastar holds him? Here in the Plaguewood?

The Plaguewood is a big place... but we will find him. We WILL find Gidwin.

Immediately to our east and our west are a pair of necropoli that flank the entrance to Stratholme. Inside them, you will find a pair of death knights - Rivendare's lieutenants. I doubt either would have any use for a paladin hostage, but perhaps they will have some information on his location.

passages.title: Guardians of Stratholme
passages.text: We're getting close.  I only hope it's not too late.

passages.title: Guardians of Stratholme
passages.text: We've got to keep moving!  We're getting so very close!

passages.title: Augustus' Receipt Book
passages.text:
I'm ready for business! What do you want?

Oh wait... I can't open up shop without my receipt book. How am I to keep track of things without my receipt book?

I must have left it in town somewhere. I had a room in the inn... the book must be there.

Bring me my book. Please, bring it to me! Bring me my book and you'll see! I'll set up shop and you'll see that my prices are INSANE!

passages.title: Augustus' Receipt Book
passages.text: Do you have my receipt book?  I can't wait to get back to business!

passages.title: Augustus' Receipt Book
passages.text:
There it is!  And oh my!  I forgot how full it was!

This is a glorious day, <name>!  Stupendous!  Insanely good, I say!

passages.title: Just a Little Touched
passages.text:
I like to check in on Augustus in Terrordale every once in a while, just to make sure he's alright. Some of us undead cope with the plague better than others, I suppose.

Terrordale is west of here. Would you mind checking in on him for me?

passages.title: Just a Little Touched
passages.text: You've come to the right place, mister!  No place better than Terrordale, yes siree, that's right!  The jewel of Lordaeron!

passages.title: Any Portal in a Storm
passages.text:
Our friends in the Earthen Ring have been trying to open portals back to Stormwind, with no luck. But Thordun here tells me he might just have the key.

The crazed water elementals in the nearby Verrall River Delta have been sent into a frenzy. Thordun tells me we can channel their energy into a portal.

I don't understand all this elemental-claptrap, but I understand one thing: killin' elementals and takin' their whirlpool cores. Deliver them to Talaa in the courtyard!

passages.title: Any Portal in a Storm
passages.text: Hello, <class>. Kurdran tells me you've got a solution to getting this portal opened?

passages.title: Any Portal in a Storm
passages.text:
My word, <name>. These elemental energies are so powerful, so chaotic - no wonder the Twilight's Hammer has chosen to build their stronghold here!

I should be able to channel these energies into something more benign and productive though. Let's give it a try...

passages.title: The Perfect Poultice
passages.text:
Are you goin' by way of the Verrall river delta? I've got a tip that'll help your men here... and my bird!

When water elementals carve their way through rock, they create a peculiar kind of muck. It dries hard as stone but carries with it the rejuvenating power of water. You make a cast out of that muck and broken bones knit together like iron.

Bring some of that muck to Talaa, your shaman downstairs. She'll know what to do with it!

passages.title: The Perfect Poultice
passages.text: What is this I keep hearing about the muck of the Verrall River?

passages.title: The Perfect Poultice
passages.text:
Oh... mud. You brought me mud?

Wow - this stuff oozes with power! I see what Thordun was saying, now. I'll distribute this to all of the healers. Our wounded will be on their feet in no time!

passages.title: The Wildhammer
passages.text:
No doubt you've felt the earthquakes. You may even have seen elementals attacking the lands or towns. The Earthen Ring struggles to understand what is going on. We've been fortunate to gain assistance from the Wildhammer shamans.

Gavan Grayfeather is in Stormwind Keep to help coordinate our efforts with the various faction leaders. Speak to him and see what you may learn about these events, <name>.

passages.title: The Wildhammer
passages.text:
Well met, <class>.  I am Gavan Grayfeather, emissary of the Wildhammer shaman.

There is much work to be done.  The leaders fear for their citizens, as many have turned to cults.  We shaman are concerned with the elemental unrest.

Our advice to you, <class>, is to be vigilant.  Help where you can, be it calming the people or putting the elementals at rest.  There is plenty to do.

passages.title: Cenarion Tenacity
passages.text:
Those druids never give up, I swear. I'd given up on the Plaguelands years ago, but the Cenarion Circle folks keep telling me that the land is not beyond hope.

The most recent visitor was a night elf, on her way to the Fungal Vale, to the north. She told me that these lands will make a full recovery, if we try hard enough. I'm not sure I believe her.

Do you buy this drivel? Maybe you and her should talk. She should still be up there.

passages.title: Cenarion Tenacity
passages.text:
I suppose I had better work on my stealth, if you were able to find me.

Are you interested in helping me heal the Plaguelands?

passages.title: Speak with Captain Anton
passages.text:
No doubt you've felt the earthquakes. You may even have seen elementals attacking the lands or towns. We have sent many of our brightest minds to Nagrand to commune with the elements.

But there is still much work to be done here. Stormwind Guards are being overwhelmed with citizens worried about their loved ones.

Please, <class>, speak with Captain Anton in Stormwind Keep and see how you might assist him.

passages.title: Speak with Captain Anton
passages.text: King's honor, <class>.  I am Captain Anton.  I am leading the investigation into the cultists that have appeared in Stormwind.

passages.title: Of No Consequence
passages.text:
Our forces in Pyrewood were recently taken by way of sneak attack. The 7th Legion managed to infiltrate the town with their scouts, ultimately decimating our troops.

The Dark Lady has tasked us with a rescue mission. We are to find survivors and get them out of Pyrewood safely. If any soldiers live they are likely worthless, but we do as the Dark Lady commands.

Let's get this nonsense over with, <name>. Pyrewood is directly southwest of the Forsaken Front.

passages.title: Of No Consequence
passages.text: The sooner we rescue survivors the sooner we can burn down the whole of Pyrewood.

passages.title: Of No Consequence
passages.text: What happened here today is between us. Say a word to anyone and you will find yourself in a corpse pit next to these poor fools.

passages.title: Lessons in Fear
passages.text:
Our enemies are becoming smarter - adapting to our tactics. Recently an attack was made upon Pyrewood Village, southwest of here. Our troops occupying the town were decimated, of course, but what made the attack especially interesting was the racial composition of the attacking force. No humans were used.

<Walden laughs.>

Rightfully, they fear being reanimated as Forsaken.

Let us teach the non-humans a lesson in fear. Together we will show them what happens to corpses that we cannot use.

passages.title: Lessons in Fear
passages.text: Pyrewood Village must be reduced to ashes and our enemies slain!

passages.title: Lessons in Fear
passages.text: I suspect we'll see fewer humans at the Battlefront. The risk for these cowards is too great.

passages.title: The Baroness' Missive
passages.text:
The note is from Baroness Anastari, and it describes a ritual that is about to happen in the Plaguewood's central slaughterhouse - just south of where Tarenar is at. This could be where they're holding Gidwin!

Tarenar will want to know about this... and quickly, before it's too late!

passages.title: The Baroness' Missive
passages.text: What?  Did you find something?

passages.title: The Baroness' Missive
passages.text:
This is it!  If this missive is to be believed, then he's literally right over this hill!

What are we waiting for, <name>?

passages.title: In Defense of the Redoubt
passages.text:
Calen sent word - the Twilight are within the redoubt!

If there will ever be a time when you can earn his favor, this is it!

passages.title: In Defense of the Redoubt
passages.text: I hope you're as tough as your gear suggests. The Twilight's Hammer have made their way within the redoubt somehow and I need someone to hunt them down.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text:
We've managed to infiltrate the Dark Iron Prison!

Well...we may have, anyway.

Kevin Dawson had the...honor...of seeing what was going on over there, and we haven't heard back from him since. You look like the type that doesn't like to die, you should go see if he's ok!

He's supposed to be inside the hall on the south end of the cavern ahead...though something tells me he may not have made it quite that far.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text:
I don't know how I'm still alive. The patrols keep walking past me like I'm not even here.

...Am I dead, <class>?

passages.title: A Gathering in Outland
passages.text:
Greetings, <class>. The elements have grown more restless and we seem to be making little progress to a solution for this problem. Some of our wisest shaman have gathered in Nagrand at the Throne of Elements to discuss what ails our land.

Head to the Throne of Elements and speak with Gavan Grayfeather, he will surely have some task for you.

passages.title: A Gathering in Outland
passages.text: It is good to see you, <name>.  Here at the Throne of Elements we may be able to uncover what ails Azeroth.

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text:
This is a little hard to believe, but there are Twilight's Hammer members here in Blackrock Depths! I don't know how many there are crawling throughout this place, but I did hear that their lead interrogator, Gerstahn, is in this hallway.

I don't know what they're here torturing for, but maybe you can find out by confronting Gerstahn?

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: Go! Go! Go!

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: I see...she did not cooperate. Hopefully we can still stop them before something else terrible happens.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text:
Can ye keep a secret? I have a secret tae share with ye if ye can.

Everybody here is CRAZY!!!

There's goblins over there, Dark Irons right over there, and a giant living fire thing right past this gate! An' that's just what I see in this little cave!

And ye! What're ye doin' here!?

Oh, I see. Winky sent ye, did he? Sent ye tae talk t' Prospector Seymour, past this gate and t' the right, did he? Well go! Oralius doesn't even care!

...I'll GET YOU FOR THIS WINKY!!!

<Oralius begins to sob.>

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text:
I would stay away from Oralius. Far, far, far away. He isn't quite right in the head.

Now, let's get onto business!

passages.title: Dark Iron Tacticians
passages.text:
General Angerforge and Golem Lord Argelmach lead the Dark Iron armies and their golems against us. If we are to overcome them, the two must be slain.

Go through this door and unlock The Shadowforge Lock, which separates the East and West Garrisons. Then, follow the stairs and keep to the left at the top until you reach the West Garrison. It is there you will find the General and Golem Lord.

Keep your wits about you, they are both well-seasoned combatants. Find Mayara Brightwing should you succeed.

passages.title: Dark Iron Tacticians
passages.text:
I'm sure you are up to the task I have for you if you've made it this far in one piece.

<Mayara Brightwing lowers her voice to a whisper.>

Between you and me, you may want to enjoy yourself in the Grim Guzzler while you're there. It could be the last drink you ever have.

passages.title: The Situation So Far
passages.text:
No doubt you've felt the earthquakes. You may even have seen elementals attacking the lands or towns. The Earthen Ring struggles to understand what is going on. We've been fortunate to have one of the greatest shaman as our Warchief.

Thrall has been consulting with his advisors, and we don't want to interrupt his council. But perhaps our brother, Gotura Fourwinds, has learned of Thrall's plans.

passages.title: The Situation So Far
passages.text:
Greetings, <class>.  The situation here is tense.  The elements are restless and the people are scared and confused.  The Warchief is trying to find a semblance of balance between leading the people and protecting Azeroth.  Though it seems he will soon be leaving us to travel to Nagrand and gain insight about the elementals.

Regardless of the Warchief's choice, we still must do what we can.  Help calm the populace, scour the lands for rogue elementals.  These tasks will surely help our cause.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
Some say that the Grim Guzzler is the secret to the Dark Iron war effort. Their warriors recharge there and emerge thirsty for another innocent soul. I think we can seriously hinder them by causing a bit of chaos here.

I need you to start a fight with three of the bar's infamous patrons. Damage the kegs and Hurley Blackbreath will come running. Steal items off the tables near Plugger Spazzring and he'll fight. As for Ribbly Screwspigot...just talk to the little hothead. Report to Orfus when you're done.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text: Hurry, please. Time is not a luxury we currently have.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
The Dark Irons took our Thunderbrew. I'll never let them live after that. I'd kill 'em all myself if I could!

However, look ahead and you'll see we have slightly more dire matters to attend to at the moment.

passages.title: A Gathering in Outland
passages.text:
Greetings, <class>. The elements have grown more restless and we seem to be making little progress to a solution for this problem. Some of our wisest shaman have gathered in Nagrand at the Throne of Elements to discuss what ails our land.

Head to the Throne of Elements and speak with our Warchief, he will surely have some task for you.

passages.title: A Gathering in Outland
passages.text: It is good to see you, <class>.  Here at the Throne of Elements we may be able to uncover what ails Azeroth.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text:
Ahead is the creature known only as Ambassador Flamelash. He is the ambassador to the Dark Iron Nation from Ragnaros the Firelord. Beyond that chamber is the Summoners' Tomb, home to the spirits of the seven Dark Iron patriarchs who summoned Ragnaros into our world.

You may not know of the Great Fire, but he will be the end of Azeroth if he is not stopped, and these individuals are directly tied to his hold over the Dark Iron. Slay them, so that this nation may perhaps one day be redeemed.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text: I cannot proceed any further alone, regardless of my combat experience. The Lyceum has proven too difficult for me. If you are here, though...you might be the key to all of this.

passages.title: Patchwork Command
passages.text:
Recent events make it even more apparent that holing up here and making sporadic attacks isn't enough to keep our kind safe, much less retake Grim Batol. We need to be more aggressive, we need to strike into their heart.

I've agreed to send dragons to the aid of your commanders. They were already hatching a plan to strike at Grim Batol, so you should focus your attention there first.

You should be able to find Patch in Dragonmaw Pass, in the canyon below us to the south.

passages.title: Patchwork Command
passages.text:
You got the dragons in the game! Good on you.

We'd already laid out plans for our ambush by the time the dragons contacted us. They're helping by cutting off their retreat.

It's not too late for you to join in on the fun though. We saved some for you.

passages.title: 7th Legion Battle Plans
passages.text:
While destroying Pyrewood will certainly garner us an advantage over the Alliance upon the field of battle, our true purpose here is to leave them crippled.

Southwest of here, near the Greymane Wall, lies the 7th Legion Base Camp. We must search the base camp for battle plans. With the 7th Legion battle plans we will be able to pinpoint all Alliance troop advancement in Silverpine Forest.

passages.title: 7th Legion Battle Plans
passages.text: Search every filthy dwarven corpse.

passages.title: 7th Legion Battle Plans
passages.text:
<Walden flips through the battle plan.>

It looks like the reinforcements from the ships in Gilneas are marching soon. Crowley and Bloodfang have set up an encampment to the southeast for the Gilneas Liberation front.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text:
Da Twilight's Hammer be here for some reason. We don't know why, but Thal'trak be lettin' you in on a lil' secret of ours - da rogue Lexlort waits outside da hall where High Interrogator Gerstahn be so he can kill her if he gets da chance.

She's too smart for dat, though, so you gonna go in an' do it, ya? Go talk to Lexlort and let him know. I'm sure he be ok with it.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text: Get over here. If you blow my cover, I swear to the Warchief I'll kill you where you stand.

passages.title: Sowing Discord
passages.text: The Alliance reinforcements have established a foothold in the southwest region of Silverpine called 7th Legion Base Camp. Our primary goal at the base camp is to sow discord amongst the troops. This is a lightning fast assassination mission to kill their field commander, General Marstone. His death won't stop the Alliance advance, but it will certainly soften their ranks.

passages.title: Sowing Discord
passages.text: Marstone is a decorated field general. He will not go down easy.

passages.title: Sowing Discord
passages.text: The rest of the Alliance fleet will arrive shortly, only to find their base camp decimated. Now for the second and most important part of our battle plan.

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text:
Gerstahn is too heavily guarded and too smart to leave her post, so I'm not going to kill her.

You are.

I'll throw in a little something I picked up off of a guard to make it worth your while.

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: Does it look like I want to be waiting her any longer than is necessary?

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: The Twilight's Hammer's presence only complicates our mission here further, but you've done your part for now.  You've earned a reward for your efforts...and some rest. Let's get out of here.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text:
We're fighting a losing battle right now, I'm afraid. The Dark Irons would be difficult to defeat on their own, but their elemental allies have given them new bleeding edge warriors that we simply can't compete with.

I need you to help us infiltrate their domain and kill as many of their vital leaders as possible. Hopefully that will shock their forces and turn the tide in our favor. Report to Razal'blade for further instruction. He's stationed beyond this gate and to the right.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text: Beyond this door lies the commander of the Dark Iron Army, surrounded by trained soldiers. Are you up for a little killing?

passages.title: The 109th Division
passages.text:
General Angerforge and Golem Lord Argelmach are directly responsible for the horrific slaughter of the 109th Division of the Kargath Expeditionary Force. There were a lot of good trolls and orcs in that division, many of them my close friends.

Well, young <race>, it's time for our fallen brothers to at last have their revenge.

Unlock The Shadowforge Lock, go up the stairs and bear left until you reach the West Garrison. Kill Angerforge and Argelmach, and don't you dare show them any mercy.

passages.title: The 109th Division
passages.text: I'm quite surprised to see you here! You'll be very useful indeed.

passages.title: The 109th Division
passages.text:
Up ahead is the Grim Guzzler. A disgusting bar full of all our enemies, intoxicated and therefore unfit for proper battle.

<Hierophant Theodora Mulvadania grins.>

Ripe for the slaughter.

passages.title: Maliciously Delicious
passages.text:
You know, I've got a problem you might be able to help me out with, here.

See, in addition to the fine pursuit of arms dealing, I'm trying to liven up the entertainment here in Bogpaddle. Apparently there's a bunch of these makrura things in the north waters that don't take kindly to the wild beach parties we've been throwing.

Joke's on them. I'm not gonna be pushed around by giant lobsters; they're my next source of revenue! You bring me some of their tails and we'll turn a problem into profit.

passages.title: Maliciously Delicious
passages.text: You got those tails? Don't be tryin' to push no hacked-up ones on me!

passages.title: Maliciously Delicious
passages.text:
I can see it now: our own famous Bogpaddle Lobster-Poppers! Made fresh from the sea! Oh, it's like this stuff writes itself...

Your help is very much appreciated, my friend. I'll start seeing if I can't cut your people a favorable arrangement, eh?

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
Everyone inside the Grim Guzzler is absolutely hammered and, therefore, easily angered. I think we can seriously hinder the Dark Irons by causing a bit of chaos here.

I need you to start a fight with three of the bar's infamous patrons. Damage the kegs and Hurley Blackbreath will come running. Steal items off the tables near Plugger Spazzring and he'll fight. As for Ribbly Screwspigot...just talk to the little hothead. Report to Thunderheart when you're done.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text: Hurry, please. Time is not a luxury we currently have.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
I hear quite the commotion coming from the Grim Guzzler. I see you've been hard at work.

If you'll direct your attention opposite me, you'll notice that we have bigger issues to worry about than toying with drunkards.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text:
Inside this chamber lies Ambassador Flamelash. He is the ambassador to the Dark Iron Nation from Ragnaros the Firelord. Beyond that chamber is the Summoners' Tomb, home to the spirits of the seven Dark Iron patriarchs who summoned Ragnaros into our world.

You may not know of the Great Fire, but he will be the end of Azeroth if he is not stopped, and these individuals are directly tied to his hold over the Dark Iron. Slay them all, and may this unholy union cease.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text: I cannot proceed any further alone, regardless of my combat experience. The Lyceum has proven too difficult for me. If you are here, though...you might be the key to all of this.

passages.title: The Prophet Hadassi
passages.text:
Prophet Hadassi is the wisest and eldest member of the Orsis tribe.

He has not been accounted for and his well-being is of vital importance.

Go into Orsis and find him. A great day of reckoning will come to the Al'Akir's lackeys if he's been hurt.

passages.title: The Prophet Hadassi
passages.text: Who... who are you?  Sent here... to rescue my people and fight our enemies.

passages.title: The Heart of the Mountain
passages.text:
For years I have sought a certain gem. It is called the Heart of the Mountain and it's the size of your fist! The Dark Iron dwarves have it locked in their vault and, try as I may, they won't let me purchase it.

So I must resort to force.

Fight your way to The Black Vault near the Hall of Crafting, breach its secret safe and gain the Heart. To do that, you must defeat Watchman Doomgrip, and he won't appear until you've opened every relic coffer in the vault!

Good luck.

passages.title: The Heart of the Mountain
passages.text: Do you have the Heart of the Mountain?  To me, its value is without limit.

passages.title: The Heart of the Mountain
passages.text:
You have the heart!  Amazing!  It is even more beautiful than I imagined!

Please, <name>, take this as payment!

passages.title: Crazy Larry
passages.text:
You're gettin' it, <name>. You scratch my back, I scratch yours. Well, more like I scratch the back of your whole army, and just a little harder than the backs of the other side! Was that too complicated?

What I'm sayin' is, that's a lot of backs. So I'm gonna have to ask you to scratch mine a few more times. Whoever stole those landmines may have just hit our boys on the eastern shore.

Head to our camp to the southeast and check on Crazy Larry; he'll fill you in when you get there.

passages.title: Crazy Larry
passages.text:
Silversnap sent you?! I'm DOOMED!

Oh, he sent you to help me! That's different, haha!

passages.title: Kill Gil
passages.text:
Gilblins!

<Larry stares at you silently for a while.>

You never seen a gilblin before? They're crazy! Crazier than me! I just blow stuff up for a living, these guys are WHACKED!

Dunno where they came from, but they're like awful fish goblins! Gills and everything! They wiped out all my men down at the beach, and they took our shipping freighter!

You gotta help! They're just down to the east, go on and get rid of those gilblins!

passages.title: Kill Gil
passages.text: That'll show those fish-faced freaks! Good work!

passages.title: The Prophet's Dying Words
passages.text:
We... are... bound by oath... to protect the scepter of Orsis.

Listen, <class>, I don't have much time... left.

Find the sacred receptacle... in the southern end of the city.

Do not... let it... fall into their... hands...

passages.title: The Prophet's Dying Words
passages.text: Though the chest is locked, there is a plaque bearing interesting hieroglyphs above it.

passages.title: The Sealed Gate
passages.text:
At one end of the Dark Iron Highway stands a massive gate much like the one that protects Shadowforge City on the opposite side. However, we have no idea what's behind it!

All we know is that it's heavily guarded by Anvilrage patrols and the molten giant Bael'gar. You simply must dispose of them and see if you can pry that gate open!

Just imagine what could lie behind it...there could be an entire other half of the city we never knew about! Or nothing! Who knows!

Though, it's probably something...

passages.title: The Sealed Gate
passages.text: Were you able to get past the gate? Or scale it? What's behind it???

passages.title: The Sealed Gate
passages.text:
Darn it! I simply HAVE to know what's behind that gate! This could be the discovery that makes my career, you know!

Hmm....maybe a couple good explosions would do the trick...

passages.title: Jammal'an the Prophet
passages.text:
Jammal'an the Prophet, leader of the Atal'ai and Hakkari trolls, has obtained a small amount of Hakkar the Soulflayer's blood. They are injecting it into the green dragons to use their bodies to produce the massive quantities of blood necessary to summon Hakkar into our world.

We cannot allow this to come to pass. Slaughter Jammal'an and his priests before they get any further in their efforts!

passages.title: Jammal'an the Prophet
passages.text: Were you able to kill Jammal'an? I'll need proof that the deed is done.

passages.title: Jammal'an the Prophet
passages.text: Excellent! I suspect that without Jammal'an's leadership, the trolls will fall to infighting and Hakkar will never set his eyes upon our world.

passages.title: Eranikus
passages.text:
The Hakkar blood the Atal'ai have been injecting into the green dragons has had devastating effects on the dragons themselves. It appears that these dragons, former jailors of the Atal'ai, have been corrupted by its presence in their bodies and have become creatures of Nightmare.

Eranikus, Ysera's primary consort and lead watcher over the temple, was infused with the largest quantities of blood and has become twisted beyond imagination. After Jammal'an is dead, find Eranikus and end him.

passages.title: Eranikus
passages.text: Did you defeat Eranikus?

passages.title: Eranikus
passages.text:
You only defeated Eranikus' Shade? This is most troubling...

Let us hope that his full form does not still exist outside the Temple. Only Ysera herself is stronger than him in our flight.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
We're about to launch the attack upon the Twilight Gate, but there is one last loose end to tie up: Za'brox and Beeble'phod, the disciples of Cho'gall.

Intelligence has placed them within the Den of the Disciples, a small ogre cave at the southwest corner of the Twilight Gate.

Would you go back in there and kill them?

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text: Is that blood dripping from your pack?

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
<The paladin frowns.>

That's quite a gruesome trophy collection you have there. I would have believed you if you had simply said they were dead. Regardless, thank you for having the foresight to take care of them.

The Twilight Gate will soon be ours. Time to move up to the Twilight Citadel.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
Now, while we're about to launch the attack upon the Twilight Gate, there is one last loose end to tie up: Za'brox and Beeble'phod, the disciples of Cho'gall.

Intelligence has placed them within the Den of the Disciples, a small ogre cave at the southwest corner of the Twilight Gate.

Please head back in and kill them.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text: Is that blood dripping from your pack? I hope that it's not yours.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
<The noble lady grins wickedly.>

That's quite a gruesome trophy collection you have there. I would have believed you if you had simply said they were dead, though I do appreciate the extra effort. Thank you for having the foresight to take care of them.

The Twilight Gate will soon be ours. Time to move up to the Twilight Citadel.

passages.title: The Wrathcaster
passages.text:
One of the more vile members of the Scarlet Crusade, Mataus the Wrathcaster, lurks within the barracks' dungeon. Undeath suits his dark manner.

Were I younger and on the front lines, I'd run him through myself. As things are, I'm left behind to lead our forces from the rear. So I leave the pleasure to you.

passages.title: The Wrathcaster
passages.text: You are well on your way to becoming a true champion of the Light, <name>.  Well done.

passages.title: The Huntsman
passages.text:
We've already lost half a dozen men to a hail of bullets and arrows coming from atop this fortress. I haven't seen the face of the enemy that's firing, but I don't need to. I know the name of the man up there.

Leopold.

That's right, there's only one man up there, picking off my men one-by-one. And from what I can see, there's only one of you.

Sounds like a fair fight to me.

passages.title: The Huntsman
passages.text: If it were up to me, I'd throw him off the edge of the tower.

passages.title: The Huntsman
passages.text: One less thing to worry about.  Nice work up there.

passages.title: The Commander
passages.text:
Scarlet Commander Marjhan is cunning, shrewd, and willing to do anything to win a battle. Before all these things, however, she is loyal.

I have no doubt you'll find her in the barracks' central chamber, fighting under a crimson banner, until she either wins or dies.

Make sure it's the latter.

passages.title: The Commander
passages.text: Good, good.  These barracks are as good as fallen.

passages.title: Like Rats
passages.text:
Well, I'm glad that Eligor and Korfax left some fun for me. It was a battle unto itself to keep them from rushing headlong into the middle of this cathedral.

That's YOUR job, after all.

The cathedral lies ahead of us, the last real bastion of Scarlet power remaining. Within it, Crusader Lord Valdelmar sits atop Tyr's Hand's crumbling pulpit of lies.

There will be no escape; there will be no mercy. The last simpering vestiges of the Scarlet Crusade end here. Slay him.

passages.title: Like Rats
passages.text:
While I can't agree with their methods, I can't argue with their results.  In many ways, the Scarlet were well-intentioned, but their zeal grew too strong, and their hate blinded them to reason.

I only hope that the same doesn't happen to our Brotherhood of Light.

passages.title: In Defense of Quel'Danil
passages.text:
The undead are here! The Forsaken! They've been moving closer and closer, but to launch an all-out attack on us... those horrid abominations!

The young draenei I was charged with have trained with the Highvale elves in combat. They are not defenseless, but they need help!

Please, <name>, assist them! Drive back the Forsaken!

passages.title: In Defense of Quel'Danil
passages.text: Such aberrations in the face of the light... You are brave to face them, <name>.

passages.title: Just a Fancy Cockroach
passages.text:
Evidently, the ancient statues were home to various species of scarab.

Determined to leave this site in the best condition possible, you resolve to ridding the chamber of these pests.

passages.title: Send Word to Phaoris
passages.text:
Hurry, <name>. We must speak to my brother, the king.

He is bent on averting war with Al'Akir and the Neferset. He has foolish hopes that there is a diplomatic solution to this problem.

Maybe once he hears what occurred here he will see reason.

passages.title: Send Word to Phaoris
passages.text: This is just the beginning, <name>.  If Deathwing's minions can bury entire cities, we have little chance of defeating them through conventional means.

passages.title: The Vizier's Vote
passages.text:
Getting Vizier Tanotep to go against my brother's wishes is going to be extremely difficult. His very position is based on enforcing the will of Phaoris.

I've had little luck making the case for open war against Neferset.

Nevertheless you must speak to him. Perhaps he will listen to an outsider's perspective.

You will find the Vizier at the Akhenet Fields on official business.

passages.title: The Vizier's Vote
passages.text:
What manner of creature are you?  You will leave the king's lands before...

Wait!  You are that <name> I've heard so much about.

You must pardon my lack of hospitality.  We have seen all manner of hostile intruders since the barrier around Uldum failed.

passages.title: The High Priest's Vote
passages.text:
High Priest Amet's vote is the only one that is completely outside of our control.

He will vote as his divinations tell him and nothing we do will dissuade him.

I figure that gives us even odds either way.

The only problem we face is that his clairvoyance has failed him ever since the barriers around Uldum fell.

He will not cast a vote unless he regains power over his divinations.

Take the stairs at either side of the Vir'naal Dam and Speak to him to see what you can do to help.

passages.title: The High Priest's Vote
passages.text:
War, you say.

Divinations for war are always difficult.  Some wars must never be fought, even if victory was assured.  Some wars have to be waged even if defeat is certain.

passages.title: The High Commander's Vote
passages.text:
If we're to pass a resolution for war, the high council's vote needs to be unanimous.

I'm certain High Commander Kamses will give us his vote once he hears about what happened at Orsis.

Please speak to him in Ramkahen and make sure that's the case. I must make preparations in case our plan fails.

passages.title: The High Commander's Vote
passages.text:
No need to fill me in on the events in Orsis, <name>.

I've heard about them already.  And about you.  Any enemy of Al'Akir is a friend of mine.

passages.title: Tanotep's Son
passages.text:
I have devoted my life to serving the King. That service is unrivaled in importance by anything... with one exception: my son.

Tahet was captured by Neferset sentries.

They claim my son was trespassing upon their territory. Phaoris is attempting to negotiate his release... but I fear for the worst.

If you were to find Tahet, I would pledge my vote to you.

I do not know where they take the prisoners, but I've seen the guards consult maps to guide them through the thick vegetation.

passages.title: Tanotep's Son
passages.text: This might be the map you're after.

passages.title: Tanotep's Son
passages.text: You've obtained a map of the Vir'Naal river delta.

passages.title: The Blood God Hakkar
passages.text:
Hakkar... The mere mention of The Soulflayer's name will send many running. In the Sanctum of the Fallen God the Atal'ai have recovered a significant portion of his skeleton and seek to restore him to life. Already his children have begun to show up in the area.

Place this egg in that sanctum, and it will force his summoning prematurely. <name>, do not hesitate. Strike once his avatar appears!

passages.title: The Blood God Hakkar
passages.text:
You have successfully stopped Hakkar here, but I fear we are far from done. The Atal'ai transported most of the blood they produced to Zul'Gurub, where the Hakkari work to summon The Blood God there.

<name>, I do not think that this was ever meant to be the place of Hakkar's arrival - it was merely a test to see if the blood was potent enough! Hakkar can only be summoned in Zul'Gurub...and I fear we may be too late to stop the Hakkari with the blood they now have in their possession.

passages.title: Decontamination
passages.text:
You've been down here in Gnomeregan for a long time, <name>, and it's amazing that you've survived and kept your wits so long! We need to get you out.

Before we can send you to the surface to join the rest of the gnomes, you have to go through the decontamination process. Just head into the next room and board the Sanitron 500. It will do the rest! It shouldn't even hurt... much.

When you're all done, check in with Technician Braggle and he'll make sure you get some suitable gear.

passages.title: Decontamination
passages.text: There, now you're fit to head off to the surface and start your new life. The High Tinker will be delighted to hear of your arrival.

passages.title: Dunwalds Don't Die
passages.text:
As I understand it, you're to be looking to bring the Wildhammer clans together with the Alliance for war. Not sure you know what you're gettin' into.

Anyway, if it's battle you're preparin' for, there's definitely one family you want by your side. Head southwest, to the opposite side of the Crucible of Carnage, and there you'll find Clan Dunwald's ruins. They're rightly ravaged, but that's not likely to be stoppin' the Dunwalds. It's just a matter of findin' them.

passages.title: Dunwalds Don't Die
passages.text: If it's Dunwalds you be lookin' for, it's Dunwalds you've found. A couple of'm anyway. I can't find me other brothers for the life of me.

passages.title: While Meeting The Family
passages.text:
Hey there, <lad/lass>. I'm sure Keely's got you worrying about our brothers, but they can take care of themselves. They'll find their way back here one way or another.

Maybe you can do me a favor while you're out meeting the family... Dunwald territory is still infested with Twilight's Hammer and their servants. I'd appreciate it if you could remind them that they're not welcome.

passages.title: While Meeting The Family
passages.text: Now that's what I'm talkin' about lad. My kinda <race>.

passages.title: Sifting Through The Wreckage
passages.text:
The Twilight's Hammer were damn thorough when they sacked our town. Me and me brothers may well be the only ones that held'm back. I gotta be sure though.

As you're siftin' through the ruins, keep an eye out for the bodies of me kinsmen. I wanna know if dere were any survivors... or if it seems like some might have gotten away.

passages.title: Sifting Through The Wreckage
passages.text:
That many dead, eh? Not seemin' likely that anyone outside of me brothers fought through it then. I guess I already expected as much.

Thanks for takin' the time to look for me.

passages.title: Donnelly Dunwald
passages.text:
So you be lookin' to find us, and I be lookin' to find me brothers. It sounds to me like we got some common ground in there abouts.

Donnelly's our eldest, and while his size shows it, his wits might not. He's usually up in the northern ruins - in the hovel. Do ya think you might go lookin' for him for me? It'd be a right comfort if I knew he were safe.

passages.title: Donnelly Dunwald
passages.text:
Hi friend! I don't think I know you... I'm Donnelly Dunwald.

What's your name? I don't think I know you... Do I know you?

passages.title: Eoin Dunwald
passages.text:
Eoin's one of the twins. He's got a penchant for the drink. You'll likely be findin' him over by the old well - the ale stores were in a building there.

Mind making him to pay his worrying sister a visit? Shouldn't take much convincin' if you can get to the ale first.

passages.title: Eoin Dunwald
passages.text: Of all the buildings in all the towns to collapse, why'd it have to be this one?!

passages.title: Cayden Dunwald
passages.text:
Cayden's the other twin. He's got a thirst too, but not for ale. I'm sure he's been havin' a grand time of it since the Twilight came to our doorstep. Gettin' some of that aggression out of his system mayhaps.

I'm thinkin' the best place to go lookin for him is at market row, by the old smithy. He used ta hang out there anyway, but since that place is swarmin' with the most Twilight, he's probably got all the more reason to be callin' it home now.

Bring'm back for me. In one piece would be nice.

passages.title: Cayden Dunwald
passages.text:
Well look at ya, all geared and fancy. Keely send you to keep an eye on old Cayden, eh? Won't be needin' it. I got these louts handled.

Hahah! They chose the wrong dwarf to be ambushin' today! Ahahahahah!

passages.title: Finding Beak
passages.text:
I lost me gryphon. Beak! Where are you Beak?!

Wanna help me find him? I know he's in da hovel. He hasta be.

Beak?! Wheres are ya?

I hope he's okay.

passages.title: Finding Beak
passages.text: Did you find'm?! Please?

passages.title: Finding Beak
passages.text:
You found'm! You found Beak! I like you, new friend!

I'm gonna go show Keely. Keely like Beak too.

passages.title: Anything But Water
passages.text:
Look, buddy. Either you're here to help me find some drink, or you're in the way.

Why don't ya go down to the old storehouse and look downstairs. I had a mighty suspicion that ol' bookkeeper up in there was sneaking sips between pages. I bet he has a keg in his basement!

If ya find anything, come straight back to me! No dallyin'... this is urgent!

passages.title: Anything But Water
passages.text: You stink of sober! Find me some drink!

passages.title: Anything But Water
passages.text:
Donnelly's belly! That's more like it. Good to not be dyin' of the thirst again.

Here, have some. Good ol' Eoin's never so impolite as ta not share!

passages.title: A Steady Supply
passages.text:
Hey bud. Seeing as how you're so friendly and great and all, think you might do a dwarf a favor?

These are Dunwald ruins... there's SURE to be more stock in some of these buildings. If you come upon more ale, bring it my way, will ya? A good dwarf can never have enough!

I'm thinkin' I'll find my way back to Keely, so ya might have to hunt me down, but I'll try'n make it worth it to ya.

passages.title: A Steady Supply
passages.text: Where's me booze?

passages.title: A Steady Supply
passages.text:
Woooooh! That's exactly what my belly needs!

You get me all the nice things.

passages.title: Home Again
passages.text: Ya should find Keely. She'll be eager for word.

passages.title: Home Again
passages.text:
Thank you for bandin' my brothers back together. I know they're tough, but they're even tougher when they're side by side, and there's a lot of Twilight out there.

You're good to put a gal's heart at ease.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
Even I get hunted. I suppose that's what I get for hiding amongst the sheep.

<Mathias studies you for a moment.>

The Twilight's Hammer has taken it up a notch and sent their dark assassins after me. Nice bunch of guys. Dead now. They're made from the souls of the most skilled killers.

Want to do me a favor? Hunt them down. Bring back their soul pendants.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text: How many pendants do you have?

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
I'm not sure what I'm going to do with all of these. I'll probably fence them and donate the proceeds to the Stormwind orphanage.

Now to find someone sick enough to buy such a thing. It'll probably be a goblin. Or, a gnome warlock.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
Even I get hunted, <class>. But that's part of the fun of hiding amongst the sheep.

<Garona studies you for a moment.>

The Twilight's Hammer has taken it up a notch and sent their dark assassins after me. Nice for a group of dead guys. They're made from the souls of only the most skilled killers.

Do me a favor? Hunt them down.

They wear their souls in pendants about their necks. Bring them back to me. Souls optional.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text: How many pendants do you have?

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
What do you think I should do with all of these? Maybe I'll melt them down and have the metal imbued into a new dagger that I can thrust into Cho'gall's chest.

Think there's time for that?

passages.title: Croc-Out
passages.text:
The Stagalbog east of town is swarming with crocolisks. Swarming, you hear me? I've sold every bit of crocolisk you could imagine.

Crocolisk hides, teeth, tails, tongues, eyes, you name it. My point is, they ain't sellin' anymore. There's too many crocs! We're over-supplied and under-demanded.

So since they're of no use to me, and they occasionally eat my guests, I need you to just kill the suckers. Do me the favor, eh? I'll be here negotiatin' things with your people.

passages.title: Croc-Out
passages.text:
All taken care of? Good to hear. Takes a load off my mind.

Now I can focus on proper business for the fine folk of Marshtide and Stonard, weary from the war... and all that junk.

passages.title: Fire the Cannon
passages.text:
My arch-nemesis, Lord Cannon, has foolishly decided to throw his allegiance to the Twilight's Hammer.

In the past, we've coexisted with a shaky truce, but his change of heart leaves me little choice but to put an end to him. Or, I should say, if you want the information that you seek from the dead dwarf, you're going to kill Lord Cannon for me.

Seek him at Cannon's Inferno to the southeast.

passages.title: Fire the Cannon
passages.text:
I am pleased. Lord Cannon was always an unworthy adversary.

Very well, <race>, I will help you gain the information which you seek.

passages.title: Tastes Like Strider
passages.text:
You there! Yes, you! You want a good word put in with the Trade Baron? Give me a hand!

I heard you're the one that got all those makrura tails. They're wonderful, but not enough for proper swamp food. I need drumsticks for my gumbo!

There's plenty of swampstriders just outside town in the Sorrowmurk. I want the biggest drumsticks you can find!

passages.title: Tastes Like Strider
passages.text: Have you got those drumsticks?

passages.title: Tastes Like Strider
passages.text: Ah, good, good! Just what I needed.

passages.title: Pinned Down
passages.text:
My name is Nevin Twistwrench and I'm the commander of the Survivor Assistance Facilitation Expedition, or S.A.F.E.

I don't know how you managed to survive the radiation down here, <name>, but most of the others haven't fared so well. My team is rounding up the survivors, but the radiation-addled leper gnomes are too numerous for us to hold back much longer. They've lost their minds!

If you're still strong enough to wield a weapon or cast a spell, would you help us clear out some of these leper gnomes?

passages.title: Pinned Down
passages.text: Help my men get the way cleared out so we can help the other survivors get out of here!

passages.title: Pinned Down
passages.text: Well done, <name>. My men can take it from here. Let's focus on getting the other survivors out now.

passages.title: See to the Survivors
passages.text:
If we don't do something quick, neither Nevin nor the survivors will make it out of here alive. I'm going to give you my squad's emergency teleport beacon. We still have enough strength and ammunition to fight our way out of here, but those survivors are in no condition to make a run for it.

Use the beacon on survivors to arrange for them to be teleported out of here to the safe area my men have set up. Once you've done that, report back to me and we'll make arrangements to get you out of here.

passages.title: See to the Survivors
passages.text: Nevin's team found a lot of survivors this time, but he's cutting it awful close.

passages.title: See to the Survivors
passages.text:
I know Nevin will be pleased with all the survivors you managed to help. I still can't believe you managed to stay so strong down here in the radiation. You've seen the shape the other survivors are in.

Let's get you to the loading room for decontamination.

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text:
In the Map Chamber there is a door which leads to the legendary Chamber of Khaz'mul. Who knows what secrets could be hidden inside!

What we do know is that it is guarded by Ironaya, a Titanic Watcher of immense size and power. You'll need to defeat her if you intend to unlock the secrets of Uldaman!

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text: Don't worry about the chamber, my boys will check it out! You have more important things to do!

passages.title: It's What's Inside That Counts
passages.text:
The Makers built two Ancient Stone Keepers to help protect Uldaman from would-be invaders and to oversee daily operations while Ironaya and Archaedas slumber. One is still fully operational in Temple Hall, but the one in Echomok Cavern has been corrupted by something.

I fear that one of the Old Gods is responsible for this, and you're going to help me see if that's the case! Topple both of the guardians and bring me their power cores. They'll tell us all we need to know.

passages.title: It's What's Inside That Counts
passages.text:
Where are the cores, lad? By Muradin's Beard, where are the bloody cores?

<Kand takes a deep breath.>

Sorry about that. Have you been able to obtain the cores?

passages.title: It's What's Inside That Counts
passages.text:
This is incredible, <name>. The power coursing through each core...the contrasting powers so close together!

I'll take this to the proper dwarves right away. These cores are extremely important!

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text:
Galgann Firehammer and his band of Dark Irons are in Dig Three guarding a door that we know nothing about! I've had it with their men getting in the way of our work here! The Explorers' League is the only group authorized to handle the artifacts throughout Uldaman!

Go to the dig and dispose of him so that our work can continue undisturbed. I want to know what's behind that door!

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text: Fantastic! Great work! We'll know all that Dig Three has to tell us in no time at all!

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text:
The true goal in Uldaman is to obtain the Discs of Norgannon. The secrets on these discs could change everything about how we view our world. Countless secrets of the Makers are inscribed on them...their value is beyond any material wealth you could possibly imagine.

The problem is that Archaedas, an ancient and powerful creation of the Makers, guards the discs with a venerable army at his disposal. I need you to defeat him and secure the discs for the Explorers' League!

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text: Well done, lad! Now go to the discs and learn all you can!

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text:
In the Map Chamber there is a locked door which I believe leads to the legendary Chamber of Khaz'mul. We do not yet know what artifacts wait inside it.

What we do know is that it is guarded by Ironaya, a Titanic Watcher of immense size and power. You'll need to defeat her if you intend to progress any further into this place.

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text: Reliquary agents are en route to investigate the chamber. You have more important matters to attend to.

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text:
The true goal in Uldaman is to obtain the Discs of Norgannon. These platinum discs could grant our order unbelievable power. Countless secrets of the Makers are inscribed on them...their value is beyond any material wealth you could possibly imagine.

The only problem in obtaining them is that Archaedas, an ancient and powerful creation of the Makers, guards the discs with a venerable army at his disposal. I need you to defeat him and secure the discs for The Reliquary.

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text: You are a most reliable agent, <name>. Proceed to the discs and learn all you can. Report back to me immediately after.

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text:
Galgann Firehammer and his band of Dark Irons are in Dig Three guarding a door that we know nothing about! I've had it with their men getting in the way of our work here! The Reliquary is the only group authorized to handle the artifacts throughout Uldaman!

Go to the dig and dispose of him so that our work can continue undisturbed. I want to know what's behind that door!

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text: Well done. Dig Three and any secrets beyond that door will soon be ours and ours alone.

passages.title: We Require More Minerals
passages.text:
The Titans built two Ancient Stone Keepers to help protect Uldaman from would-be invaders and to oversee daily operations while Ironaya and Archaedas slumber. One is still fully operational in Temple Hall, but the one in Echomok Cavern has been corrupted by something.

I suspect that one of the Old Gods is responsible for this, and you're going to help me see if that is indeed true. Topple both of the guardians and bring me their power cores. They'll tell us all we need to know.

passages.title: We Require More Minerals
passages.text: Do you have the cores with you, or are you just here to chat? Perhaps we should stop this whole charade and enjoy some snacks and fine wine instead?

passages.title: We Require More Minerals
passages.text:
Both of these cores are still far more potent than most of the cores we use  to power our own protectors, and these are ancient devices!

Thank you, these will prove extremely valuable to our society.

passages.title: Into the Woods
passages.text:
I saw the strangest commotion coming through town the other day. A horse-drawn cart, loaded with crates and chests, a worgen woman at the reins, a blood elf by her side, and a dwarven paladin running behind, yelling some of the most creative obscenities I've heard in quite some time.

They looked like they were headed to Eastern Plaguelands, though I'd imagine they can't be far past the Thondroril River by now. I wonder what they were up to?

passages.title: Into the Woods
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Visitors
passages.text:
My sources at the Menders' Stead have informed me that we will be having some visitors soon. A group of paladins - led by a worgen tradeswoman, of all things - will be arriving here shortly. I look forward to meeting them. Particularly one of them.

Would you mind stopping in and checking in on them? I can't say for sure, but by the time you get there, they should just be crossing the Thondroril River, far to the west.

passages.title: Visitors
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Good Deed Left Undone
passages.text:
G'day, <laddie/lassie>.

The name's Rendel.

Seems ol' Moanah and I got here in the nick of time, eh?

Erunak wasn't kiddin' when he said it was life or death!

So... in our rush ta git over here, we left a little unfinished business off to the east a ways.

A little lady was near death herself. We had no choice but ta leave her by a little air vent when we came here to yer rescue.

How bout yeh git over and help her while there's still time?

passages.title: Good Deed Left Undone
passages.text:
Oh, finally...

I don't know how much longer I can last!

passages.title: An Opened Can of Whoop Gnash
passages.text:
What an accomplishment, felling a mighty sea giant!

The new residents of Smuggler's Hole will feel considerably safer knowing this monster is no longer loitering outside their haven.

passages.title: An Opened Can of Whoop Gnash
passages.text: You took down that Sea Giant, <class>?

passages.title: An Opened Can of Whoop Gnash
passages.text:
It's not much, but it's all I've got down here.

You're more than welcome to it, <class>.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text:
There are three candidates for Ascendancy that we need to eliminate: Dame Alys Finnsson, Master Klem, and Mia the Rose.

I'd like for you to serve as my distraction. When the time is right, I'll step in and finish them off from behind.

Whatever you do, <name>, do not underestimate them. Each got to where they are by being ruthless and very good at what they do.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text:
That takes care of most of their leaders outside of the Bastion of Twilight.

We work well together, <name>.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text:
There are three candidates for Ascendancy that need killing: Dame Alys Finnsson, Master Klem, and Mia the Rose.

I want you to serve as a distraction. When the time is right, I'll step in to finish them off from behind.

Just make sure that whatever you do, you don't underestimate them, <name>. Each of those lunatics got to where they are by being ruthless and very good at what they do.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text: That takes care of most of their leaders outside of the Bastion. Not bad work, <name>. Not bad at all.

passages.title: Marshfin Madness
passages.text:
I'm afraid the rest of the Steamwheedle here are gone. All the young ones at the camp to the east were lost when the murlocs came.

Yes, there's always been murlocs on these shores... but not in these numbers. They came in droves from the sea at night, howling and frothing, swarming up onto the land to attack!

We can't have them still running around, now can we? Would you put an old goblin at ease and go beat some of them back into the water?

passages.title: Marshfin Madness
passages.text: I've still got a few tricks up my sleeve, but I'm not going to tussle with murlocs if I don't have to.

passages.title: Marshfin Madness
passages.text:
You have to wonder just what's out there. This is the coast of the Forbidding Sea, with nothing beyond its reaches... but all these fishy folk just stomped right out of it.

What's more, I saw where they've been going...

passages.title: The Warden's Game
passages.text:
You see the statue split into two, then four, then eight identical statues in a square formation.

You hear a voice, not through your ears, but in the back of your mind:

 "A true warden does not face OUTWARD, searching for signs of danger.
 A true warden keeps his gaze INWARD, always focused on protecting his quarry."

Perhaps this is a riddle of some sort?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text:
The Twilight cowards have captured and killed too many red dragons, but one yet lives. Do you remember Lirastrasza? She's shackled nearby and we're going to free her.

But first, we need something sharp enough to cut through her chains.

There's an old ettin named Blindeye the Guardian. He stands watch at the Altar of Ascension to the south.

He has a purely-wrought Elementium axe. I wonder if that's Cho'gall's "ultimate" weapon?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text: Do you have the axe? They're going to kill Lirastrasza soon.

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text:
That thing looks sharp. Sharp enough to the do deed, at least.

But if I'm a judge of weaponry, that's not what Cho'gall's after.

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text:
The Twilight cowards have captured and killed many red dragons, but one's still breathing. Do you remember Lirastrasza? She's chained nearby and we're going to free her.

But first, we need something sharp enough to cut her free.

There's an old ettin named Blindeye the Guardian. He stands watch at the Altar of Ascension to the south.

He has a purely-wrought Elementium axe. I wonder if that's Cho'gall's "ultimate" weapon?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text: Do you have the axe?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text: That's a very sharp axe. It'll do the job, but if I'm any judge of weaponry, that's not what Cho'gall's after.

passages.title: Corruption in Maraudon
passages.text:
<name>, I require your assistance immediately! I am Zaetar, son of Cenarius, and I am trapped here after an unfortunate series of events! Before saving me is an option, you must help me clean out the corruption that runs so rampant through Maraudon.

Lord Vyletongue is the satyr ruler of the purple crystal caverns. He is an insidious agent of the Burning Legion and his continued presence can only lead to chaos and death. He can live no longer!

passages.title: Corruption in Maraudon
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>! Eliminating Vyletongue's presence is a key step to freeing me and, ultimately, saving these lands from corruption. Take this as a token of my thanks and an incentive to continue your work here.

passages.title: Servants of Theradras
passages.text:
Princess Theradras, my former mate, has used her enormous power to corrupt the very nature of Maraudon. Even now her creations run rampant here, and I fear that they may soon escape into the open world to sow the seeds of death and destruction.

<name>, venture forth and kill Noxxion and Razorlash. They are two of her most powerful minions and their deaths would cause the callous Princess much deserved grief and suffering of her own. Then, perhaps, you can help free my spirit from her grasp.

passages.title: Servants of Theradras
passages.text: Without her powerful servants, Princess Theradras is significantly more vulnerable. Find her lair, <name>...it is time to strike.

passages.title: Shark Weak
passages.text:
That's one tough shark!

You determine that it's in everyone's best interest to try and distract Budd and hope his attention never returns to Gnaws and this Skeletal Reef.

Perhaps the teeth of the beast will prove captivating enough...

passages.title: Shark Weak
passages.text: Whatcha got there, pal?

passages.title: Shark Weak
passages.text:
What?!

Gnaws ain't dead?!

This kinda takes the quick outta my get rich quick scheme...

Them giant shark teeth are nice and all, but we can't stop 'til that shiney is ours!

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text:
Look at that. Lirastrasza's destroying them!

There are drakes that she's downing that need finishing off, <name>. Wouldn't want the Twilight's healers to get them back up into the air.

Time for a little Coup de Grace.

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text: Our efforts to improve relations with the red dragons has really paid off, <name>.

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text:
Look at that. Lirastrasza's destroying them!

There are still drakes that she's downing that need finishing off, <name>. We don't want the stinking Twilight healers to get them back up into the air.

Time for a little Coup de Grace.

passages.title: Coup de Grace
